<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_003"></A>Item
1. Business.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_004"></A>Background
and Current Status of BRAC</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Broad
Capital Acquisition Corp. (the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;) was incorporated in the State of Delaware on April 16, 2021. The Company was incorporated
for the purpose of effecting a merger, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, reorganization or similar business combination
with one or more businesses, which we refer to as our initial business combination. Since the closing of our initial public offering
on January 13, 2022, we have focused our efforts on the search for an initial business combination that may provide significant opportunities
for attractive investor returns.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
January 13, 2022, we closed our initial public offering of 10,000,000 units. Each unit consists of one share of common stock of the Company,
par value $0.000001 per share and one right of the Company, with each right entitling the holder thereof to receive one-tenth (1/10)
of a share of common stock upon consummation of our initial business combination. The units were sold at a price of $10.00 per unit,
generating gross proceeds to the Company of $100,000,000.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Simultaneously
with the closing of the initial public offering, we completed the private sale of an aggregate of 446,358 units to our sponsor at a purchase
price of $10.00 per placement unit, generating gross proceeds of $4,463,580. On February 9, 2022, the Underwriters partially exercised
the over-allotment option and on February 10, 2022, purchased an additional 159,069 Units from the Company (the &ldquo;Over-Allotment
Units&rdquo;), generating gross proceeds of $1,590,690 and the Company completed the additional private sale of 4,772 private units at
a purchase price of $10.00 per private placement unit, to the Company&rsquo;s sponsor generating gross proceeds to the Company of $47,720.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
connection with the closing and sale of the Over-Allotment Units and the additional private placement units (together, the &ldquo;Over-Allotment
Closing&rdquo;), a total of $1,606,597 in proceeds from the Over-Allotment Closing (which amount includes $31,814 of the Underwriters&rsquo;
deferred discount) was placed in a U.S.-based trust account established for the benefit of the Company&rsquo;s public stockholders, maintained
by Continental Stock Transfer &amp; Trust Company, acting as trustee (&ldquo;CSTT&rdquo;).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
management team is led by Johann Tse, our Chief Executive Officer, and Rongrong (Rita) Jiang, our Chief Financial Officer, both of whom
permanently reside in, and are citizens of, the United States. Mr. Tse brings more than 30 years of leadership experience across numerous
engagements in the fields of corporate operation and management, venture capital, and multinational mergers and acquisitions and has
served as an independent board member of several Chinese companies listed in the United States in sectors including tourism, media and
restaurant supplies manufacturing and sales. Mr. Tse and Ms. Jiang are directors of the Company and the co-managers and 50:50 owners
of our sponsor.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
January 18, 2023, the Company entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger and Business Combination Agreement (the &ldquo;Merger Agreement&rdquo;)
with Openmarkets Group Pty Ltd., an Australian proprietary limited company (&ldquo;Openmarkets&rdquo;), BMYG OMG Pty Ltd., an Australian
proprietary limited company and Broad Capital LLC, solely as the Company&rsquo;s sponsor. On February 12, 2025, the Company received
a notice of termination from Openmarkets Group Pty Ltd. advising the Company of their termination of the Merger Agreement pursuant to
Section 11.1(d)(i) and Section 11.3 thereof, at which point the Merger Agreement became null and void with no further force and effect
(other than the provisions of Section 9.6 of the Merger Agreement, Article XIII of the Merger Agreement and Section 11.3 of the Merger
Agreement, which survive the termination of the Merger Agreement).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Since
the termination of the Merger Agreement, we have commenced our search for a new business combination target and, since that time,
the Company has conducted negotiations and entered into one letter of intent concerning a potential target business on April 24,
2026 involving a target company in the construction and engineering industry. The letter of intent is governed by and construed
under the laws of the State of New York and is non-binding with respect to the proposed transaction. No party is obligated to proceed
with the transaction unless and until definitive agreements are executed. The business purpose of the Company is to continue to seek
the acquisition of or merger with an existing company.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company is a &ldquo;blank check&rdquo; company. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the &ldquo;SEC&rdquo;) defines a &ldquo;blank
check&rdquo; company as &ldquo;any development stage company that is issuing a penny stock, within the meaning of Section 3(a)(51) of
the Exchange Act, and that has no specific business plan or purpose, or has indicated that its business plan is to merge with an unidentified
company or companies.&rdquo; Under SEC Rule 12b-2 under the Exchange Act, the Company also qualifies as a &ldquo;shell company,&rdquo;
because it has no or nominal assets (other than cash) and no or nominal operations. As a shell company, the Company may experience difficulty
attracting potential acquisition candidates, obtaining financing, maintaining service providers, and developing a trading market for
its securities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of June 30, 2026, the Company had $42,368 in cash, and its auditors have issued an opinion raising substantial doubt about its ability
to continue as a going concern. Many states have enacted statutes, rules and regulations limiting the sale of securities of &ldquo;blank
check&rdquo; companies in their respective jurisdictions. Management does not intend to undertake any efforts to cause a trading market
to develop in our securities, whether debt or equity, before we have successfully concluded a business combination. This statement does
not preclude us from obtaining working capital loans, sponsor or affiliate support, private financing, or other financing arrangements
to fund our operations, transaction expenses, or the consummation of a business combination, as described elsewhere in this registration
statement. The Company&rsquo;s need for cash to fund operating expenses until the completion of a business combination does not change
that conclusion. Any interim financing that the Company may seek or obtain would be for working capital purposes, including expenses
associated with maintaining its reporting status, identifying and evaluating potential business combination opportunities, and negotiating
and completing a business combination. Such financing would not be undertaken for the purpose of developing a market in the Company&rsquo;s
securities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">To
the extent the Company raises additional capital before completing a business combination, management expects that any such financing
would be conducted through private arrangements with founders, sponsors, affiliates, existing securityholders, or other accredited or
sophisticated investors, as applicable, and not through activities intended to create or stimulate a public trading market. Accordingly,
the Company believes that its potential need for working capital is not inconsistent with the disclosure that management does not intend
to undertake efforts to cause a market to develop in the Company&rsquo;s securities before a business combination is completed. The Company
intends to comply with the periodic reporting requirements of the Exchange Act for so long as it is subject to those requirements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s principal business objective for the next 12 months and beyond such time will be to achieve long-term growth potential
through a combination with a business rather than immediate, short-term earnings. The Company will not restrict its potential candidate
target companies to any specific business, industry or geographical location and, thus, may acquire any type of business. The Company
has not conducted any active operations since inception, except for its efforts to locate suitable acquisition candidates. We have entered
into a Business Combination Agreement with Conwall Construction Industries Limited, Conwall DE Sub Inc. and Conwall Construction
Industries Sdn. Bhd. (collectively, &ldquo;Conwall&rdquo;). The Business Combination has not closed as of the date
of this filing.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
planned Business Combination with Conwall has not closed to date. The Conwall business, financial statements, management discussion
and risk factors included in this registration statement provide information for evaluating the proposed transaction, but the Business
Combination remains subject to its closing conditions. Although our management will endeavor to evaluate the risks inherent in any particular
target business, we cannot assure you that we will adequately ascertain or assess all significant risk factors.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Summary
of the proposed Business Combination</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On

October 5, 2026 (the Business Combination Agreement). The following summary is qualified by the agreement filed as Exhibit 2.3 and the
more detailed disclosures below.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"><P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Questions
                                            and answers for BRAC securityholders</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>What
does this Form 10 do and what will stockholders vote on?</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">This
Form 10 registers BRAC Common Stock under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act. It does not solicit a vote, constitute a redemption demand
or register the issuance of Holdco shares under the Securities Act. The separate Form F-4 and proxy materials will describe the Business
Combination and related proposals, voting procedures, record date and meeting date. Approval of the Business Combination requires the
affirmative vote of a majority of BRAC&rsquo;s outstanding shares entitled to vote; abstentions and failures to vote therefore have the
effect of votes against that proposal.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"><P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>What
                                            will I receive?</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">A
holder of an unredeemed BRAC common share will receive one Holdco Ordinary Share. Public shares properly redeemed will receive cash and
will not also receive exchange shares. Rights convert separately at ten rights for one Holdco Ordinary Share even if the holder redeems
its public common shares. Units must be separated to exercise redemption rights. Rights carry no claim to the Trust Account.</FONT> </P>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>How
do redemption and dilution affect me?</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Eligible
public stockholders may request redemption whether they vote for or against the transaction or do not vote, subject to the charter and
the procedures in the definitive proxy materials. The June 30, 2026 illustrative Trust Account amount is $87,208, or approximately $12.51
per remaining public share. Actual payments depend on the permitted trust calculation at the applicable date. Founder shares, rights
conversion, loan conversion, underwriting settlement and any future financing dilute the percentage interests of holders who retain shares.
See &ldquo;Closing capitalization and dilution scenarios&rdquo; and Item 4.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>When
could the transaction close and what are the principal risks?</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Closing
depends on SEC registration, approvals and the other contractual conditions; it is not assured. The agreement&rsquo;s Outside Date is
April 30, 2027, distinct from BRAC&rsquo;s charter deadline of July 13, 2027. Risks include failure to satisfy listing requirements,
limited remaining trust cash, additional financing needs, Sponsor conflicts, substantial dilution, Conwall&rsquo;s customer and project
concentration, execution and licensing risks in Malaysia, and uncertainty in forecasts. Holdco shares will carry Cayman Islands shareholder
rights. See Item 1A and the comparison in Item 11.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Organizational
structure and transaction steps</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Holdco
and Conwall Construction Industries Limited are the same Cayman Islands legal entity. CCISB is Conwall Construction Industries Sdn. Bhd.,
the Malaysian operating company. The diagrams distinguish the completed July 16, 2026 share swap from the proposed Delaware merger.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

and treatment of each class of securities</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
original 30,000,000-share reorganization consideration is historical. After the September 8, 2026 cancellation of 5,329,076 shares, the
amended Business Combination Agreement fixes the net Company Reorganization Consideration at 24,670,924 Holdco Ordinary Shares. The $250,000,000
contractual enterprise value, the Company Equity Value after net indebtedness, and the number of Holdco shares are different measures.
The fixed share allocation is not an additional 24,670,924-share issuance on top of the existing target block.</FONT> </P>

and negotiations</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">BRAC
evaluated potential targets across industries and jurisdictions after the Openmarkets termination. Its review focused on operating history,
competitive position, growth opportunities, capital needs, management and the prospects for a U.S. listing. The following chronology
summarizes the material contacts disclosed for the Conwall transaction.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Diligence
included management presentations, data-room materials, financial statements, material project contracts, backlog, customer concentration,
working capital, indebtedness, permits, litigation, employee matters, related-party transactions and listing readiness. BRAC considered
continuing its target search and the risk of failing to complete a business combination within the available period. The parties negotiated
the consideration and structure; the valuation adviser did not set the transaction price.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>BRAC
Board determination and material factors</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
BRAC Board approved the original Business Combination Agreement in August 2026 and determined that the transaction was fair to, advisable
for and in the best interests of BRAC and its stockholders. The parties signed the amended and restated agreement on October 5, 2026.
The BRAC Board ratified the amended agreement and reaffirmed its determinations on October 8, 2026.</FONT> </P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Favorable
factors included Conwall&rsquo;s specialized cleanroom, process-utility and engineering capabilities; fiscal 2026 growth and return to
profitability; potential geographic and service expansion; possible access to capital; the negotiated consideration; and governance and
Closing protections. Adverse factors included customer, project and Malaysia concentration; a limited history of profitability at the
current scale; reliance on forecasts and new awards; collection and working-capital risks; industry cyclicality; BRAC&rsquo;s limited
trust balance and float; financing, dilution and listing risks; and the interests of the Sponsor, officers and directors. Continuing
the target search could preserve alternatives but would entail additional expense and the risk of liquidation if no transaction could
be completed.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">There
is no separate majority-of-unaffiliated-stockholders approval condition, and BRAC did not appoint a representative solely for its unaffiliated
stockholders. The full BRAC Board, including its independent directors, participated in the August 2026 approval of the original agreement.
The October 5 amended agreement was ratified by the BRAC Board on October 8, 2026. The Sponsor&rsquo;s voting commitment and substantial
shareholding may affect the stockholder approval outcome.</FONT> </P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Independent
valuation and financial due diligence</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">BRAC
engaged HK Credible Market Research Co., Limited (&ldquo;HK Credible&rdquo;) to prepare an independent target equity valuation and financial
due diligence analysis of Conwall in connection with the proposed Business Combination. BRAC identified HK Credible through an evaluation
process that included consideration of several potential providers, including Frost &amp; Sullivan and Nikkei Business Research. BRAC
evaluated the firms based on, among other factors, their prior case experience, professional fees and analyst qualifications, and selected
HK Credible based on these considerations. BRAC paid or agreed to pay HK Credible a fixed fee of $12,000 for the independent target equity
valuation and financial due diligence analysis. Such compensation was not contingent upon the valuation conclusion, transaction consideration,
financing, shareholder approval or consummation of the Business Combination. During the two years preceding the date of the Valuation
Report, except for its engagement by BRAC and receipt of the fixed professional fee described in this section, neither HK Credible nor,
to HK Credible&rsquo;s knowledge, the personnel participating in the Valuation Report had any equity ownership, control, employment relationship,
debt arrangement, success fee, underwriting fee, financing participation or other economic relationship with BRAC, the Sponsor, Conwall,
or their respective controlling shareholders, directors, officers, financial advisors, legal advisors, PIPE investors or other transaction
participants that would materially impair HK Credible&rsquo;s independence. The September 25, 2026 revision described in this section
updates the valuation date to June 30, 2026 and presents the separate analyses summarized below.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">HK
Credible Market Research Co., Limited (&ldquo;HK Credible&rdquo;) prepared an independent target equity valuation and financial due diligence
analysis, revised September 25, 2026, with a valuation date of June 30, 2026 (the &ldquo;Valuation Report&rdquo;), described in this
section. The report presents separate analytical outcomes: a $356.4 million to $520.4 million future-earnings scenario range, a $138.2
million policy discounted-cash-flow indication, and a $102.6 million to $149.8 million actual trailing-twelve-month diagnostic range.
These analyses use different earnings bases and assumptions and are not combined into a weighted valuation or midpoint. The future-earnings
range is conditional on projected performance, new project awards and financing; the DCF does not corroborate that range. The report
is not a fairness opinion or a recommendation to approve the Business Combination. The negotiated $250 million enterprise value remains
unchanged; it is distinct from the report&rsquo;s equity-value indications and from the fixed 24,670,924-share target allocation.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
BRAC Board considered the information available to it when it approved the Business Combination in August 2026. The September 25 revision
postdates that approval and is provided as updated information for BRAC&rsquo;s consideration; it should not be read as information available
to the Board at its August meeting. HK Credible&rsquo;s analysis is one factor in evaluating the transaction and does not determine the
negotiated consideration.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">HK
Credible&rsquo;s principal methods were discounted cash flow, conditional future-earnings capitalization and a trailing-earnings diagnostic.
It relied on information furnished by management and market comparisons and did not independently verify the forecasts. The report&rsquo;s
assumptions include forecast growth, financing availability, margins, reinvestment and discount rates. It is not a fairness opinion,
and its higher conditional range should not be presented as independent corroboration that the negotiated consideration is fair. The
September revision was not available at the August approval.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Revenue,
EBITDA and management net income are management estimates. EBITDA is a non-GAAP measure of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. It presents projected operating earnings before those items; projected GAAP net income is the most
directly comparable measure. EBITDA is not a substitute for GAAP net income.
The normalized earnings rows are HK Credible&rsquo;s calculations using D&amp;A of 0.4% of revenue, annual net interest of approximately
$0.327844 million and a 24% tax rate. They are not management&rsquo;s reconciliation of projected EBITDA to projected GAAP net income.
The FY2030 difference of $4.469 million, or approximately 18.2% of normalized net income, remains attributable to unresolved tax and
normalization assumptions; no tax incentive is established by that difference.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Material
assumptions include revenue growth of approximately 35% annually, substantial new awards, timely execution and collections, margin expansion,
adequate skilled capacity and financing, and a presentation exchange convention of approximately RM4.70 per U.S. dollar. The June 2026
quarter generated $11.286729 million of revenue, leaving $79.513271 million required in the remaining nine months to reach FY2027 projected
revenue. June 30 RPO of $7.605215 million covers only approximately 9.56% of that remaining requirement, assuming full recognition by
March 31. The $71.908056 million difference depends on additional awards and their timely conversion into revenue. At a 13.2% award-by-value
rate and complete same-period delivery, that gap would require approximately $544.8 million of eligible quotations; at 25%, approximately
$287.6 million. These are arithmetic sensitivities, not forecasts of awards.</FONT> </P>

DCF equity indication was approximately $138.2 million, compared with the conditional future-earnings range of $356.4 million to $520.4

projections were prepared for specific transaction purposes, have not been audited, and do not predict actual results. Their assumptions
are sensitive to customer concentration, industry spending, backlog conversion, project timing, costs, financing, licensing and foreign
exchange. Actual performance may differ materially. The September 25 reaffirmation is the latest affirmation identified here; it should
not be understood as a new affirmation as of a later filing or mailing date.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Redemption
procedures and limitations</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Only
holders of BRAC public common shares are entitled to redeem those shares for their pro rata interest in the Trust Account, subject to
the charter and applicable law. A holder must submit a written demand identifying its legal name, address and telephone number and deliver
its shares to Continental Stock Transfer &amp; Trust Company, physically or electronically through DTC&rsquo;s DWAC system, at least
two business days before the vote at the special meeting. Street-name holders must instruct their bank or broker in time to meet the
deadline. Unit holders must first separate units into shares and rights. The definitive proxy materials will specify the actual dates
and instructions.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">A
holder may redeem whether it votes for, against or does not vote on the Business Combination. Redemption is conditional on completion;
if the transaction is not completed, tendered shares will be returned. Rights are not redeemable and confer no Trust Account interest.
A public-share redemption does not cancel separately held rights. The Sponsor and insider holders&rsquo; waivers apply as described in
their agreements.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">At
June 30, 2026, the Trust Account held $87,208 for 6,969 public shares, equivalent to $12.5137 per share before subsequent permissible
adjustments. The redemption price at the actual measurement date may differ. The $291,400 liability arising from trust over-withdrawals
is separate and is not netted against that reported cash balance. Maximum redemption in the illustrations means all 6,969 remaining public
shares. The agreement imposes no minimum cash or net-tangible-asset Closing condition, but this does not waive an independently applicable
charter restriction or Nasdaq condition. No proceeds from an undisclosed or uncommitted backstop, non-redemption agreement, forward purchase
or PIPE are assumed.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
original 29,293,888 / 29,290,404 / 29,286,919 subtotals exclude underwriting settlement shares. Adding 3,000,000 produces the complete
illustrative totals above; no rights or loan shares are counted twice. Actual underwriting shares equal $1,500,000 divided by the higher
of $0.50 and ten times the contractual recent average BRAC Rights price, subject to the ownership cap and other terms. The illustration
is not a commitment to issue 3,000,000 shares.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Additional
PIPE shares equal financing proceeds divided by the actual issuance price, adjusted for any other securities or economics. At the contractual
$5 floor, hypothetical $3 million and $5 million equity financings would add 600,000 and 1,000,000 shares, respectively, but no such
financing is assumed committed here. Loan balances, interest, waivers, fractional rights, equity compensation and return or cancellation
of underwriting shares may also change ownership. &ldquo;Public shares plus public-rights shares&rdquo; describes issuance origins, not
a verified list of unaffiliated holders or Nasdaq unrestricted public float. Comparative per-share measures appear in Item 13.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Closing
conditions timing and termination</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
parties&rsquo; obligations are subject to the required BRAC and Conwall shareholder approvals; effective Form F-4 without a stop order;
applicable regulatory approvals and absence of prohibitory orders; completion of the reorganization; Nasdaq approval and applicable listing
requirements after redemptions; and effectiveness of the ancillary agreements. BRAC&rsquo;s conditions also include the specified Conwall
representations, covenants, absence of material adverse effect, third-party consents, holder-specific lock-up deliveries and the D&amp;O
insurance evidence required by Sections 6.7 and 9.2. Conwall&rsquo;s conditions include the specified BRAC representations, covenants,
absence of material adverse effect, ancillary deliveries and reporting compliance.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
agreement does not impose a minimum cash or minimum net-tangible-assets Closing condition. Its approximately $3 million to $5 million
financing objective is non-binding. Nasdaq approval, permitted treatment of restricted shares and any independently applicable charter
restrictions remain separate requirements. Any waiver must comply with the agreement, including the independent, disinterested board
and audit-committee process for the specified insurance condition.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">No
fixed Closing date is available. Section 10.1 states an April 30, 2027 Outside Date. That date is not the July 13, 2027 charter liquidation
deadline. Termination is permitted for mutual written consent; final prohibitory orders; failure of BRAC stockholder approval; failure
of Conwall consent within ten business days after Form F-4 effectiveness; specified listing or reorganization failures; an uncured qualifying
breach, subject to the applicable fifteen-day cure period; or failure of effectiveness or Closing by the Outside Date, subject to the
agreement&rsquo;s limitations on a materially breaching party.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
termination, the agreement becomes void except for its surviving provisions and liability for specified pre-termination willful and material
breaches. Generally, each party bears its own expenses, subject to the express allocation provisions and reimbursement of reasonable
documented out-of-pocket expenses up to $5 million following specified material-breach termination. Proxy and registration expenses are
shared equally subject to true-up under Section 8.1. At Closing, Holdco pays the parties&rsquo; transaction expenses under Sections 2.5
and 11.6; Covered Loans convert separately. The amended agreement has no transaction expense cap or related Sponsor cap-excess cash payment
or share forfeiture. The $5 million termination reimbursement limit and $1.5 million underwriting settlement are not loan-conversion
or Closing-expense caps.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Material
U.S. federal income tax considerations</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
following summarizes the intended treatment described in the transaction disclosure for U.S. holders that hold their securities as capital
assets. It does not address every holder or all state, local or non-U.S. taxes. Special rules apply to, among others, five-percent holders,
the Sponsor and holders of founder or private securities, financial institutions, dealers, tax-exempt investors and compensatory holders.
Investors should obtain advice for their own circumstances.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Exchanges
and cross-border limitations</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
parties intend that the July reorganization and the BRAC merger, considered together, qualify under Section 351 of the Internal Revenue
Code and that the BRAC merger not trigger gain under Section 367(a)(1), subject to the applicable requirements. If that treatment applies,
a qualifying U.S. holder generally would recognize no gain or loss on exchanging BRAC common shares for Holdco shares, carry over its
aggregate basis, and include the holding period of the surrendered shares. Section 367 and its regulations impose additional conditions
for transfers to a foreign corporation. A holder owning at least five percent of Holdco&rsquo;s vote or value after the transaction may
need a timely five-year gain recognition agreement and related compliance to avoid recognition of gain, but not loss. Satisfaction of
the five-percent rules does not dispense with the other requirements of Sections 351 and 367.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">If
the exchange is taxable because the intended treatment fails, a U.S. holder generally recognizes gain or loss equal to the fair market
value of the Holdco shares received less the basis of the surrendered shares; its new basis generally equals fair market value and its
new holding period begins the following day. Capital-loss limitations and holder-specific rules apply. The July reorganization, September
share changes, advisory transfers and all Closing issuances must be considered in the transaction-specific analysis. Rights holders and
Covered Loan creditors require separate analysis of their particular instruments; the common-share discussion does not establish their
tax treatment.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Redemptions</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">A
cash redemption is generally analyzed under Section 302 as a sale or exchange if the applicable substantially disproportionate, complete-termination
or not-essentially-equivalent-to-a-dividend test is met, taking account of constructive ownership, including relevant rights. Sale treatment
generally produces capital gain or loss equal to cash received less basis. Otherwise, Section 301 generally treats the payment as a dividend
to the extent of earnings and profits, then as a reduction of basis and then gain. A holder that redeems all shares and receives no Holdco
shares ordinarily is not exposed to Holdco&rsquo;s PFIC rules or Section 367 solely through the merger; a partial redeemer receiving
Holdco shares may be.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Holdco
PFIC risk and information</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">BRAC
is a domestic corporation and is not a PFIC. Holdco is foreign and may be a PFIC for a year if at least 75% of gross income is passive
or at least 50% of assets produce or are held to produce passive income, subject to the applicable look-through rules. Status is determined
annually and depends on actual income, assets, valuations and the use of cash. No assurance is given that Holdco or a relevant subsidiary
will not be a PFIC. Absent an effective qualified electing fund or mark-to-market election where available, gains and excess distributions
can be subject to adverse allocation, tax-rate and interest-charge rules. Elections, information reporting, dividends and subsequent
disposals are subject to holder-specific requirements.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
agreement provides for PFIC determinations and commercially reasonable efforts to supply applicable annual information statements within
the specified framework, including a 120-day determination period after the relevant year-end. This covenant does not guarantee availability
or effectiveness of any investor election. Backup withholding and information-reporting rules may also apply.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Tax
analysis and opinions</B></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">No
transaction-specific U.S. tax opinion is included in this registration statement. The intended treatment is an objective rather than
an opinion that the applicable requirements have been met, and Closing is not conditioned on receipt of such an opinion. No IRS ruling
has been requested or is intended. CCISB reports that it has no U.S. holders and does not foresee material U.S. federal income tax consequences
of the Business Combination to its pre-merger stockholders on that basis. This limited statement does not establish the entity-level
tax consequences to BRAC, Holdco or CCISB, or the treatment of BRAC rights, debt conversion or redemption excise tax, which require completed
transaction-specific analysis by U.S. tax counsel. The parties intend to engage U.S. tax counsel to provide the required transaction-specific
opinion and consent with a subsequent Form F-4 amendment. Neither is included in the supplied draft, and no tax-treatment conclusion
is represented as having been delivered. Neither the pro forma assumptions nor this summary replaces that analysis.</FONT> </P>

  <TR STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD></TR>
  <TR STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">(f)</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">the
    extent to which the business opportunity can be advanced; and</FONT></TD></TR>
  <TR STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD></TR>
  <TR STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">(g)</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">the
    accessibility of required management expertise, personnel, raw materials, services, professional assistance and other required items.</FONT></TD></TR>
  </TABLE>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
applying the foregoing criteria, no one of which will be definitive, management will attempt to analyze all factors and circumstances
and make a determination based upon reasonable investigative measures and available data. Potentially available business opportunities
may occur in many different industries, and at various stages of development, all of which will make the task of comparative investigation
and analysis of such business opportunities extremely difficult and complex. Due to the Registrant&rsquo;s limited capital available
for investigation, the Registrant may not discover or adequately evaluate adverse facts about the opportunity to be acquired. In addition,
we will be competing against other entities that possess greater financial, technical and managerial capabilities for identifying and
completing business combinations.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
evaluating a prospective business combination, we will conduct as extensive a due diligence review of potential targets as possible given
the lack of information which may be available regarding private companies and our limited personnel and financial resources. We expect
that our due diligence will encompass, among other things, meetings with the target business&rsquo;s incumbent management and inspection
of its facilities, as necessary, as well as a review of financial and other information which is made available to us. This due diligence
review will be conducted either by our management or by unaffiliated third parties we may engage, including but not limited to attorneys,
accountants, consultants or other such professionals. The costs associated with hiring third parties as required to complete a business
combination may be significant and are difficult to determine as such costs may vary depending on a variety of factors, including the
amount of time it takes to complete a business combination, the location of the target company, and the size and complexity of the business
of the target company.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
limited funds and the lack of full-time management will likely make it impracticable to conduct a complete and exhaustive investigation
and analysis of a target business before we consummate a business combination. Management decisions, therefore, will likely be made without
detailed feasibility studies, independent analysis, market surveys and the like, which, if we had more funds available to us, would be
desirable. We will be particularly dependent in making decisions upon information provided by the promoters, owners, sponsors or others
associated with the target business seeking our participation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
time and costs required to select and evaluate a target business and to structure and complete a business combination cannot presently
be ascertained with any degree of certainty. The amount of time it takes to complete a business combination, the location of the target
company, and the size and complexity of the business of the target company, whether current stockholders of the Company will retain equity
in the Company, the scope of the due diligence investigation required, the involvement of the Company&rsquo;s auditors in the transaction,
possible changes in the Company&rsquo;s capital structure in connection with the transaction, and whether funds may be raised contemporaneously
with the transaction are all factors that determine the costs associated with completing a business combination transaction. The time
and costs required to complete a business combination can be estimated once a business combination target has been identified. Any costs
incurred with respect to the evaluation of a prospective business combination that is not ultimately completed will result in a loss
to us.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Through
information obtained from industry professionals including attorneys, investment bankers, and other consultants with experience in the
reverse merger industry, the Company is aware that there are hundreds of shell companies seeking a business combination target. As a
result, the Company believes it is in a highly competitive market for a small number of business opportunities which could reduce the
likelihood of consummating a successful business combination. We are, and will continue to be, an insignificant participant in the business
of seeking mergers with, joint ventures with and acquisitions of small private and public entities. A large number of established and
well-financed entities, including small public companies and venture capital firms, are active in mergers and acquisitions of companies
that may be desirable target candidates for us. Nearly all these entities have significantly greater financial resources, technical expertise
and managerial capabilities than we do; consequently, we will be at a competitive disadvantage in identifying possible business opportunities
and successfully completing a business combination. These competitive factors may reduce the likelihood of our identifying and consummating
a successful business combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">None
of BRAC&rsquo;s current directors or executive officers is presently involved in any other blank-check company. They may become associated
with another blank-check company in the future, which could create conflicts in allocating business opportunities. In evaluating opportunities
among entities with which management may become affiliated, management would consider applicable fiduciary duties, the stage of transaction
development, industry focus, capital requirements, target company preferences and other relevant factors.&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">At
this time, the Company has not identified any specific factors or criteria that will be used to determine which entity will proceed with
a proposed transaction in the event of a conflict of interest and management reserves the right to use any such criteria as it determines
to be relevant at the time a proposed transaction is presented. However, in the event a conflict of interest arises in connection with
the identification of a proposed business transaction, the Company&rsquo;s management and board of directors will use its reasonable
judgment and intends to take all such actions as may be required in order to satisfy its fiduciary duties. At this time, there are no
specific conflicts of interests identified by our management.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
presently have no employees apart from our management. Our officers and directors are engaged in outside business activities and are
employed on a full-time basis by other companies. Our officers and directors will be dividing their time amongst these entities and anticipate
that they will devote very limited time to our business until the acquisition of a successful business opportunity has been identified.
We anticipate that our officers will devote on average approximately 5 to 10 hours per week to the Company&rsquo;s operations, including
corporate governance, regulatory compliance and identifying potential business opportunities. Management anticipates that this time commitment
may increase as the Company moves closer to identifying and executing a business combination. The specific amount of time that management
will devote to the Company may vary from week to week or even day to day, and therefore the specific amount of time that management will
devote to the Company on a weekly basis cannot be ascertained with any level of certainty. In all cases, management intends to spend
as much time as is necessary to exercise their fiduciary duties as an officer and/or director of the Company and believes that they will
be able to devote the time required to consummate a business combination transaction as necessary.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
expect no significant changes in the number of our employees other than such changes, if any, incident to a business combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company was formed as a blank check company, or special purpose acquisition company, for the purpose of effecting a merger, capital stock
exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses. The Company
is filing this registration statement on Form 10 in connection with the re-registration of its shares of common stock, par value $0.000001
per share, to complete a business combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
January 13, 2022, the Company consummated its initial public offering of 10,000,000 units. Each unit consisted of one share of common
stock and one right, with each right entitling the holder thereof to receive one-tenth of one share of common stock upon consummation
of the Company&rsquo;s initial business combination. The units were sold at a price of $10.00 per unit, generating gross proceeds to
the Company of $100,000,000. Simultaneously with the closing of the initial public offering, the Company completed the private sale of
an aggregate of 446,358 units to Broad Capital LLC, the Company&rsquo;s sponsor, at a purchase price of $10.00 per placement unit, generating
gross proceeds to the Company of $4,463,580.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> The 94,247-share reduction reflects redemptions
in connection with the January 2026 extension, at approximately $12.42 per share. The net change in trust cash also reflects the other
trust-account movements shown in the financial statements and is not necessarily equal to redeemed shares multiplied by the rounded redemption
price. Outstanding shares, record holders and beneficial holders are different measures; the latest record-holder count must be obtained
from the transfer agent. The share totals above do not establish that count. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Form
of Acquisition</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
manner in which the Registrant participates in an opportunity will depend upon the nature of the opportunity, the respective needs and
desires of the Registrant and the promoters of the opportunity, and the relative negotiating strength of the Registrant and such promoters.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">It
is likely that the Registrant will acquire its participation in a business opportunity through the issuance of its Common Stock or other
securities of the Registrant, which could result in substantial dilution to the equity of stockholders of the Registrant immediately
prior to the consummation of a transaction. The proposed Conwall transaction is governed by the amended Business Combination Agreement.
Its intended tax treatment is subject to applicable legal requirements and the facts at Closing. It should be noted that the criteria
for determining whether an acquisition is a so-called &ldquo;tax-free&rdquo; reorganization under Section 368(a)(1) of the Internal
Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &ldquo;Code&rdquo;), depend upon the transaction meeting certain statutory and non-statutory
requirements. There are different statutory requirements for each type of tax-free reorganization, and each transaction must be reviewed
carefully to determine its eligibility. One statutory requirement in a tax-free reorganization is that at least a certain percentage
of the total consideration must be voting stock of the acquirer corporation. This could result in substantial dilution to the equity
of those who were stockholders of the Registrant before the reorganization. In addition, post-transaction dispositions of Registrant
stock received as consideration could have implications for the tax-free nature of the transaction. The Company does not intend to supply
disclosure to stockholders concerning a target company before consummation of a Business Combination unless required by
applicable law or regulation. In the event a proposed Business Combination involves a change in a majority of the
directors of the Company, the Company will file and provide to stockholders a Schedule 14F-1, which will include information concerning
the target company, as required. The Company will file a current report on Form 8-K, as required, within four business days of a Business
Combination that results in the Company ceasing to be a shell company. This Form 8-K will include complete disclosure of the
target company, including audited financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
present stockholders of the Registrant will likely not have control of a majority of the voting securities of the Registrant following
a reorganization transaction. As part of such a transaction, all or a majority of the Registrant&rsquo;s directors may resign and one
or more new directors may be appointed without any vote by stockholders.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
the case of an acquisition, the transaction may be accomplished upon the sole determination of management without any vote or approval
by stockholders. In the case of a statutory merger or consolidation directly involving the Company, it will likely be necessary to call
a stockholders&rsquo; meeting and obtain the approval of the holders of a majority of the outstanding securities. The necessity to obtain
such stockholder approval may result in delay and additional expense in the consummation of any proposed transaction and will also give
rise to certain appraisal rights to dissenting stockholders. Any proposed business combination will be structured and completed in accordance
with applicable Delaware law, federal securities laws, SEC rules and regulations, and any applicable stock exchange requirements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company has entered into a Business Combination agreement with Conwall.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
