<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Related-party
financing transactions are not negotiated at arm&rsquo;s length and may not reflect terms that would be available from unaffiliated third
parties.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">All
financing transactions between us and our sponsor, officers, directors, or their respective affiliates are conducted between related
parties and are not the result of arm&rsquo;s-length negotiations. Accordingly, the terms of such transactions, including interest rates,
repayment terms, conversion features, and security interests, may not reflect terms that would be available to us if we were to obtain
financing from unaffiliated third-party lenders. The lack of arm&rsquo;s-length negotiation increases the risk that such transactions
may be on terms that are less favorable to the Company (or more favorable to the related party) than would otherwise be obtainable. Although
our board of directors (or a committee thereof) may review and approve related-party transactions, the inherent conflicts of interest
among our officers, directors, and sponsor create a risk that such transactions may not be entered into solely in the best interests
of the Company and its public shareholders. There can be no assurance that any related-party financing will be on terms that are fair
to the Company or that comparable financing could not have been obtained on more favorable terms from unaffiliated sources.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I><A NAME="ju_021"></A>Risks
Relating to Conflicts of Interest</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Our
officers and directors may have conflicts of interest arising from their involvement with other entities, which could adversely affect
their ability to devote time and attention to our affairs.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Certain
of our officers and directors presently have, and any of them in the future may have, additional fiduciary or contractual obligations
to other entities, including other special purpose acquisition companies, pursuant to which such officer or director is or will be required
to present business combination opportunities. Accordingly, they may have conflicts of interest in determining to which entity a particular
business opportunity should be presented. These conflicts may not be resolved in our favor and a potential target business may be presented
to another entity prior to its presentation to us, subject to applicable fiduciary duties under Delaware law. Our officers and directors
are not required to commit their full time to our affairs, and the amount of time they devote to us may vary from time to time. The other
entities to which our officers and directors owe fiduciary or contractual duties may compete with us for business combination opportunities,
and our officers and directors may be incentivized to favor such other entities over us due to their existing financial interests, commitments,
or relationships with those entities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>The
financial interests of our sponsor and insiders in the completion of a business combination may differ from, and conflict with, the interests
of our public shareholders.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
sponsor acquired founder shares prior to our initial public offering for nominal consideration. These founder shares (and any shares
issuable upon conversion thereof) will be worthless if we do not consummate a business combination. Additionally, our sponsor and certain
of our officers and directors hold private placement rights that were purchased simultaneously with the consummation of our initial public
offering, which rights will also expire worthless if we do not consummate a business combination. The personal and financial interests
of our sponsor and insiders in completing a business combination may influence their judgment and create a conflict of interest in determining
whether a particular target business is an appropriate candidate for a business combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
nominal consideration paid by our sponsor for the founder shares and private placement rights creates a disparity between the economic
interests of our insiders and those of our public shareholders. Our insiders may realize a substantial return on their investment even
if the business combination results in a decline in the value of our public shares, because the founder shares were acquired at a price
substantially below the per-share price paid by public shareholders in our initial public offering. This economic disparity may create
an incentive for our insiders to complete a business combination that may not be in the best interests of our public shareholders, including
a combination with a less favorable target or on less favorable terms than would otherwise be acceptable.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Fiduciary
duties owed by our officers and directors to multiple entities may result in the allocation of business opportunities away from us.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
officers and directors owe fiduciary duties to us under Delaware law. However, to the extent that our officers and directors serve as
officers or directors of other entities, including affiliates of our sponsor, they also owe fiduciary or contractual duties to those
entities. Where a business combination opportunity is appropriate for both us and one or more of such other entities, our officers and
directors may have a conflict of interest in determining to which entity such opportunity should be presented. Under Delaware law, the
doctrine of corporate opportunity may not clearly resolve such conflicts, particularly where our certificate of incorporation includes
a provision renouncing the Company&rsquo;s interest in certain business opportunities. We cannot assure you that any conflicts of interest
will be resolved in our favor. Additionally, our officers and directors may become aware of business opportunities that may be appropriate
for presentation to us or to the other entities to which they owe duties, and may present such opportunities to other entities before
presenting them to us. The loss of potential business combination opportunities to other entities could limit our ability to identify
and consummate a suitable business combination, which could result in our liquidation and dissolution.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I><A NAME="ju_022"></A>Risks
Relating to the Uncertainty of Completing a Business Combination</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>There
is no assurance that we will consummate a business combination, and if we fail to do so within the required timeframe, we will be required
to liquidate.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">There
is no guarantee that we will be able to identify a suitable target business, negotiate and execute a definitive agreement with respect
to a business combination, obtain the requisite shareholder and regulatory approvals, and satisfy all conditions to closing within the
timeframe required by our governing documents. Our ability to consummate a business combination is subject to numerous risks, uncertainties,
and conditions beyond our control, including market conditions, the availability of suitable targets, competition from other acquirors,
and our access to sufficient capital to complete a transaction. If we are unable to consummate a business combination within the required
timeframe, our governing documents require that we (i) cease all operations except for the purpose of winding up, (ii) redeem all public
shares for a pro rata portion of the funds held in trust (less taxes payable and amounts previously released for permitted purposes),
and (iii) thereafter liquidate and dissolve. In such event, our public shareholders may receive less than the original per-share price
paid in our initial public offering, and our rights will expire worthless.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Shareholder
redemptions in connection with a business combination may reduce the amount of cash available to consummate a transaction, impairing
our ability to close.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
connection with a proposed business combination, our public shareholders have the right to redeem their shares for a pro rata portion
of the trust account. The Company has already experienced significant redemptions, and as a result, only 6,969 public shares of common
stock remain outstanding. If additional public shareholders exercise their redemption rights in connection with a proposed business combination,
the amount of cash available to fund the business combination consideration or to satisfy minimum cash conditions required by the target
company or its advisors will be further and substantially reduced. Given the already diminished share count, even a modest number of
additional redemptions could cause us to fail to satisfy minimum cash or net tangible asset conditions required to consummate the business
combination, which could prevent us from closing the transaction.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Given
the significant redemptions already experienced, with only 6,969 shares of common stock remaining outstanding, we may seek to reduce
the extent of further redemptions through arrangements such as forward purchase agreements, backstop agreements, or non-redemption agreements
with third parties. However, there can be no assurance that such arrangements will be available or that they will provide sufficient
capital to close the transaction. If we are unable to consummate a business combination because of excessive redemptions or our failure
to satisfy closing conditions related to cash on hand, we may be forced to seek alternative transactions on less favorable terms or ultimately
liquidate.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Our
governing documents may impose minimum cash or net tangible asset conditions that could prevent us from completing a business combination.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
amended and restated certificate of incorporation and the agreements governing our trust account may impose conditions requiring that
we maintain a minimum level of net tangible assets or a minimum amount of cash at the time of closing a business combination. Given that
only 6,969 public shares of common stock remain outstanding following prior redemptions, the amount of funds available in the trust account
has been significantly reduced. If, after giving effect to any further shareholder redemptions and the payment of transaction expenses,
we are unable to satisfy such conditions, we may be prevented from consummating the proposed business combination. Additionally, the
SEC has adopted rules requiring that a special purpose acquisition company have a minimum of $5,000,001 of net tangible assets in order
to avoid being subject to the provisions of the Exchange Act applicable to &ldquo;penny stocks.&rdquo; If we fail to meet these conditions,
we may be required to seek alternative transactions, raise additional capital, or liquidate.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>If
we are forced to liquidate, our rights and founder shares will expire worthless, and the distribution to public shareholders may be less
than anticipated.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
the event of a liquidation, the proceeds of the trust account will be distributed to holders of our public shares on a pro rata basis,
after satisfaction of taxes and certain permitted expenses. As of the date of this registration statement, only 6,969 public shares of
common stock remain outstanding as a result of prior redemptions. Our rights will expire worthless, and holders of such securities will
receive no distribution in connection with the liquidation. Similarly, our founder shares do not participate in the liquidation distribution,
and our sponsor and insiders will lose their entire investment in such shares. The per-share distribution amount will be reduced by any
taxes payable, amounts previously withdrawn from trust for permitted purposes, extension deposits, and costs associated with the dissolution
and liquidation process. As a result, public shareholders may receive less than the original per-share price paid in our initial public
offering. The liquidation process may be time-consuming and costly, and the actual amount and timing of distributions to shareholders
is uncertain. We cannot assure you that the funds remaining in the trust account after satisfaction of all obligations will be sufficient
to provide shareholders with a meaningful return on their investment, particularly after giving effect to any reduction in trust account
value during the period of our operations.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I><A NAME="ju_023"></A>Risks
Relating to Limited Cash Resources</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>We
have limited cash resources outside of the trust account, which may be insufficient to fund our operations and pursuit of a business
combination.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
proceeds of our initial public offering were placed into a trust account and are generally not available to us for operating expenses,
transaction costs, or other corporate purposes other than as specifically permitted by our governing documents. The funds available to
us outside the trust account, together with any loans or advances from our sponsor and its affiliates, may be insufficient to fund our
ongoing operations, conduct due diligence on prospective targets, negotiate and complete a business combination, and pay our general
and administrative expenses. We have limited sources of revenue, and our existing cash resources outside the trust account may be depleted
before we are able to consummate a business combination. If we are unable to obtain additional working capital from our sponsor or other
sources, we may be required to curtail our search for a business combination target, reduce our operating activities, or liquidate earlier
than anticipated. The limited availability of cash outside the trust account creates a risk that we may be unable to adequately evaluate
prospective targets, fund necessary due diligence activities, or pay professional fees and expenses required to consummate a business
combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>We
are dependent on our sponsor for working capital support, and there can be no assurance that such support will be provided.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
ongoing operations have been funded primarily by loans and advances from our sponsor and its affiliates. Our sponsor is under no contractual
or legal obligation to provide additional funding to us beyond what has already been committed. If our sponsor determines not to provide
further working capital support, or is unable to do so due to its own financial constraints or other reasons, we may lack sufficient
funds to continue our operations, pursue business combination opportunities, or satisfy our obligations as they become due. The reliance
on our sponsor for working capital support also means that our ability to operate independently is limited. Decisions regarding the timing
and amount of working capital contributions may be influenced by our sponsor&rsquo;s own financial interests, the sponsor&rsquo;s assessment
of potential business combination opportunities, or the sponsor&rsquo;s evaluation of the likelihood that we will successfully consummate
a transaction. There can be no assurance that the interests of our sponsor in providing (or withholding) working capital support will
align with the interests of our public shareholders.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Insufficient
funds outside the trust account may force us to liquidate earlier than planned, which could result in reduced distributions to public
shareholders.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">If
we exhaust our available cash resources outside the trust account and are unable to obtain additional financing from our sponsor or other
sources, we may be unable to continue our search for a business combination target or fund the costs necessary to consummate a proposed
transaction. In such circumstances, we may be forced to commence liquidation proceedings earlier than the deadline imposed by our governing
documents. An early liquidation could result in reduced distributions to public shareholders because (i) we would have less time to allow
interest to accrue on trust account funds, and (ii) the costs of an early liquidation, including professional fees and administrative
expenses, would reduce the amount available for distribution.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><TD STYLE="text-align: center; width: 100%"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->42<!-- Field: /Sequence --></TD></TR></TABLE></DIV>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Restrictions
on the use of trust account funds limit our operational flexibility and our ability to pursue business combination opportunities.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
funds in our trust account are subject to strict restrictions on use and may only be released in connection with the consummation of
a business combination, shareholder redemptions, tax payments, and limited other permitted purposes as set forth in our governing documents
and the trust agreement. These restrictions significantly limit our operational flexibility and our ability to deploy capital in pursuit
of business combination opportunities. For example, we may not use trust account funds to pay deposits, fund due diligence expenses,
or make preliminary investments in a target company prior to the closing of a business combination. Additionally, our inability to use
trust account funds for general corporate purposes means that we are entirely reliant on funds outside the trust account and related-party
financing for our day-to-day operations. If we are unable to secure sufficient funding from these limited sources, we may be unable to
take advantage of business combination opportunities that arise, potentially resulting in our failure to consummate a transaction and
our ultimate liquidation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I><A NAME="ju_024"></A>Risks
Relating to Potential Dilution from Rights and Future Financings</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>The
conversion of rights into shares of common stock upon consummation of a business combination will dilute the ownership interests of public
shareholders.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Each
holder of a right included in the units sold in our initial public offering is entitled to receive a fraction of a share of common stock
(for example, one-tenth of a share) upon the consummation of a business combination. The issuance of shares upon conversion of these
rights will dilute the ownership interests of holders of our public shares and will increase the number of shares outstanding. The dilutive
effect of the conversion of rights will reduce the per-share value of our common stock, and public shareholders who do not hold rights
(or who hold fewer rights relative to their share ownership) will bear a disproportionate share of this dilution. Additionally, the conversion
of rights upon a business combination is automatic and occurs without the payment of additional consideration by the rights holders.
This means that the issuance of shares upon conversion of rights will increase the total number of shares outstanding without a corresponding
increase in the aggregate value of the Company, resulting in dilution to all other shareholders.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>The
issuance of founder shares to our sponsor at nominal cost creates significant dilution to public shareholders and may misalign incentives.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Prior
to our initial public offering, our sponsor was issued founder shares representing approximately 20% of our total outstanding shares
of common stock following the offering, in exchange for nominal consideration. Following significant redemptions by public shareholders,
only 6,969 public shares of common stock remain outstanding, which means the founder shares now represent a substantially larger percentage
of our outstanding equity than they did at the time of the initial public offering. The disparity between the price paid by our sponsor
for such shares and the price paid by our public shareholders in the initial public offering results in immediate and substantial dilution
to public shareholders, and this dilutive effect has been significantly magnified by the reduction in public shares outstanding due to
redemptions. The founder shares are BRAC common stock. At the Conwall Business Combination, each outstanding BRAC common share is to
be exchanged for one Holdco Ordinary Share under the amended Business Combination Agreement; the Sponsor has waived its anti-dilution
rights under the BRAC Charter. The existence of the founder shares may make it more difficult for us to consummate a Business Combination
with a target company at a price that would deliver attractive returns to public shareholders, as the value represented by the founder
shares must effectively be absorbed by the value of the combined company. Furthermore, because the founder shares were acquired at nominal
cost, our sponsor may realize a positive return on its investment even if the per-share value of the post-combination company declines
significantly below the per-share price paid by public shareholders.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Future
equity or convertible financings undertaken in connection with or following a business combination may result in additional dilution
to public shareholders.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
connection with a business combination, or following the consummation thereof, we may issue additional shares of common stock, preferred
stock, convertible securities, or other equity-linked instruments to finance the transaction consideration, raise additional working
capital, fund the operations of the post-combination company, or for other corporate purposes. Any such issuance will dilute the ownership
interests of our existing shareholders, and the terms of such securities may include rights, preferences, or privileges that are senior
to those of our common stock. There can be no assurance that future financing transactions will be completed on terms that are favorable
to existing shareholders, and any dilutive financing could adversely affect the per-share value of our common stock. Additionally, we
may issue equity or equity-linked securities to the sellers of a target business as part of the business combination consideration, to
financial advisors or service providers as transaction fees, or to investors in a private investment in public equity (PIPE) transaction
or similar financing. The aggregate dilutive effect of such issuances, together with the conversion of rights and the outstanding founder
shares, could be substantial and could significantly reduce the percentage ownership of public shareholders in the post-combination company.
Investors should be aware that they may experience significant dilution from multiple sources in connection with a business combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>BRAC&rsquo;s
directors&rsquo; and officers&rsquo; insurance has lapsed, and obtaining replacement and prior-acts coverage may be costly or may not
fully protect BRAC or its directors and officers.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">BRAC&rsquo;s
directors&rsquo; and officers&rsquo; liability insurance has lapsed and is not currently in force. Claims arising during the lapse, or
from conduct predating replacement coverage, may leave BRAC and its directors and officers exposed to uninsured defense costs, judgments
or settlements, subject to applicable indemnification arrangements. Such liabilities could strain BRAC&rsquo;s limited liquidity, impair
its ability to retain directors and officers and adversely affect completion of the Business Combination. Management intends to secure
full directors&rsquo; and officers&rsquo; protection in connection with the de-SPAC, including coverage for prior BRAC acts and go-forward
coverage, as contemplated by the amended Business Combination Agreement. Full protection cannot be assured: coverage remains subject
to underwriting, exclusions, limits, retentions and the policy&rsquo;s terms, and a new policy may not eliminate the existing coverage
gap.&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Section
6.7 of the amended Business Combination Agreement requires, at or before Closing, a six-year run-off, tail, legacy or prior-acts policy
for BRAC and the required go-forward directors&rsquo; and officers&rsquo; coverage effective at Closing. The agreement requires the best
coverage commercially available on commercially reasonable terms, specifies protections for prior BRAC acts and requires delivery of
binders and evidence of payment or irrevocable funding at Closing. If the specified prior-acts coverage is unavailable, the agreement
requires the best available alternative supported by written broker evidence and the prescribed consultation. The applicable closing
condition may be waived only through the independent, disinterested board and audit-committee process specified in Section 9.2. An intention
to obtain coverage after Closing does not satisfy those requirements. Coverage availability or cost could delay the transaction, and
any permitted alternative or waiver could leave material uninsured exposure.</FONT></P>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_025"></A>Risks
Related to Conwall</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
following risks relate to CCISB and its business, industry and markets. In this subsection, &ldquo;we,&rdquo; &ldquo;our,&rdquo; &ldquo;us&rdquo;
and the &ldquo;Company&rdquo; mean CCISB and its consolidated business. These risks would affect Holdco following the Business Combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <B>Execution and licensing failures could interrupt
projects and materially reduce revenue</B> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> Conwall&rsquo;s fixed-price and other project
contracts expose it to estimating errors, material and labor inflation, subcontractor failures, changes in scope, delayed customer approvals
and liquidated damages. Losses on a large project can outweigh profits elsewhere. Completion of Chipbond work and concentration in Coherent
increase dependence on a small number of replacement awards. June 30 RPO of $7.605 million is substantially below the revenue assumed
in management&rsquo;s forecasts and may be delayed, amended or cancelled. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> Conwall terminated its local CIDB G7 registration
on October 5, 2026 and its foreign-contractor application remains pending. The loss of current registration or restrictions during the
transition could prevent bidding, delay work or impair contract performance. Permits, foreign-worker approvals, subcontractor qualifications
and local premises licenses are separate requirements. No assurance is given that all necessary approvals will be obtained in time. The
detailed construction, concentration, backlog, personnel and regulatory risks below further explain these exposures. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <B>Malaysian operations and foreign enforcement
create additional risks</B> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> All Conwall revenue in the periods presented
was generated in Malaysia. Local political, tax, licensing, labor and foreign-investment policy changes can affect eligibility for awards
and project economics. Restrictions on foreign workers, higher levies or delayed approvals may increase costs or interrupt delivery.
Ringgit revenues, costs and balance-sheet amounts translated into U.S. dollars may fluctuate even without a change in underlying operating
activity. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> Substantially all operating assets and many
relevant persons are outside the United States. Service of process and enforcement of U.S. judgments in Malaysia or the Cayman Islands
can be more difficult and may require separate proceedings under local law. Foreign courts may not recognize particular securities-law
judgments or claims. These limitations can increase the time and cost of pursuing remedies and reduce an investor&rsquo;s practical ability
to obtain recovery. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> <B>Holdco shareholder protections reporting and
listing may differ from those of BRAC</B> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> Holdco is a Cayman Islands company. Its articles
and Cayman law differ from Delaware law in meetings, shareholder action, inspection, derivative remedies and enforcement, as summarized
in Item 11. If Holdco qualifies as a foreign private issuer, it may report on Forms 20-F and 6-K and use permitted home-country practices;
investors may receive information on different schedules and with different content from a U.S. domestic issuer. Qualification is not
assured merely by Cayman incorporation. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> In the full no-redemption underwriting illustration,
Ng Boon Teik would hold approximately 50.421% of Holdco. The issuance of approximately 271,732 additional ordinary shares, with no change
in his holdings, would reduce his ownership to 50% under that illustration. Controlled-company status therefore depends on actual Closing
capitalization and cannot be assumed under every financing scenario. Any available governance exemption could reduce minority protections.
Loss of foreign-private-issuer status or failure to satisfy initial or continued Nasdaq standards could increase compliance costs, delay
Closing or impair trading and liquidity. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <B>The Business Combination may dilute investors
without delivering the expected benefits</B> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> Founder shares, conversion of existing rights
and Covered Loans, variable-price underwriting settlement and any financing can materially dilute nonredeeming holders. Higher redemptions
reduce cash while rights and many other issuances remain outstanding. The Sponsor and insiders&rsquo; acquisition costs and potential
recovery of loans or fees may create incentives that differ from public investors&rsquo; incentives. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> The transaction may fail because of regulatory,
listing, financing or other conditions. Unquantified transaction costs and retained liabilities can reduce resources available after
Closing. The preliminary pro forma does not resolve all settlement accounting, and forecasts depend heavily on uncontracted awards and
financing. If Closing occurs, integrating governance, controls and public-company reporting may take longer or cost more than expected.
If it fails, BRAC will incur costs without the anticipated benefits and may be required to liquidate at its charter deadline, while rights
may expire without value. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I><U><A NAME="ju_026"></A>Risks
Related to Conwall&rsquo;s Business and Industry</U></I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>If
we are unable to maintain and strengthen our competitive advantages in high-tech production facility projects, our ability to win new
projects and maintain margins may be adversely affected.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
results depend on our ability to deliver construction and maintenance services for high-tech production facilities in a manner that satisfies
customer requirements, technical specifications, project schedules and quality expectations. If customers perceive that our technical
capabilities, project execution, innovation, quality control or cost efficiency are inferior to those of competitors, we may be unable
to secure new projects, retain existing customers or maintain pricing. Any failure to strengthen our competitive position could adversely
affect our revenue, profitability and prospects.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Competition
from specialized M&amp;E contractors and larger general contractors may reduce project awards, pricing and margins.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company faces competition from specialized semiconductor infrastructure and cleanroom engineering contractors, including local mechanical
and electrical (M&amp;E) and controlled-environment specialists, as well as international engineering, procurement, construction (EPC),
engineering, procurement, and construction management (EPCM), and facility-integration providers.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">If
competitors offer lower pricing, broader balance-sheet support, stronger customer references, faster mobilization, more comprehensive
semiconductor experience or better access to qualified personnel, suppliers or financing, the Company may be unable to win projects on
commercially acceptable terms. Increased competition could also require the Company to accept lower margins, less favorable contract
terms, greater performance obligations or higher working-capital commitments, any of which could materially adversely affect revenue,
profitability, backlog conversion and cash flow.</FONT></P>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
project awards depend on competitive tendering and customer qualification requirements, and our historical quotation conversion rates
are not indicative of future awards.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
secure projects through customer qualification, tender invitations, technical and commercial submissions, negotiations and formal purchase
orders or contract awards. In the three months ended June 30, 2026, we submitted 212 quotations with an aggregate value of $3.9 million
and received 61 purchase orders with an aggregate value of $0.8 million, representing conversion rates of approximately 28.8% by number
of quotations and 20.0% by aggregate value. During the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, we submitted 705 quotations with an aggregate
value of $211.6 million and received 205 purchase orders with an aggregate value of $27.9 million, representing conversion rates of approximately
29.1% by number of quotations and 13.2% by aggregate value. During the twelve months ended March 31, 2025, we submitted 768 quotations
with an aggregate value of $261.7 million and received 241 purchase orders with an aggregate value of $56.7 million, representing conversion
rates of approximately 31.4% by number of quotations and 21.7% by aggregate value.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
period from submission of a quotation to award of a contract has historically been approximately three months, followed by approximately
one week from award to project mobilization. Our ability to participate in certain tenders depends on our satisfying applicable customer
qualification requirements and maintaining approved-vendor status. Our results of operations in any period may be materially affected
by the number and aggregate value of project awards we receive, and historical conversion rates are not necessarily indicative of future
awards.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>We
compete for project awards on the basis of a limited number of reference projects and customer qualifications, and we may be unable to
win new work on commercially acceptable terms.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
compete for work primarily on the basis of technical capability, demonstrated experience on comparable facilities, price, schedule certainty,
safety and quality performance, and our ability to satisfy customer qualification and approved-vendor requirements. Our experience in
high-specification production facilities is concentrated in a small number of recent projects, and customers procuring cleanroom, process
utility and mechanical and electrical works typically require evidence of comparable completed work, financial capacity, guarantee or
bonding support and relevant certifications before inviting a contractor to tender.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">If
we fail to maintain the qualifications, certifications and reference projects our customers require, if our execution, quality control
or safety performance does not meet customer standards, or if competitors offer more attractive pricing, schedules or technical solutions,
we may be excluded from tenders, lose approved-vendor status or be unable to win projects on acceptable terms. Because we bid predominantly
on a fixed-price basis, we may also have to accept lower margins or greater performance risk in order to remain competitive, which would
reduce our profitability.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
inability to control construction costs, subcontractor expenses, material costs, staffing costs and administrative expenses could reduce
our margins.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
cost of revenues includes purchased construction, subcontractor expenses, materials, salaries and welfare, outsourcing expenses and other
project execution costs. Our operating expenses include staffing costs, professional fees, insurance, office expenses and other administrative
expenses. Increases in any of these costs, or our inability to pass such increases on to customers, could reduce gross margin and operating
margin. Large projects may amplify the impact of cost overruns, inaccurate estimates, supplier delays, labor shortages or productivity
issues. Our profitability therefore depends substantially on our ability to control project costs, staffing costs and administrative
expenses while maintaining customer service quality and project execution standards, and our ability to attract and retain qualified
employees, identify business opportunities, secure new customer contracts, control procurement costs, manage subcontractors and improve
employee productivity affects our margins and operating results.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
recent revenue growth may not be sustainable and should not be viewed as indicative of future periods.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
revenue increased from $4.1 million in fiscal year 2025 to $67.3 million in fiscal year 2026, primarily due to increased project execution,
including a significant project that was 95.53% complete as of June 30, 2026. A substantial portion of this growth may reflect the timing
and progress of a limited number of large projects rather than recurring revenue. If similar projects are not awarded, if customers delay
capital expenditures, or if project completion percentages decline in future periods, our revenue and profitability could decrease materially.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>We
recognize revenue over time using the cost-to-cost method, and our results, contract balances and operating cash flows may vary significantly
from period to period</I></B>.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Revenue
is recognized over time using the cost-to-cost method, whereby project progress is measured by comparing costs incurred to date against
the estimated total contract costs. As a result, our revenue, gross profit, contract assets, deferred revenue, retention receivables
and operating cash flows depend on project commencement, progress toward completion, customer approvals, billing milestones, collection
timing, procurement timing and subcontractor payment terms, and our results may vary significantly from period to period. Our contracts
are typically billed through progress claims based on the value of work completed and certified by the client&rsquo;s consultant. Progress
payments are generally subject to a 5% retention, with 50% of the retention sum released upon issuance of the Certificate of Practical
Completion (CPC) and the remaining 50% released upon expiry of the Defects Liability Period (DLP), subject to the applicable contractual
provisions. Certified progress claims are generally payable within 30 to 60 days from the date of certification, although actual payment
timing may vary depending on the client&rsquo;s internal certification and payment approval processes. During periods of rapid project
growth, our revenue and net income may increase while our operating cash flow declines if contract assets, accounts receivable, project
retention or fixed deposits increase faster than customer collections. Changes in estimated total contract costs, disputed or unapproved
variation orders, delayed certifications or slower collections could therefore materially affect our reported results, liquidity and
working capital.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Demand
for our services depends substantially on industry capital expenditures, which are cyclical, difficult to predict and affected by customer
investment decisions.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s revenue and growth prospects are closely linked to capital expenditure programs of semiconductor manufacturers, integrated
device manufacturers, foundries, outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) providers, memory manufacturers, advanced packaging
companies and other technology customers. These customers periodically adjust facility-expansion, cleanroom, utility and infrastructure
investments based on market demand, product pricing, inventory levels, profitability, financing conditions, technology roadmaps, geopolitical
developments and macroeconomic conditions. A reduction, postponement or reprioritization of semiconductor capital expenditures could
reduce bidding opportunities, delay contract awards, slow backlog conversion and adversely affect revenue, margins and cash flow.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Semiconductor
capital spending may decline during memory market downturns, periods of excess capacity, inventory corrections or budget reductions.
The memory market, including dynamic random access memory (DRAM), NAND flash memory and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), has historically
experienced significant pricing and demand volatility. If memory manufacturers or other semiconductor customers experience weaker demand,
lower selling prices, excess inventory or lower utilization rates, they may defer facility expansions, cleanroom upgrades, process utility
investments, equipment installation projects or manufacturing support infrastructure. Even where projects are ultimately completed, delays
may disrupt resource planning, increase project costs and reduce the Company&rsquo;s ability to utilize personnel and subcontractors
efficiently.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
exposure to AI-related growth is indirect, and AI infrastructure investment may not result in revenue for us.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Any
exposure to AI-related growth is indirect and depends on whether demand for AI applications and computing capacity leads customers to
invest in semiconductor fabrication, advanced packaging, memory, testing, data-center-related manufacturing infrastructure and related
cleanroom or process utility projects. Increased AI adoption does not assure that customers will award contracts to the Company, that
projects will be undertaken in the Company&rsquo;s markets or that any awarded projects will be profitable.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">AI
infrastructure investment is also subject to substantial timing and demand uncertainty. Hyperscale cloud providers, technology companies
and data-center operators may reduce, delay or reprioritize capital expenditures based on profitability, utilization levels, return-on-investment
expectations, financing conditions, power availability, regulatory constraints or changes in technology architecture. If AI adoption
slows, customer spending becomes more disciplined or AI-related infrastructure buildout is reduced, semiconductor manufacturers and related
customers may scale back expansion plans, which could reduce demand for the Company&rsquo;s cleanroom, M&amp;E, civil, structural and
architectural (CSA), commissioning and facility-integration services.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Demand
related to graphics processing units (GPUs), HBM and advanced packaging may fluctuate and may not translate into project awards or sustained
growth.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Demand
for GPUs, HBM and advanced packaging may support long-term semiconductor infrastructure investment. However, these markets remain subject
to technology transitions, customer capital allocation, manufacturing constraints, competitive dynamics, pricing pressure, inventory
cycles and changes in computing architecture. Customers may satisfy demand through existing capacity, outsourcing, yield improvements,
equipment upgrades or investments in regions or suppliers where the Company does not participate. If GPU, HBM or advanced packaging demand
weakens, if expansion plans are delayed, or if customers choose competing contractors, the Company may not realize the anticipated benefits
of these industry trends.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Advanced
packaging also involves evolving technical requirements. As customers transition among chiplet architectures, 2.5D and 3D packaging,
heterogeneous integration, wafer-level packaging, fan-out packaging, HBM integration and other technologies, facility requirements may
change. The Company may need to invest in additional engineering resources, supplier relationships, qualification processes and project-management
capabilities to remain competitive. Failure to keep pace with customer specifications or technology migration could reduce the Company&rsquo;s
ability to win projects in advanced packaging and related semiconductor infrastructure markets.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Semiconductor
overcapacity could reduce customer spending, intensify competition and compress margins.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
semiconductor industry has historically experienced periods of rapid expansion followed by excess manufacturing capacity, inventory corrections
and reduced capital expenditures. Overcapacity may arise when manufacturers, encouraged by AI-related demand, government incentives,
supply-chain diversification initiatives or competitive pressures, add capacity faster than actual end-market demand develops. Excess
capacity can reduce customer utilization, pricing power and profitability, causing customers to postpone expansion phases, defer new
projects, reduce utility upgrades or prioritize operational efficiency over new facility investments.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">During
periods of reduced customer spending, competition among engineering, construction and infrastructure providers may intensify. A smaller
pool of available projects may lead to more aggressive pricing, less favorable contract terms, greater customer demands and lower margins.
Customers may also require stronger technical credentials, bonding capacity, financing support or contractual commitments. These conditions
could adversely affect the Company&rsquo;s ability to secure projects on commercially acceptable terms and maintain historical profitability.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Customer
concentration, project concentration and non-recurring project revenue may cause significant volatility in our results.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s business is project-based and may depend on a limited number of large customers or significant projects in any fiscal
period. Major semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, industrial and technology customers often undertake substantial but non-recurring
capital projects. Completion of a major project does not assure follow-on work, and future projects depend on customer capital expenditure
plans, qualification decisions, market conditions, procurement policies and competitive bidding. The loss of a significant customer,
reduction in spending by a key customer or failure to replace completed projects could materially affect revenue, profitability, backlog
and cash flow.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Large
projects are also subject to suspension, postponement, scope reduction or cancellation due to changes in market conditions, semiconductor
downturns, budget reductions, financing constraints, supply-chain disruptions, permitting delays, geopolitical developments, technology
changes, corporate restructuring or strategic reprioritization. Even where contracts provide for reimbursement of certain costs, the
Company may not recover all expected revenue, profit margins, overhead allocations, mobilization costs or business-development expenditures.
Project cancellations or delays may also result in underutilized personnel, equipment, subcontractor commitments and other resources,
increasing operating costs and reducing profitability.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>We
depend on a single customer, Chipbond Technology Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. (&ldquo;Chipbond&rdquo;), for a substantial majority of our revenue,
and the completion, loss or reduction of the Chipbond contracts would materially and adversely affect our results of operations.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
revenue is highly concentrated in one customer. For the year ended March 31, 2026, Chipbond contributed approximately 79.1% of our total
revenue of $67,259,375. A single Chipbond project accounted for revenue of $52,024,368, or approximately 77.4% of our total revenue for
the year ended March 31, 2026, generated gross profit of $6,341,627, representing a gross margin of approximately 12.20%, and was approximately
91.7% complete as of March 31, 2026. We completed two other Chipbond projects during the same fiscal year. For the three months ended
June 30, 2026, Chipbond contributed to approximately 24.7% of our total revenue, while Coherent Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. contributed approximately
66.3%. Our work for Chipbond is awarded on a project-by-project basis, and the completion of a project does not assure us of follow-on
work. Completion of the large Chipbond project and the need to obtain replacement awards may materially affect revenue, margins and working-capital
requirements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
