<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Because
the principal Chipbond project was substantially complete as of March 31, 2026, revenue attributable to that project will decline in
subsequent periods, and our results for the year ended March 31, 2026 should not be regarded as indicative of our results for future
periods unless we are able to secure replacement work of comparable size and margin. There can be no assurance that we will be awarded
additional projects by Chipbond or that we will be able to diversify our customer base.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
proposed CRaaS data-center infrastructure strategy is preliminary and may expose us to capital-intensive development, financing, leasing,
utilization and operating risks that differ from our historical EPC business.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Management
is evaluating a proposed CRaaS model under which we may seek to secure or prepare data-center sites, arrange power and network access,
develop or co-develop high-specification controlled facilities, and lease or provide related infrastructure to customers. This strategy
would require substantial upfront capital and may require land acquisition or land-use rights, power allocation, utility interconnection,
zoning, permits, governmental approvals, network connectivity, project financing, customer commitments, construction execution and ongoing
facility operations. If we implement our proposed CRaaS model and proceed with infrastructure build-out before definitive customer commitments,
financing or approvals are obtained, we could incur significant costs without realizing expected revenue. A CRaaS project could also
depend on one or a small number of anchor customers, and any customer delay, default, reduction in capacity requirements or renegotiation
could materially reduce expected cash flow and return on invested capital. In addition, data-center facilities are sensitive to power
availability, electricity tariffs, cooling performance, water availability, backup generation, technology obsolescence, utilization rates,
market rental rates and regional competition. Because these risks are different from our traditional project-delivery business, any failure
to manage the CRaaS strategy could adversely affect liquidity, profitability, leverage, management focus and reputation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>We
may be liable for customer losses if our systems contribute to manufacturing yield loss, production downtime or contamination events.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Semiconductor
and advanced packaging facilities operate under stringent contamination-control, environmental-stability and utility-reliability requirements.
Failures in cleanroom, electrostatic discharge (ESD), temperature and humidity control, vibration isolation, specialty gas, ultrapure
water (UPW), chemical delivery, clean dry air (CDA), exhaust, wastewater or electrical systems may contribute to yield loss, production
downtime, contamination, customer claims or reputational harm. Our contracts may require us to indemnify customers for such losses, may
provide for liquidated damages for delay or performance failures, and may not effectively limit our aggregate liability or exclude consequential
damages such as lost production. Even where we are not solely responsible, we may be required to defend claims, incur remediation costs,
forfeit retention amounts or suffer harm to customer relationships, and the amounts involved could exceed both the profit earned on the
affected contract and our available insurance.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
insurance coverage may be insufficient to cover project claims, professional liability, property loss or business interruption.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Cleanroom
and process utility projects may give rise to claims involving design errors, defective workmanship, delays, customer production losses,
contamination events, system failures, workplace accidents, environmental matters or business interruption. Insurance may be subject
to exclusions, deductibles, limits, coverage disputes and premium increases. If our coverage is unavailable, inadequate in amount or
scope, or more expensive than expected, we may bear these losses directly. Because we work predominantly under fixed-price contracts,
a single uninsured or underinsured claim could exceed the profit earned on the affected project and materially affect our results of
operations and liquidity.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
business may be adversely affected by shortages, wage inflation or productivity issues affecting subcontractors and site labor.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
rely on subcontractors and site labor for portions of installation, construction management, commissioning support and related project
work. Labor shortages, wage increases, site access restrictions, safety incidents, subcontractor underperformance or disputes may increase
costs and delay project completion. Because our projects are often subject to customer schedules and milestone requirements, labor disruptions
may materially affect margins and customer relationships.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
ability to execute projects depends on our ability to hire, retain and deploy qualified engineers, project managers and technical personnel.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
projects require experienced personnel with knowledge of cleanroom design, process utilities, HVAC and M&amp;E integration, specialty
gas systems, commissioning and controlled-environment operations. Competition for qualified semiconductor infrastructure personnel may
be significant. Our average employee workforce increased from approximately 33 employees in the twelve months ended March 31, 2025 to
approximately 52 employees in the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, with period-end headcount increasing from 34 to 59 employees, primarily
to support the execution of multiple concurrent projects, and we increased our reliance on subcontractors for specialized trades such
as civil, mechanical, electrical, HVAC, cleanroom installation and piping works in order to meet project schedules. Project activity
during the twelve months ended March 31, 2026 also required significant overtime, particularly for engineering, site supervision, safety,
quality assurance and quality control and commercial personnel supporting fast-track projects, which increased our staffing costs for
the period, and most technical and professional training programs were deferred to the twelve months ending March 31, 2027 as resources
were prioritized for project execution. We expect to resume regular training as project workloads normalize, but if we cannot attract,
retain, train or deploy qualified personnel, our ability to secure and execute projects, control costs, and maintain customer satisfaction
and project quality may be adversely affected.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
procurement and supply-chain activities may expose us to principal/agent, inventory, warranty and credit risks.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
frequently procure equipment and materials on behalf of our customers. Depending on whether we control those goods before they are transferred,
we may be required to present the related revenue on a gross basis, as principal, or on a net basis, as agent. A change in that determination,
or a revision to a prior determination, could significantly change our reported revenue and gross margin without any corresponding change
in our underlying activity or cash flows. Procurement activities may also expose us to supplier defaults, customer credit risk, inventory
or site risk, warranty claims, logistics delays, foreign-exchange exposure and disputes over specifications. If procurement risks are
not properly managed, our margins, cash flow and financial reporting could be adversely affected.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
contracts are generally fixed-price, and delays in the delivery of long-lead materials and equipment, or increases in their cost, may
increase project costs and delay revenue recognition.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
project costs and project schedules depend on the availability, delivery lead times and pricing of the specialized construction materials
and mechanical and electrical equipment required for industrial and cleanroom projects. Our top five suppliers accounted for approximately
20% and 24% of total procurement expenditure in the twelve months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Long-lead items, including
uninterruptible power supply (UPS) units, air volume control (AVC) units, vacuum pumps and fire roller shutters, typically require lead
times ranging from 14 to 21 weeks, and during the periods under review we experienced extended waiting times for these items, which delayed
the progress of certain projects. Our fixed-price contracts generally do not provide for automatic recovery of material price escalation,
although we may submit variations and change orders for changes in client requirements or instructions, and we generally bear the risk
of cost overruns arising from increases in labor, material, equipment or subcontractor costs within the agreed contractual scope. As
of March 31, 2026, we had outstanding purchase commitments of approximately $4.2 million relating to piping and civil and structural
works subcontractors. Because our contracts are generally fixed-price, increases in the price of materials or equipment, or delays in
their delivery, may increase project costs, delay the timing of revenue recognition and reduce gross margin in the periods affected.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

interest rate increases and foreign exchange movements may reduce margins and increase financing costs.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
costs may be affected by inflation in materials, equipment, freight, subcontractor labor, insurance and professional fees. Interest expense
may increase if bank loans, invoice financing or other credit facilities bear floating rates or are refinanced on less favorable terms.
Foreign exchange movements may also affect procurement costs, project margins and reported results. We may not be able to pass all cost
increases to customers, and adverse cost movements may reduce margins or cash flow.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
bank loans and invoice financing obligations may limit financial flexibility.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of June 30, 2026, we had bank loans totaling $6,056,543, comprising the $5,902,207 Multi-Option Loan and $154,336 Fixed Loan,
and invoice financing of $6,506,252. Debt service obligations may reduce cash available for operations and growth. Our facilities may
include covenants, security interests, guarantees, collateral requirements, dividend restrictions or events of default. If we cannot
comply with financing terms or refinance on acceptable terms, our liquidity and operations could be adversely affected.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Related-party
transactions may create conflicts of interest or governance concerns.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
have engaged, and may in the future engage, in transactions with related parties, including directors, officers, principal stockholders
and entities they control. Related-party transactions may be entered into on terms that are not the result of arm&rsquo;s-length negotiation,
may not be documented by written agreements, and may not be subject to the same procedures, controls and documentation standards applied
to transactions with unaffiliated third parties. Such transactions may give rise to actual or perceived conflicts of interest, complicate
our financial reporting and internal control over financial reporting, and attract scrutiny from investors, auditors or regulators. Although
related-party transactions are expected to be subject to review and approval by our audit committee in accordance with our related-party
transaction policy, we cannot assure you that these procedures will identify all conflicts of interest, that any such transaction will
be on terms as favorable as could be obtained from an unaffiliated third party, or that related-party transactions will not adversely
affect our business, results of operations or reputation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Material
weaknesses or deficiencies in internal control may be identified.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
have operated as a private company and have not been required to maintain internal control over financial reporting, or disclosure controls
and procedures, at the standard applicable to U.S.-listed public companies, and our finance function is small relative to the complexity
of our project accounting. Areas that may require enhancement include revenue recognition, cost-to-cost estimates, contract modifications,
procurement, related-party transactions, treasury, financial close, IT access controls, segregation of duties and disclosure controls.
If we identify one or more material weaknesses and are unable to remediate them, we may be unable to report our results accurately or
on a timely basis, we could be required to restate previously issued financial statements, we may fail to satisfy our reporting obligations
or applicable listing requirements, and investor confidence and the market price of our securities could decline.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
business plan depends on assumptions about future project awards and execution that are inherently uncertain, and our actual results
may differ materially.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
internal plans and growth assumptions rest on estimates of the number and value of project awards we will receive, average contract value,
quotation conversion rates, backlog and customer pipeline, semiconductor capital expenditure trends and our historical execution performance.
Each of these drivers is uncertain, is substantially outside our control and has varied significantly between the periods presented &mdash;
our quotation conversion rate by aggregate value, for example, moved from approximately 21.7% for the twelve months ended March 31, 2025
to approximately 13.2% for the twelve months ended March 31, 2026. If our assumptions prove inaccurate, or if project awards, financing,
customer demand or market conditions differ from our expectations, our actual results may differ materially from our plans, and you should
not place undue reliance on any projection, estimate or growth assumption.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Regional
supply-chain diversification and semiconductor localization may not produce material opportunities for us.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Supply-chain
diversification and semiconductor localization initiatives may increase investment in Southeast Asia, and other regions. However, the
timing, scale and geographic distribution of those investments are uncertain and depend on customer decisions, government incentives,
infrastructure readiness, power availability, labor resources, regulatory approvals, financing conditions and broader industry cycles.
Announced semiconductor investments may be delayed, modified, reduced or cancelled and may not result in projects within the Company&rsquo;s
target markets or service scope.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>All
of our revenue is generated in Malaysia, and our planned expansion into other Southeast Asian markets may not succeed.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
the year ended March 31, 2026 and the three months ended June 30, 2026, all of our revenue was generated from projects in Malaysia, and
we did not generate any revenue from outside Malaysia during these periods. We operate as one reportable segment, construction and maintenance
services. Revenue generated from projects in Malaysia was $67,259,375, representing 100% of our total revenue for the twelve months ended
March 31, 2026, compared with $4,062,207, also representing 100% of our total revenue for the twelve months ended March 31, 2025, and
Malaysia was accordingly the only country representing 10% or more of our revenue, assets or project exposure during both periods. We
do not currently expect our geographic concentration to change materially in the near term. We intend to expand our footprint into Singapore,
Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia, but our plans remain subject to market conditions, customer demand, regulatory requirements and other
factors, and there can be no assurance that we will successfully establish a presence or generate material revenue from such markets.
Expansion beyond Malaysia may also increase costs and operational complexity. Participation in new markets such as Singapore, Thailand,
Vietnam and Indonesia may require local licensing, personnel, bonding capacity, customer qualification, tax and legal compliance, partnerships
and management resources. The Company may not be able to establish market credibility, obtain required approvals, hire qualified personnel
or compete effectively against local or international providers. Any unsuccessful expansion could increase expenses without generating
expected revenue.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Export
controls, trade restrictions and geopolitical developments could disrupt customer investment plans, procurement and project execution.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
semiconductor industry is affected by export controls, sanctions, investment restrictions, trade measures, licensing requirements and
other regulatory actions involving advanced semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, software, materials and related technologies.
These measures may increase compliance costs, delay procurement, restrict technology transfers, disrupt equipment deliveries, alter customer
capital expenditure plans or limit the Company&rsquo;s ability to serve certain customers or projects. Because semiconductor infrastructure
projects often depend on specialized equipment, components and international suppliers, trade restrictions or regulatory uncertainty
could materially affect project timing, costs and margins.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Geopolitical
developments, including tensions involving Taiwan, may also affect semiconductor supply chains and customer investment decisions. Taiwan
plays a significant role in global semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, foundry services and technology development. Any
escalation of cross-strait tensions, military conflict, trade disruption, sanctions, export-control actions or changes in customer supply-chain
strategy could affect semiconductor capital expenditures, regional investment patterns, equipment availability, customer confidence and
the Company&rsquo;s future opportunities. The Company cannot predict the timing or impact of these developments.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I><U><A NAME="ju_027"></A>Risks
Related to Operating in Malaysia</U></I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>A
severe or prolonged slowdown in the Malaysian or global economy could materially adversely affect our business.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
business may be affected by economic conditions in Malaysia and globally. Economic downturns, geopolitical tensions, armed conflicts,
inflation, financing constraints, reduced business investment or declines in customer confidence may cause customers to delay or reduce
construction and maintenance projects. A deterioration in economic conditions could reduce demand for our services, create pricing pressure,
increase collection risk, impair profitability and adversely affect our cash flows, financial condition and prospects.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Fluctuations
in the value of the Malaysian ringgit against the U.S. dollar, and changes in Malaysian foreign exchange policy, could adversely affect
our reported results and our ability to transfer funds.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Substantially
all of our revenue and operating costs are denominated in Malaysian ringgit, while we report our financial results in U.S. dollars. Appreciation
or depreciation of the ringgit against the U.S. dollar affects our reported revenue, expenses, earnings, assets and liabilities, as well
as the U.S. dollar value of any dividends or other distributions. The ringgit appreciated significantly against the U.S. dollar during
2025 and 2026, and market commentators have cautioned that a sharp correction in either direction is possible. In addition, Bank Negara
Malaysia administers foreign exchange policy rules governing borrowing, investment abroad and the conversion and repatriation of proceeds,
and has in recent periods encouraged the repatriation and conversion of foreign earnings by Malaysian corporations. Changes in those
rules, including as a result of currency policy understandings under discussion between the U.S. Department of the Treasury and Bank
Negara Malaysia, could restrict our ability to move funds within our group, hedge our exposures or pay dividends. We do not currently
maintain a comprehensive currency hedging program.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Failure
to comply with environmental, workplace safety, building, construction, tax, labor or licensing regulations could adversely affect our
operations.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
projects may involve wastewater treatment, air pollution control, process exhaust, chemical delivery, specialty gases, electrical systems,
cleanroom environments, site construction and worker safety matters. We are subject to laws and regulations governing environmental protection,
workplace safety, building approvals, construction practices, labor, tax, licensing and cross-border operations. Non-compliance may result
in fines, project delays, work stoppages, remediation costs, reputational harm or loss of customer qualification.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>U.S.
tariff and trade measures affecting Malaysia could reduce customer capital spending and demand for our services.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Although
we perform our services within Malaysia, our customers are largely export-oriented semiconductor, electronics and industrial manufacturers
whose investment decisions depend on access to the U.S. market. In 2025, the United States imposed reciprocal tariffs on Malaysian goods,
subsequently reduced to 19% under the U.S.-Malaysia Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, with exemptions for certain semiconductor and electrical
and electronics products. A pending U.S. Section 232 investigation into semiconductor imports could result in additional duties that
would directly affect back-end assembly, packaging and test operations in Malaysia, which are among the principal activities of the customers
we serve. Reinstatement of higher reciprocal rates, withdrawal of existing exemptions, new export controls on semiconductor equipment
or technology, or retaliatory measures by other jurisdictions could cause customers to cancel, delay or relocate facility expansions
in Malaysia, reduce bidding opportunities and adversely affect our revenue and margins.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>We
may not be able to transfer cash or pay dividends when desired.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
operating subsidiaries may generate cash in Malaysia or other jurisdictions, while public company expenses and stockholder obligations
may arise at the holding-company level. Restrictions on dividends, intercompany loans, service fees or other transfers could limit our
ability to use cash efficiently across the group. We paid dividends of $253,424 in fiscal year 2026, but there can be no assurance that
dividends will be paid in the future.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>We
depend on foreign labor, and increases in levies, quotas or immigration restrictions could increase our costs or delay our projects.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Construction
and installation work in Malaysia depends heavily on foreign workers. We utilize foreign labor through various arrangements, including
foreign workers who perform work under our supervision and direction, as well as foreign workers engaged by our subcontractors or through
third-party labor or outsourcing arrangements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
employment and deployment of foreign workers in Malaysia are subject to quotas, source-country arrangements, permit approvals and annual
levies administered by the relevant Malaysian authorities. The annual levy for foreign workers in the construction sector in Peninsular
Malaysia is currently RM1,850 per worker, in addition to visa and processing fees. The Malaysian government has also implemented a multi-tier
levy framework under which the levy payable by employers may vary based on their reliance on foreign labor. Employer contribution obligations
for foreign workers under the Employees Provident Fund and social security regimes have also been extended in recent years.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Increases
in levies, tightening of quotas, delays or suspensions in permit approvals and renewals, minimum wage revisions, changes in requirements
applicable to foreign-worker arrangements, or the unavailability of workers from source countries could increase our direct or subcontracted
labor costs, disrupt our access to foreign workers, delay project delivery, expose us to liquidated damages and reduce our margins.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Cybersecurity
incidents could disrupt our operations or expose confidential project information.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
rely on information systems for engineering design, project management, procurement, financial reporting, customer communication and
vendor coordination. Cyberattacks, ransomware, unauthorized access, data loss or system disruptions could delay projects, compromise
confidential customer or supplier information, disrupt operations, increase costs and damage our reputation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>



<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Allegations
of forced labor or non-compliant recruitment practices, whether by us or our subcontractors, could result in enforcement action, loss
of customers and reputational harm.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Malaysian
employers of migrant workers have been subject to sustained scrutiny over recruitment fees, passport retention, wage deductions and worker
accommodation, including U.S. import enforcement actions against Malaysian producers and findings published by the Office of the United
States Trade Representative in June 2026 that named Malaysia among the economies whose prohibition and enforcement against goods produced
with forced labor were considered inadequate. Multinational customers commonly impose responsible sourcing and labor standards audits
on contractors and subcontractors working at their sites, and we may not be able to detect or prevent non-compliance by the labor suppliers
and subcontractors we engage. Allegations or findings of forced labor or unlawful recruitment practices, whether or not substantiated
and whether relating to us or to our subcontractors, could result in loss of customer qualification, contract termination, regulatory
investigation, penalties, restrictions affecting our customers&rsquo; exports and significant reputational harm.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Changes
in Malaysian government policy, taxation and licensing requirements could increase our costs or restrict our ability to bid for projects.</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
ability to operate depends on maintaining registration with the Construction Industry Development Board and other permits, approvals,
licenses and contractor grades, which are subject to renewal, periodic audit and compliance requirements. Following the July 16, 2026
share swap, which placed CCISB under the ownership of a Cayman Islands company, CCISB terminated its CIDB registration as a Grade G7
local contractor on October 5, 2026 and has applied to CIDB for registration as a foreign contractor. That application remains pending.
Any delay or refusal, or the grant of registration at a lower grade, in narrower categories or subject to restrictive conditions, could
materially and adversely affect our ability to perform existing contracts, tender for new projects and generate revenue. Malaysian
policy continues to evolve in areas that directly affect our cost base and project pipeline, including the scope of the sales and service
tax, subsidy rationalization for fuel and electricity, minimum wage revisions, electronic invoicing requirements and incentive programs
for the semiconductor sectors. Political developments, changes in administration, or shifts in policy toward foreign investment, local
participation requirements or industrial incentives could reduce the volume of projects available to us, increase our compliance costs,
or adversely affect the terms on which we compete.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_028"></A>Item
2. Financial Information.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_029"></A>BRAC
Management&rsquo;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
are a blank check company formed under the laws of the State of Delaware on April 16, 2021, for the purpose of effecting a merger, capital
stock exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, reorganization or other similar Business Combination with one or more businesses.
We intend to effectuate our Business Combination using cash from the proceeds of the IPO and the sale of the private placement, our capital
stock, debt or a combination of cash, stock and debt. The Company has not conducted any active operations since inception, except for
its efforts to locate suitable acquisition candidates. No revenue has been generated by the Company since inception. It is unlikely the
Company will have any revenues unless it is able to effect an acquisition or merger with an operating company, of which there can be
no assurance. The Company&rsquo;s plan of operation for the remainder of the fiscal year shall be to continue its efforts to locate suitable
acquisition candidates.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
principal business objective for the next 12 months and beyond such time will be to achieve long-term growth potential through a combination
with a business rather than immediate, short-term earnings. The Company will not restrict our potential candidate target companies to
any specific business, industry or geographical location and, thus, may acquire any type of business. The costs of investigating and
analyzing business combinations for the next 12 months and beyond such time will be paid with funds to be loaned to or invested in us
by our stockholders, management or other investors.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">During
the next 12 months we anticipate incurring costs related to:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
cannot assure you that our plans to raise capital or to complete our initial Business Combination will be successful.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">All
activity through June 30, 2026, relates to our formation and preparation of our IPO, which closed on January 13, 2022, and our search
for an initial Business Combination and our pursuit of approval of the Business Combination pursuant to the Business Combination Agreement
with Conwall.&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
our IPO, we completed the sale of 10,000,000 units that consisted of one share of common stock, par value $0.000001 per share and one
right, with each right entitling the holder thereof to receive one-tenth (1/10) of a share of common stock upon consummation of our Business
Combination. Simultaneously with the closing of our IPO, we closed a private placement of an aggregate of 446,358 units at a price of
$10.00 per private placement unit, generating total gross proceeds of $4,463,580. On February 9, 2022, the underwriters partially exercised
the Over-Allotment Option and purchased an additional 159,069 Units generating $1,590,690, and the Company completed the private sale
of 4,772 private units generating $47,720 for a total of $4,511,300 from the placement units. In connection with the closing and sale
of the Over-Allotment Units and the additional private placement units, $1,606,597 in proceeds from the Over-Allotment Closing (including
$31,814 of the Underwriters&rsquo; deferred discount) was placed in a U.S.-based trust account maintained by Continental Stock Transfer
&amp; Trust Company, acting as trustee.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of December 31, 2025, we had cash held in the Trust Account for the benefit of the Company&rsquo;s public stockholders of $1,257,251
(including $71,826 of interest earned during the year ended December 31, 2025). The trust fund account is invested in interest-bearing
demand deposit account and the income earned on those cash is also for the benefit of our public stockholders.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
January 9, 2026, we held a Special Meeting of Stockholders at which our stockholders approved an amendment to the Company&rsquo;s Charter,
(a) to extend the date by which we have to consummate a business combination from January 13, 2026 (the &ldquo;Termination Date&rdquo;)
by up to eighteen one-month extensions to July 13, 2027 and (b) to decrease the monthly extension fee to the Adjusted Monthly Extension
Loan commencing on January 13, 2026. The Company filed the amendment to the Company&rsquo;s Charter with the Office of the Secretary
of State of Delaware.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
also amended the investment management trust agreement dated as of January 10, 2022, as amended on January 10, 2023, June 12, 2023, January
8, 2024 and January 13, 2025 between the Company and Continental Stock Transfer &amp; Trust Company, allowing the Company to reduce the
amount of the Monthly Extension Loan to the Adjusted Monthly Extension Loan for each one-month extension beginning on January 13, 2026
until July 13, 2027, to extend the Termination Date for an additional eighteen (18) one-month extensions and to update certain defined
terms in the Trust Agreement. Stockholders holding 94,247 shares of common stock exercised their right to redeem their shares for cash
at an approximate price of $12.42 per share of the funds in the Trust Account. As a result, approximately $1,170,652 was removed from
the Trust Account to pay such holders. Following the redemption, 6,969 Public Shares remained outstanding and subject to redemption.
As of June 30, 2026, the Company had cash held in trust of $87,208. The Company must deposit into the Trust Account $139.38 for each
monthly extension period (commencing on January 13, 2026 and ending on July 13, 2027, unless the closing of the Company&rsquo;s initial
business combination shall have occurred).&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
management has broad discretion with respect to the specific application of the net proceeds of IPO and the Private Placement, although
substantially all of the net proceeds are intended to be applied generally towards consummating a business combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_030"></A>Results
of Operations</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
have neither engaged in any operations nor generated any revenues to date. Our only activities since inception have been organizational
activities, those necessary to prepare for our Initial Public Offering and identifying a target company for our initial Business Combination.
We do not expect to generate any operating revenues until after completion of our initial Business Combination. We generate non-operating
income in the form of interest income on cash and cash equivalents held in the Trust Account. We incur expenses as a result of being
a public company (for legal, financial reporting, accounting and auditing compliance), as well as expenses as we conduct due diligence
on prospective Business Combination candidates.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
the year ended December 31, 2025, we had a net loss of $949,536 consisting of general, administrative and operational costs of $655,503
and franchise tax of $19,491 and interest expenses of $346,368 offset by interest earned on cash held in Trust of $71,826. By comparison,
for the year ended December 31, 2024, we had a net loss of $1,189,262 consisting of general, administrative and operational costs of
$1,641,956 and franchise tax of $177,055 and interest expenses of $264,321 offset by interest earned on cash held in Trust of $894,070.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_033"></A>Going
Concern Consideration</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company expects to incur significant costs in pursuit of its financing and acquisition plans. In connection with the Company&rsquo;s
assessment of going concern considerations in accordance with Accounting Standards Update (&ldquo;ASU&rdquo;) 2014-15, &ldquo;Disclosures
of Uncertainties about an Entity&rsquo;s Ability to Continue as a Going Concern,&rdquo; management has determined that if the Company
is unsuccessful in consummating an initial business combination within the prescribed period of time from the closing of the Initial
Public Offering, the requirement that the Company cease all operations, redeem the Public Shares and thereafter liquidate and dissolve
raises substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. The financial statements do not include any adjustments that
might result from the outcome of this uncertainty. Management has determined that the Company does not have sufficient funds to fund
the working capital needs of the Company until the consummation of an initial business combination or the winding up of the Company as
stipulated in the Company&rsquo;s amended and restated memorandum of association. The accompanying financial statement has been prepared
in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America (&ldquo;U.S. GAAP&rdquo;), which contemplate
continuation of the Company as a going concern.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_034"></A>Internal
Control Over Financial Reporting</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
connection with the preparation and audit of the Company&rsquo;s financial statements as of and for the year ended December 31, 2025,
management identified material weaknesses in the Company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting. The material weaknesses consisted
of: (i) inadequate segregation of duties within accounting processes due to limited personnel; (ii) insufficient written policies and
procedures for accounting, information technology, financial reporting and recordkeeping; (iii) a lack of controls over the financial
reporting process that failed to recognize the accrual of penalties and interest on tax payables and resulted in the revision of previously
issued financial statements; and (iv) a lack of controls to monitor compliance with the provisions of the Trust Agreement relating to
the use of funds withdrawn from the Trust Account for payment of the Company&rsquo;s tax liabilities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">These
material weaknesses increase the risk that a material misstatement of the Company&rsquo;s annual or interim financial statements may
not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis, and could result in additional revisions to the Company&rsquo;s financial
statements, additional penalties and interest on tax liabilities, or noncompliance with the Trust Agreement. The Company is an emerging
growth company and is not required to have, and MaloneBailey, LLP was not engaged to perform, an audit of the effectiveness of the Company&rsquo;s
internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, MaloneBailey, LLP did not express an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&rsquo;s
internal control over financial reporting.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_035"></A>Material
Weaknesses in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
connection with the preparation and audit of the Company&rsquo;s financial statements as of and for the year ended December 31, 2025,
management identified material weaknesses in the Company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting. The material weaknesses related
to inadequate segregation of duties within accounting processes due to limited personnel, insufficient written policies and procedures
for accounting, information technology, financial reporting and recordkeeping, lack of controls over the financial reporting process
that failed to recognize the accrual of penalties and interest on tax payables and resulted in revisions to previously issued financial
statements, and lack of controls to monitor compliance with the provisions of the Trust Agreement related to the use of funds withdrawn
from the Trust Account for payment of the Company&rsquo;s tax liabilities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
a result of these material weaknesses, there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the Company&rsquo;s annual or
interim financial statements would not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. The Company has begun evaluating remediation
measures, including enhancing review controls over financial reporting, tax accruals and Trust Account withdrawals, and developing additional
accounting, information technology, financial reporting and recordkeeping policies and procedures. The material weaknesses will not be
considered remediated until the applicable controls have been designed, implemented and operated for a sufficient period of time and
management has concluded, through testing, that the controls are operating effectively.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_036"></A>Contractual
Obligations</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of June 30, 2026, we do not have any long-term debt, capital lease obligations, operating lease obligations or long-term liabilities,
other than an agreement to pay an affiliate of our Sponsor a monthly fee of $10,000 for office space, utilities and administrative support
provided to the Company and deferred underwriting commission payable to the underwriter. We began incurring these fees on January 13,
2022 and will continue to incur these fees monthly until the earlier to occur of the completion of the initial Business Combination and
the Company&rsquo;s liquidation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of June 30, 2026, the Company had recorded a deferred underwriting commission liability of $3,555,674 relating to its initial public
offering. The Deferred Underwriting Fees are $1,500,000 and will be settled at Closing through the issuance of Holdco Ordinary Shares
at a price per share equal to the higher of $0.50 and ten times the recent average trading price of the Company Rights, subject to a
9.9% ownership cap. The underwriter&rsquo;s net proceeds from sales of those shares may not exceed $1,500,000, and any remaining shares
must be returned to Holdco for no consideration. The 3,000,000-share figure is an illustration at the $0.50 floor before application
of the variable price and ownership cap, not a fixed issuance. All settlement shares legally outstanding at Closing are included in Closing
capitalization even if they may later be returned. The underwriting obligation is separate from the Covered Loan Amount and does not
cap loan conversion. The pro forma accounting for this share settlement is preliminary as described in the notes to the unaudited pro
forma financial information.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_037"></A>Critical
Accounting Estimates</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
preparation of financial statements and related disclosures in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United
States of America requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, disclosure
of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements, and income and expenses during the periods reported. Actual
results could materially differ from those estimates. We have not identified any critical accounting estimates.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_038"></A>Recent
Accounting Pronouncements</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
November 2024, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (&ldquo;ASU&rdquo;) 2024-03, &ldquo;Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive
Income-Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses&rdquo;, requiring public entities
to disclose additional information about specific expense categories in the notes to the financial statements on an interim and annual
basis. ASU 2024-03 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2026, and for interim periods within fiscal years beginning
after December 15, 2027, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of adopting ASU 2024-03.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Management
does not believe that any recently issued, but not effective, accounting standards, if currently adopted, would have a material effect
on the Company&rsquo;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ju_039"></A>JOBS
Act</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
JOBS Act contains provisions that, among other things, relax certain reporting requirements for qualifying public companies. We will
qualify as an &ldquo;emerging growth company&rdquo; and under the JOBS Act will be allowed to comply with new or revised accounting pronouncements
based on the effective date for private (not publicly traded) companies. We are electing to delay the adoption of new or revised accounting
standards, and as a result, we may not comply with new or revised accounting standards on the relevant dates on which adoption of such
standards is required for non-emerging growth companies. As a result, our financial statements may not be comparable to companies that
comply with new or revised accounting pronouncements as of public company effective dates.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Subject
to certain conditions set forth in the JOBS Act, if, as an &ldquo;emerging growth company,&rdquo; we choose to rely on such exemptions
we may not be required to, among other things, (i) provide an auditor&rsquo;s attestation report on our system of internal controls over
financial reporting pursuant to Section 404, (ii) provide all of the compensation disclosure that may be required of non-emerging growth
public companies under the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, (iii) comply with any requirement that may be adopted
by the PCAOB regarding mandatory audit firm rotation or a supplement to the auditor&rsquo;s report providing additional information about
the audit and the financial statements (auditor discussion and analysis) and (iv) disclose certain executive compensation related items
such as the correlation between executive compensation and performance and comparisons of the CEO&rsquo;s compensation to median employee
compensation. These exemptions will apply for a period of five years following the completion of our IPO or until we are no longer an
&ldquo;emerging growth company,&rdquo; whichever is earlier.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>
