<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Fiscal
2026 revenue growth primarily reflected more and larger projects, including the major Chipbond project. Gross margin improved from a
loss position as execution and the revenue base improved, while payroll and professional fees increased. The June 2026 quarter&rsquo;s
revenue rose 79.8% from the prior-year quarter; gross profit rose 54.5%, but gross margin declined by 2.5 percentage points and operating
expenses rose 80.4%. Net income improved by $69,346, or approximately 14.8%. These different trends show why annual growth should not
be extrapolated without considering project completion, mix and replacement awards.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">At
June 30, 2026, current assets of $26,700,776 less current liabilities of $19,231,752 produced working capital of $7,469,024. Only $7,016,296
of cash and cash equivalents was unrestricted; $4,793,377 of fixed deposits was pledged. Receivables, contract assets and retention balances
require collection, certification or release and are not interchangeable with available cash. Bank principal comprised the $5,902,207
Multi-Option Loan and $154,336 Fixed Loan, totaling $6,056,543, plus $6,506,252 of invoice financing. The latter comprises $3,674,669
of receivables financing and $2,831,583 of payables financing and was repaid July 2.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Multi-Option Loan&rsquo;s contractual facility amount is RM26.6 million as stated in Note 10. Facility availability, amounts drawn, outstanding
principal and translated U.S. dollar balances are separate measures. The detailed period analyses, cash-flow discussions, financing schedules,
backlog rollforward, contractual commitments and known-trend disclosures follow.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Unless
the context otherwise requires, references in this section to &ldquo;Conwall,&rdquo; &ldquo;the Company,&rdquo; &ldquo;we,&rdquo; &ldquo;us,&rdquo;
or &ldquo;our&rdquo; are intended to mean the business and operations of Conwall Construction Industries Limited, a Cayman Islands exempted
company (&ldquo;Conwall&rdquo;), and its wholly owned subsidiary, Conwall Construction Industries Sdn. Bhd., a company organized under
the laws of Malaysia (&ldquo;CCISB&rdquo;).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_002"></A>Overview</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
is a Malaysia-based specialized high-technology facility infrastructure company focused on cleanroom engineering, process utility systems,
controlled-environment construction, facility integration and related maintenance services for semiconductor, advanced manufacturing
and other technology-oriented customers. Through CCISB, Conwall provides highly integrated, full package construction, maintenance, engineering,
project delivery and facility infrastructure services for projects involving high-tech production facilities and controlled manufacturing
environments. As of June 30, 2026, CCISB had completed a total of 53 construction and facility infrastructure projects, each with a contract
price of at least $24,038 (RM100,000), since commencing operations in 2021, and had 12 additional projects in progress. &nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
has experienced strong growth in recent years. Conwall&rsquo;s total revenue increased by $63,197,168, or 1,555.7%, to $67,259,375 for
the year ended March 31, 2026 from $4,062,207 for the year ended March 31, 2025, and increased by $5,009,481, or 79.8%, to $11,286,729
for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $6,277,248 for the three months ended June 30, 2025.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_003"></A>Key
Factors That Affect Our Results of Operations</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
following factors have affected, and may continue to affect, our financial condition and results of operations. These factors should
be read together with the risk factors and other information included elsewhere in this registration statement.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
ability to secure new project awards</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
secure projects through customer qualification, tender invitations, technical and commercial submissions, negotiations and formal purchase
orders or contract awards. In the three months ended June 30, 2026, we submitted 212 quotations with an aggregate value of $3.9 million
and received 61 purchase orders with an aggregate value of $0.8 million, representing conversion rates of approximately 28.8% by number
of quotations and 20.0% by aggregate value. During the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, we submitted 705 quotations with an aggregate
value of $211.6 million and received 205 purchase orders with an aggregate value of $27.9 million, representing conversion rates of approximately
29.1% by number of quotations and 13.2% by aggregate value. During the twelve months ended March 31, 2025, we submitted 768 quotations
with an aggregate value of $261.7 million and received 241 purchase orders with an aggregate value of $56.7 million, representing conversion
rates of approximately 31.4% by number of quotations and 21.7% by aggregate value. The period from submission of a quotation to award
of a contract has historically been approximately three months, followed by approximately one week from award to project mobilization.
Our ability to participate in certain tenders depends on our satisfying applicable customer qualification requirements and maintaining
approved-vendor status. Our results of operations in any period may be materially affected by the number and aggregate value of project
awards we receive, and historical conversion rates are not necessarily indicative of future awards.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
ability to procure materials and equipment on a timely and cost-effective basis</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
project costs and project schedules depend on the availability, delivery lead times and pricing of the specialized construction materials
and equipment required for our projects. During the twelve months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, our procurement activities were primarily
affected by the availability and delivery timelines of specialized construction materials and mechanical and electrical equipment required
for industrial and cleanroom projects. Our top five suppliers accounted for approximately 20% and 24% of total procurement expenditure
in the twelve months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Long-lead items, including uninterruptible power supply (UPS) units,
air volume control (AVC) units, vacuum pumps and fire roller shutters, typically required lead times ranging from 14 to 21 weeks. During
the periods under review, we experienced extended waiting times for these items, which delayed the progress of certain projects. Our
fixed-price contracts generally do not provide for automatic recovery of material price escalation, although we may submit variations
and change orders for changes in client requirements or instructions. As of March 31, 2026, we had outstanding purchase commitments of
approximately $4.2 million relating to piping and civil and structural works subcontractors. Because our contracts are generally fixed-price,
increases in the price of materials or equipment, or delays in their delivery, may increase project costs, delay the timing of revenue
recognition and reduce gross margin in the periods affected. &nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
ability to attract, retain and deploy qualified personnel</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
ability to execute projects on schedule depends on our ability to attract, retain and deploy qualified engineering, project management
and site personnel. Our average employee workforce increased from approximately 33 employees in the twelve months ended March 31, 2025
to approximately 52 employees in the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, with period-end headcount increasing from 34 to 59 employees,
primarily to support the execution of multiple concurrent projects. We strengthened our engineering, project management, site supervision,
safety and support functions while increasing our reliance on subcontractors for specialized trades such as civil, mechanical, electrical,
HVAC, cleanroom installation and piping works in order to meet project schedules.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Project
activity during the twelve months ended March 31, 2026 required significant overtime, particularly for engineering, site supervision,
safety, quality assurance and quality control and commercial personnel supporting fast-track projects, which increased our staffing costs
for the period. As resources were prioritized for project execution, most technical and professional training programs were deferred
to the twelve months ending March 31, 2027. We expect to resume regular training as project workloads normalize.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
ability to strengthen our competitive advantages</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
operating results depend in part on our ability to maintain and strengthen competitive advantages in providing construction and maintenance
services for high-tech production facilities. Customers rely on us to support the construction and maintenance of production facilities
that may require specialized project execution, technical coordination, quality control and compliance with customer specifications.
Our ability to apply technical know-how, execute projects on schedule, meet customer performance requirements and maintain our reputation
with customers directly affects our profitability and our ability to secure additional projects.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Our
ability to control costs and improve operating efficiency</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
profitability depends substantially on our ability to control project costs, staffing costs and administrative expenses while maintaining
customer service quality and project execution standards. Construction costs, including purchased construction, subcontractor expenses,
materials, salaries and welfare, and outsourcing expenses, have a direct impact on profitability. In addition, staffing costs and administrative
expenses affect profitability and operating leverage. Our ability to attract and retain qualified employees, identify business opportunities,
secure new customer contracts, control procurement costs, manage subcontractors and improve employee productivity affects our margins
and operating results.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Project
timing, percentage-of-completion revenue recognition and working capital</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
results may vary significantly from period to period because revenue recognition, gross profit, contract assets, deferred revenue, retention
receivables and operating cash flows depend on project commencement, progress toward completion, customer approvals, billing milestones,
collection timing, procurement timing and subcontractor payment terms. During periods of rapid project growth, revenue and net income
may increase while operating cash flow may decline if contract assets, accounts receivable, project retention or fixed deposits increase
faster than customer collections.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Revenues</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Total
revenue increased by $5,009,481, or 79.8%, to $11,286,729 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, from $6,277,248 for the three months
ended June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the larger scale of the construction projects undertaken during the three
months ended June 30, 2026, including projects for two significant customers.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">During
the three months ended June 30, 2026, we recognized revenue of $7,479,374 from Coherent Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. (&ldquo;Coherent&rdquo;),
a significant customer, representing approximately 66.27% of our total revenue for the period. In addition, we recognized revenue of
$2,785,205 from Chipbond Technology Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. (&ldquo;Chipbond&rdquo;), another significant customer, representing approximately
24.68% of our total revenue for the period.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Revenue
is recognized over time using the cost-to-cost method, whereby project progress is measured by comparing costs incurred to date against
the estimated total contract costs, which we consider to faithfully represent the transfer of control and performance under each contract.
We generally bear the risk of cost overruns arising from increases in labor, material, equipment or subcontractor costs within the agreed
contractual scope. However, where changes in project scope, additional works, or employer-instructed modifications occur, we are contractually
entitled to seek reimbursement through approved variation orders in accordance with the respective contract terms. Our contracts are
typically billed through progress claims based on the value of work completed and certified by the client&rsquo;s consultant. Progress
payments are generally subject to a 5% retention, with 50% of the retention sum released upon the issuance of the Certificate of Practical
Completion (CPC) and the remaining 50% released upon expiry of the Defects Liability Period (DLP), subject to the contractual provisions.
Certified progress claims are generally payable within 30 to 60 days from the date of certification, although the actual timing of payment
may vary depending on the client&rsquo;s internal certification and payment approval processes.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
operate as one reportable segment, construction and maintenance services. All of our revenue was generated from projects in Malaysia.
Revenue generated from Malaysia was $11,286,729, representing 100% of our total revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared
with $6,277,248, also representing 100% of our total revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2025. Accordingly, Malaysia was the
only country representing 10% or more of our revenue, assets or project exposure during both periods. There was no material change in
our geographic concentration between the twelve months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025. We do not currently expect our geographic concentration
to change materially in the near term.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Cost
of Revenues</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Total
cost of revenues increased by $4,401,346, or 85.3%, to $9,562,122 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, from $5,160,776 for the three
months ended June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the commencement and execution of significant construction projects
during the three months ended June 30, 2026, which were substantially larger in scale than the other projects undertaken during the period.
The project required higher expenditures for materials and purchased equipment, subcontracted and outsourced construction work, as well
as other project-related costs, including logistics, testing and commissioning, and site-related expenses.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Gross
Profit and Gross Margin</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Gross
profit increased by $608,135, or 54.5%, to $1,724,607 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, from a gross profit of $1,116,472 for
the three months ended June 30, 2025. The improvement was primarily attributable to a significant increase in revenue resulting from
larger scale of construction projects undertaken during the three months ended June 30, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
the factors discussed above, our overall gross profit margin decreased by 2.5 percentage points to 15.3% for the three months ended June
30, 2026 from 17.8% for the three months ended June 30, 2025.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Operating
Expenses</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Operating
expenses increased by $418,500, or 80.4%, to $938,820 for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $520,320 for the three months ended
June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to higher general and administrative expenses, including payroll and employee
welfare expenses, and professional service fees, partially offset by lower research and development expenses.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">General
and administrative expenses increased by $381,313, or 75.5%, to $886,533 for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $505,220 for the
three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to (i) a $178,164 increase in salaries and welfare expenses
as Conwall hired additional personnel to support the expansion of construction projects during the period, (ii) a $160,571 increase in
consulting and professional service fees, primarily related to payments made to securities advisory specialists in connection with proposed
public company or other capital markets activities, and (iii) a $24,104 increase in travel and entertainment due to business expansion.
As a percentage of revenue, general and administrative expenses decreased slightly as the revenue base expanded, from 8.0% for the three
months ended June 30, 2025 to 7.9% for the three months ended June 30, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Research
and Development Expenses</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Research
and development expenses primarily consist of outsourced software development aimed at improving the efficiency of our construction project
management processes, as well as the development of a construction model to support project planning and execution. All R&amp;D activities
were outsourced to third-party developers. As a percentage of revenue, research and development expenses were 0.0% and 0.1% for the three
months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Other
Income (Expenses), Net</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Other
income (expenses), net primarily includes interest income generated from bank deposits, interest expenses for bank loans and notes payable,
gains or losses on foreign currency transactions, other income and other expenses. Total other income (expenses), net decreased by $98,390,
or 460.2%, to other expenses, net of $77,008 for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from other income, net of $21,382 for the three
months ended June 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to an increase of $105,191 in interest expenses resulting from higher
outstanding balances of bank loans and invoice financing during the current period.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Income
Tax Expense (Benefit)</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Income
tax expense was $170,107 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to an income tax expense of $148,208 for the three months
ended June 30, 2025, representing an increase of $21,899. The increase was primarily attributable to higher taxable income generated
during the three months ended June 30, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Revenues</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Total
revenue increased by $63,197,168, or 1,555.7%, to $67,259,375 for the twelve months ended March 31, 2026 from $4,062,207 for the twelve
months ended March 31, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to an increase in both the number and size of the construction projects
we undertook during the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, including one significant project for Chipbond Technology Malaysia Sdn. Bhd.
(&ldquo;Chipbond&rdquo;). We had 30 construction projects in progress during the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, compared with 22
construction projects in progress during the twelve months ended March 31, 2025.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">During
the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, we recognized revenue of $52,024,368 from a significant project for Chipbond, representing approximately
77.4% of our total revenue for that twelve-month period. The project generated gross profit of $6,341,627, representing a gross margin
of approximately 12.20%, and was 91.72% complete as of March 31, 2026. We also completed two other projects for Chipbond during the twelve
months ended March 31, 2026. In the aggregate, Chipbond accounted for approximately 79.1% of our total revenue for the twelve months
ended March 31, 2026. There was no outstanding accounts receivable balance due from Chipbond as of March 31, 2026. Because Chipbond accounted
for approximately 79.1% of our revenue for the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, the loss of Chipbond as a customer, the completion
of its projects without replacement work, or a significant reduction in the volume of work we perform for Chipbond in the future may
have a material adverse effect on our revenue and results of operations.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Cost
of Revenues</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Total
cost of revenues increased by $53,936,366, or 1,070.0%, to $58,976,956 for the year ended March 31, 2026 from $5,040,590 for the year
ended March 31, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the higher volume and larger scale of construction and maintenance projects
undertaken during the year ended March 31, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
increase in cost of revenue of $53.9 million in the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, was primarily driven by the commencement and
execution of a significant project during the year, which was substantially larger in scale compared with other projects. The significant
project required higher levels of materials and purchased equipment, subcontractor and outsourced construction works, as well as other
project-related costs including logistics, testing and commissioning and site-related expenses.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Gross
Profit and Gross Margin</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Gross
profit increased by $9,260,802, or 946.5%, to $8,282,419 for the year ended March 31, 2026 from a gross loss of $978,383 for the year
ended March 31, 2025. Gross margin improved by approximately 36.4 percentage points to 12.3% for the year ended March 31, 2026 from negative
24.1% for the year ended March 31, 2025. The improvement was primarily attributable to (i) a significant increase in revenue resulting
from a higher number and larger scale of construction projects undertaken during the year ended March 31, 2026; and (ii) a reduction
in cost of revenues as a percentage of revenue, which decreased to 87.7% in fiscal year 2026 from 124.1% in the year ended March 31,
2025, reflecting improved project execution and cost management.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Operating
Expenses</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Operating
expenses increased by $914,064, or 49.2%, to $2,773,120 for the year ended March 31, 2026 from $1,859,056 for the year ended March 31,
2025. The increase was primarily attributable to higher general and administrative expenses, including payroll and employee welfare expenses,
and professional service fees, partially offset by lower research and development expenses.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">General
and administrative expenses increased by $953,784, or 54.0%, to $2,720,097 for the year ended March 31, 2026 from $1,766,313 for the
year ended March 31, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to (i) a $737,209 increase in salaries and welfare expenses as Conwall
hired additional personnel to support the expansion of construction projects during the period, (ii) a $104,904 increase in consulting
and professional service fees, primarily related to payments made to securities advisory specialists in connection with proposed public
company or other capital markets activities, (iii) a $73,940 increase in office, utility and supply expenses due to business expansion.
As a percentage of revenue, general and administrative expenses decreased as the revenue base expanded, from 43.5% for the year ended
March 31, 2025 to 4.0% for the year ended March 31, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Research
and Development Expenses</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Research
and development expenses primarily consist of outsourced development costs. As a percentage of revenue, research and development expenses
were 0.0% and 1.3% for the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Other
Income (Expenses), Net</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Other
income (expenses), net primarily includes interest income generated from bank deposits, interest expenses for bank loans and notes payable,
gains or losses on foreign currency transactions, other income and other expenses. Total other expenses, net decreased by $168,736, or
62.7%, to other expenses, net of $100,500 for the year ended March 31, 2026 from other expenses, net of $269,236 for the year ended March
31, 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to an increase of $349,678 in gains on foreign currency transactions, partially offset
by an increase of $224,217 in interest expenses resulting from higher outstanding balances of bank loans and newly obtained accounts
payable invoice financing during the year ended March 31, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Income
Tax Expense (Benefit)</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Income
tax expense was $1,298,112 for the year ended March 31, 2026, compared to an income tax benefit of $3,286 for the year ended March 31,
2025, representing an increase of $1,301,398. The increase was primarily attributable to higher taxable income generated during the year
ended March 31, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Net
Income (Loss)</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
reported net income of $4,110,687 for the year ended March 31, 2026, representing a $7,214,076 improvement from a net loss of $3,103,389
for the year ended March 31, 2025. The improvement was primarily attributable to significantly higher revenue, improved gross profit
and positive operating leverage, partially offset by higher general and administrative expenses, interest expense and income tax expense.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_007"></A>Liquidity
and Capital Resources</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
principal source of liquidity was cash generated from operating activities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of June 30, 2026, our reported working capital of $7.5 million includes $7.0 million of unrestricted cash and cash equivalents that are
immediately available for general corporate purposes, while the $4.8 million of restricted fixed deposits with licensed banks are pledged
as security deposits to guarantee project completion and will be released only upon project completion or customer approval. Accounts
receivable of $6.1 million represent unconditional rights to payment, but conversion to cash depends on customer collection cycles, while
the $5.8 million of contract assets and $1.4 million of project retention receivables are not available until customers approve progress
billings or release holdbacks, and they should not be equated with immediately available cash. On the liability side, deferred revenue
of $0.8 million and contract liabilities of $0.9 million, accounts payable of $8.1 million will require cash settlement with suppliers,
project security deposits of $1.4 million are refundable to customers upon meeting contractual milestones, and the $6.5 million of invoice
financing and $0.6 million of bank loan principal due within one year represent current debt obligations that must be serviced from operating
cash flows. Of all these balances, only the unrestricted cash and cash equivalents are free for general use; all other asset balances
depend on customer approval, billing, collection cycles, or release of security, and none of the contract assets, project retention,
or pledged deposits should be viewed as readily available liquidity. Management therefore focuses on unrestricted cash and cash equivalents,
together with monitoring contract asset realization and retention releases, as the primary sources for meeting immediate liquidity needs.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
liquidity depends on unrestricted cash, collections of contract assets and receivables, customer payment timing and available committed
borrowing capacity. Unrestricted cash is distinct from restricted deposits and from unbilled contract assets, which require further billing
or customer approval before collection. At June 30, 2026, unrestricted cash was $7,016,296 and restricted deposits were $4,793,377. On
July 2, 2026, we repaid $6,506,252 of invoice financing. That repayment does not by itself establish our subsequent cash balance because
operating receipts, payments and other financing also affect liquidity. We monitor cash and near-term obligations through weekly forecasts.
If collections or financing fall short of our requirements, we may need additional capital or changes to our payment and expenditure
plans.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Accounts
Receivable Invoice Financing</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Accounts
receivable invoice financing is an arrangement under which the Company pledges eligible trade receivables as collateral to obtain short-term
financing from financial institutions prior to the collection of the underlying receivables. The financial institutions generally deduct
the applicable interest and bank fees from the financing proceeds and deposit the net proceeds into the Company&rsquo;s bank account.
On the maturity date, the Company is required to repay the full amount of the financing to the financial institutions. If the Company
repays the financing before the maturity date, the financial institution generally does not refund any interest deducted from the financing
proceeds at inception.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
May 2026, the Company pledged accounts receivable with a carrying amount of $5,433,214 as collateral for short-term financing of $3,753,566,
which had an original maturity of 78 days and bore interest at an annual rate of 4.95%. The lender deducted interest of $39,705 from
the financing proceeds at inception. As of June 30, 2026, the outstanding balance of the accounts receivable invoice financing arrangement
was $3,674,669, which was fully repaid on July 2, 2026. The lender did not refund any portion of the interest deducted from the financing
proceeds upon the early repayment.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Accounts
Payable Invoice Financing</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
August 2025, we established an accounts payable (AP) invoice financing arrangement with a financial institution to fund supplier payments
on approved invoices. Under this arrangement, the lender pays qualifying supplier invoices on our behalf, and we subsequently repay the
lender, typically within 90 days. Eligible invoices are subject to the lender&rsquo;s credit approval and are limited to those supporting
specific construction project costs.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_011"></A>Quantitative
and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Currency
exposure</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
functional currency of our operating subsidiary, Conwall Malaysia, is the Malaysian Ringgit (MYR), while the reporting currency of our
Cayman Islands holding company is the U.S. dollar (USD). As substantially all of our revenue, expenses, borrowings, and trade receivables
and payables are denominated in MYR&mdash;the subsidiary&rsquo;s functional currency&mdash;we do not hold material contracts, purchases,
debt, or cash balances in a currency other than the functional currency of the respective entity. Consequently, we believe our net monetary
exposure to foreign exchange fluctuations is limited.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
functional currency is MYR and our reporting currency is USD. Exchange-rate movements can affect translation of subsidiary net assets
into USD, with the resulting translation adjustment generally recorded in other comprehensive income and equity rather than as transaction
gains or losses in net income. That treatment does not mean there is no effect on comprehensive income. Foreign-currency monetary transactions
require a separate exposure analysis. We did not use foreign-currency hedging instruments during the year ended March 31, 2026 or the
three months ended June 30, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Interest-rate
exposure</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of June 30, 2026, our outstanding borrowings totaled $12,562,795, comprising a Multi-Option Loan of $5,902,207, a Fixed Loan facility
of $154,336, accounts payable invoice financing of $2,831,583 and accounts receivable invoice financing of $3,674,669. The Multi-Option
Loan, Fixed Loan facility and accounts payable invoice financing bear floating interest rates linked to the applicable lender benchmarks.
The accounts receivable financing was contracted at 4.95% per annum for an original term of 78 days, with interest deducted at inception.
A parallel 100-basis-point increase or decrease in the applicable floating benchmark rates, applied to the June 30 floating-rate principal
of $6,056,543, excluding the invoice financing liabilities paid off on July 2, 2026, would change annual pre-tax interest expense by
approximately $60,565, assuming those balances remained outstanding for a full year. This sensitivity excludes the accounts receivable
financing contracted for that fixed term. The accounts receivable and accounts payable invoice financing balances were subsequently repaid
on July 2, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">This
sensitivity analysis assumes that the outstanding principal balance remains constant and does not consider any potential changes in borrowing
levels or mitigating actions we might take in response to rate movements. We did not use any interest rate swaps, caps, or other hedging
instruments to manage interest-rate risk during fiscal 2026 or the three months ended June 30, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_012"></A>Trend
Information </B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company may benefit from long-term trends associated with AI-enabled semiconductor demand, advanced packaging growth, ASEAN supply-chain
diversification, semiconductor localization and Malaysia&rsquo;s established semiconductor ecosystem. Management also recognizes that
future results may be negatively affected by industry cyclicality, labor-market constraints, geopolitical developments, regulatory changes,
supply-chain disruptions and infrastructure limitations.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
near-term results depend on replacing revenue from substantially completed projects, converting qualified opportunities into binding
awards, mobilizing and delivering the new work, and collecting contract balances. The Chipbond project was approximately 91.72% complete
at March 31, 2026. Remaining performance obligations at June 30, 2026 were approximately $7.605 million. Project mix, award timing, margins,
financing and incremental public-company costs can cause material variation in results.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_013"></A>Emerging
Growth Company Status</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
are an &ldquo;emerging growth company,&rdquo; as defined in Section 2(a) of the Securities Act, as modified by the Jumpstart Our Business
Startups Act of 2012 (the &ldquo;JOBS Act&rdquo;). We may take advantage of specified reduced reporting and other requirements compared
to those that are otherwise applicable generally to public companies. These provisions include exemption from the auditor attestation
requirement under Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 in the assessment of the emerging growth company&rsquo;s internal control
over financial reporting. An emerging growth company preparing U.S. GAAP financial statements may elect the extended transition period
for new or revised accounting standards where private companies have a later compliance date. This permits delayed adoption where the
election applies; it is not an exemption from accounting standards.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_014"></A>Critical
Accounting Policies, Judgments and Estimates</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The preparation of these financial statements requires management
to make estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenue and expenses. Actual results may differ
from these estimates. We periodically review our estimates and assumptions based on available information.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
accounting policies that involve the most significant judgments and estimates, and that may materially affect our financial condition
and results of operations, primarily relate to revenue recognition and project estimates, accounts receivable and other asset recoverability,
long-lived assets, and contingent liabilities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Revenue
Recognition and Project Estimates</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
derive substantially all of our revenue from construction contracts. Revenue is generally recognized over time as we satisfy our performance
obligations, with progress measured primarily using the cost-to-cost method. This method requires management to estimate total contract
revenue and costs, including the effect of change orders, claims, incentives, penalties and other variable consideration.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Because
these estimates may change as projects progress, revisions to estimated contract revenue or costs may result in cumulative catch-up adjustments
to revenue and profit in the period of change. If estimated total contract costs exceed the transaction price, the expected loss is recognized
immediately. Accordingly, the accuracy of our revenue and profit recognition depends significantly on the accuracy of our project estimates.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Accounts
Receivable and Other Asset Recoverability</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
assess the collectability of accounts receivable and other assets based on factors such as customers&rsquo; financial condition, historical
collection experience, aging of balances and other relevant information. We record allowances when amounts are not expected to be fully
recoverable.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Long-Lived
Assets and Contingent Liabilities</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
evaluate long-lived assets for impairment when events or changes in circumstances indicate that their carrying amounts may not be recoverable.
We also assess potential contingent liabilities based on the facts and circumstances available at the reporting date and recognize provisions
when required under applicable U.S. GAAP.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Foreign
Currency Translation</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
reporting currency is the U.S. dollar, while our functional currency is the Malaysian Ringgit. Financial statement balances and transactions
denominated in currencies other than the functional currency are translated in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Foreign currency movements
may therefore affect reported results and shareholders&rsquo; equity.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
above policies involve significant management judgments and estimates and therefore may cause actual results to differ from those currently
estimated.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_015"></A>Item
3. Properties.</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company neither rents nor owns any properties. The Company utilizes the office space and equipment of its management at no cost. Given
the limited need of the Company, management believes that the office space is more than suitable and adequate. The Company currently
has no policy with respect to investments or interests in real estate, real estate mortgages or securities of, or interests in, persons
primarily engaged in real estate activities.</FONT></P>

the percentage ownership of that person, shares that the person has the right to acquire within 60 days are included, including through
the exercise of any option or other right or the conversion of any other security. However, these shares are not included in the computation
of the percentage ownership of any other person.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
management team is led by Johann Tse, Chief Executive Officer, who is the founder of Aquarian Capital, LLC, which advises corporate buyers
and sellers worldwide on M&amp;A transactions. Previously, Mr. Tse was the Director of International M&amp;A with Yum! Brands where he
led acquisitions, divestitures and franchising transactions across its quick service restaurants portfolio across many countries and
previously created and managed the corporate venture capital program for Rohm and Haas Company focusing on new materials and material-enabled
technologies, and helped broaden the Company&rsquo;s avenues for growth, in addition to corporate strategic planning and M&amp;A responsibilities.
Our management team is also led by Rongrong (Rita) Jiang, CFA, our Chief Financial Officer, who brings an extensive background in domestic
and international business focusing on accounting, finance, investment and management, as a Chartered Financial Analyst. Ms. Jiang brings
significant experience conducting due diligence to potential target investment companies, negotiating investment terms and creating transaction
structures working closely with portfolio companies, and providing value-add services such as introducing strategic partners, clients,
industry investors, relevant government authorities. Moreover, we are led by four exceptional independent directors who bring exceptional
experience, professionalism, knowledge that is integral to the Company and are committed to our success.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Johann
Tse</I></B>, our Chief Executive Officer, has more than 30 years of experience in the fields of corporate operation and management, venture
capital, and multinational mergers and acquisitions and has served as an independent board member of several Chinese companies listed
in the United States in sectors including tourism, media and restaurant supplies manufacturing and sales. As a pioneer, investor and
cross-cultural entrepreneur, he brings deep insights and rich experience for the formulation and implementation of corporate development
strategies for businesses in Asia, Europe and North America on a global scale. Mr. Tse founded Aquarian Capital, LLC in August 2005,
which specializes in advising international mergers and acquisitions and investments. Aquarian Capital has founded and manages companies
in several sectors, covering North America, Greater China, Israel, Asia, Europe and Latin America.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Aquarian
Capital&rsquo;s current initiatives include the development and financing of renewable energy projects, including overall planning of
EPC and beyond. Projects include photovoltaic, wind energy and pumped-storage hydroelectricity in North America, Latin America, Asia,
Africa and Europe. Aquarian Capital also develops and operates large-scale organic farms in Mexico that serves the US market. Aquarian
Capital was an early-stage investor in Boston Heart Diagnostics, which was later sold to Eurofins Scientific.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Prior

he acquired and sold a number of businesses in Asia, Western Europe, Russia and the Americas, including the successful acquisition of
Russia&rsquo;s largest fast-food chain. Prior to this, he was responsible for strategic planning, corporate mergers and acquisitions,
and founded and managed the corporate venture capital department for Rohm and Haas (now part of Dow Chemical), a major U.S. specialty
chemicals company, from 2000 to 2004, focusing on venture capital investment in material science companies in semiconductors, optoelectronics,

corporate VC investments and collaboration to accelerate innovation and step-out growth.</FONT></P>
