Adams was awarded engineer of the year for 2015. Before his employment with PPL, Mr. Adams channeled his career with AT&amp;T Mobility
from 1999 to 2016 serving as a contract senior network engineer and eventually becoming an engineering project manager. During his career
with AT&amp;T Mobility, he conducted resource planning and analysis, engineered, personally lead turn-key projects, commissioned, programmed,
and performed quality control audits towards the evolution of cellular telecommunications for TDMA, GSM, 3G, 4G and LTE networks.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">At
the height of his career with AT&amp;T Mobility, Mr. Adams managed more than 80 engineers in several markets throughout the United States,
which included the turf areas of Philadelphia, New York City, New England, Washington D.C., Baltimore, the Carolinas, Atlanta, Houston
and Los Angeles. During his employment with AT&amp;T Mobility, Mr. Adams was awarded employee of the year for all of the United States
for 2011. He was also the recipient of several employee of the month awards during his employment with AT&amp;T Mobility. Mr. Adams began
his professional career with the United States Navy in 1996 where he proudly served as a cryptologist and maintained a top-secret security
clearance while encrypting and deciphering unknown communication codes using state-of-the art equipment. While serving on board the ship,
USS Mt. Hood AE-29, Mr. Adams was a recipient of the sailor of the month award.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Mr.
Adams received his MBA degree in Innovation and Change Management at York St. John University, his Business Diploma in Business Administration
with a focus in Management in Operations at International Business Management Institute, a Technical Degree in Network Systems and Telecommunications
at Point to Point Technical Institute, and another Technical Degree in Cryptology and Military Intelligence at Naval Technical Training
Center.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
believe that our management teams&rsquo; expertise and experience in structuring complex transactions, accessing the capital markets,
and leading special purpose acquisition corporations, combined with our extensive relationships through a network of advisors and affiliates,
will make us a partner of choice for potential business combination targets. We expect to also take advantage of our management teams&rsquo;
extended network in Asia to identify and analyze potential business combination targets.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

in the post-Business Combination management structure. Mr. Ng has more than three decades of experience in engineering, facilities management,

maintenance operations. From 2018 until joining Conwall in April 2023, he served as Chief Operating Officer of MGI Construction Industries
Sdn. Bhd. Mr. Ng also has experience in foreign direct investment-related business development, including promoting investment opportunities
in Malaysia and supporting foreign investors evaluating manufacturing operations in Malaysia. He holds a Professional Master in Business
Administration.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Mengxiang
Hu</I></B>, aged 56, currently serves as a director of Holdco and chairman of Weixin Construction Co., Ltd. (China). Mr. Hu has more
than 25 years of experience in electromechanical engineering, cleanroom engineering and industrial construction, including corporate
strategy, business development and operational leadership across the PRC and overseas markets. In these leadership roles, he provides
strategic direction for the Group&rsquo;s corporate governance, business development and international expansion, while overseeing the
successful delivery of cleanroom and industrial engineering projects serving the semiconductor, electronics and pharmaceutical industries.
Mr. Hu holds an Executive Master of Business Administration from the Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business and a Bachelor&rsquo;s Degree
in Mechatronics Engineering from Xiangtan University<I>.</I></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Ng
Boon Teik</I></B><I>, </I>aged 57, has served as Chief Executive Officer of Conwall Construction Industries Sdn. Bhd. since April 2023.
Subject to the closing of the Business Combination and applicable board approval, Mr. Ng is expected to serve as Chief Executive Officer
in the post-Business Combination management structure. Mr. Ng has more than three decades of experience in engineering, facilities management,
industrial construction and business operations. From 1991 to 1996, he served as a Project Engineer with Rite-Rite (M) Sdn. Bhd. From
1996 to 1998, he served as Senior Superintendent for the Facility Department of Arkashic Kubota (Malaysia) Sdn. Bhd. From 2001 to 2018,
he served as Executive Director of Oceantrax Engineering Sdn. Bhd., where he was involved in company operations, facility projects and
maintenance operations. From 2018 until joining Conwall in April 2023, he served as Chief Operating Officer of MGI Construction Industries
Sdn. Bhd. Mr. Ng also has experience in foreign direct investment-related business development, including promoting investment opportunities
in Malaysia and supporting foreign investors evaluating manufacturing operations in Malaysia. He holds a Professional Master in Business
Administration.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Lim
Chong Hin</I></B>, aged 69, joined Conwall Malaysia in March 2024 as General Manager and was promoted to Chief Operating Officer with
effect from April 1, 2026. Subject to the closing of the Business Combination and applicable board approval, Mr. Lim is expected to serve
as Chief Operating Officer in the post-Business Combination management structure. Mr. Lim has more than four decades of experience in
engineering, industrial construction, project management and business operations. Prior to joining Conwall Malaysia, he served for approximately
eight years as General Manager of Hexagon Tower Sdn. Bhd., a company under Hexagon Holdings Berhad, an engineering group listed on Bursa
Malaysia. His experience includes project execution, operational management, engineering coordination, plant engineering, cleanroom facilities,
environmental control systems and industrial process infrastructure. In his current role, Mr. Lim is responsible for operational execution,
project delivery, engineering coordination and delivery risk management.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Kam
Lian Hooi</I></B>, aged 68, also known as Well Kam, has served as Chief Financial Officer of Conwall Malaysia since June 1, 2026 under
a flexible working arrangement. Subject to the closing of the Business Combination and applicable board approval, Mr. Kam is expected
to serve as Chief Financial Officer in the post-Business Combination management structure. Mr. Kam has more than 43 years of experience
in financial auditing, corporate management, organisation development and business transformation. From 1983 to 1990, he worked in financial
audit with firms of chartered accountants, including Ernst &amp; Young International. From 1991 to 2000, he served as Group Accountant
and Senior Corporate Development Manager of Malayan Electro-Chemical Industry Sdn. Bhd. Since 1997, he has served as Founder and Group
Managing Director of the VA Partners group of companies. Mr. Kam holds a Master of Business Administration from the University of Portsmouth
and a Diploma in Financial Accounting from Tunku Abdul Rahman College. He is a Chartered Accountant, a member of the Malaysian Institute
of Accountants and holds the FCCA qualification.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Dato&rsquo;
Seri Wong Siew Hai</I></B>, aged 74, will serve as an independent director of Holdco upon consummation of the Business Combination. Dato&rsquo;
Seri Wong has more than 28 years of experience in the electrical and electronics industry, with a focus on semiconductor and electronics
manufacturing across the Asia Pacific and global regions. From 1976 to 1996, he held various positions with Intel Technology Sdn. Bhd.,
a manufacturer of semiconductor computer circuits, rising from Quality Assurance Engineer to General Manager of its 8-bit micro-controller
business unit. From 1996 to 1998, he served as Vice President/Managing Director of the Asia Pacific Customer Centre of Dell Computer
Corporation. He rejoined Intel in 1998 and, until his retirement in 2004, served in senior roles including Managing Director of Assembly
Test Manufacturing in Malaysia, Vice President and Country Managing Director of Intel Malaysia and Vice President, Technology and Manufacturing
Group and General Manager of Assembly Test Manufacturing, with responsibility for Intel&rsquo;s assembly test factories worldwide. He
subsequently served as a director of Invest-In-Penang Berhad from 2004 to 2008, as a board member of the Malaysia External Trade Development
Corporation from 2005 to 2017 and as Chairman of the Malaysian American Electronics Industry from 2005 to 2021. He has served as President
of the Malaysia Semiconductor Industry Association since 2021 and as Chairman of the Electrical and Electronics Productivity Nexus, and
currently serves on the boards of directors of Nationgate Holdings Berhad and Skye Chip Berhad, each listed on Bursa Malaysia. Dato&rsquo;
Seri Wong holds a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Leeds, United Kingdom and a Master of Science
in Management Science from Imperial College of Science and Technology, University of London, United Kingdom.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Triomphe
Zheng Lin</I></B>, aged 58, will serve as an independent director of Holdco upon consummation of the Business Combination. Mr. Lin has
more than 30 years of commercial and professional experience in Australia and the PRC, with a focus on corporate finance, financial advisory,
audit and IPO-related services across a range of industries. From July 2007 to January 2014, he served as International Business Director
of BDO China Shu Lun Pan CPAs LLP, Fujian Office (formerly known as Lixin Zhonglian Mindu CPAs), an accounting firm in the PRC. Since
February 2014, he has served as a founding member and Deputy Managing Partner of the Fujian Office of Moore Dahua CPAs LLP, an accounting
firm in the PRC. Mr. Lin has served as a member of the supervisory board of ZhongDe Waste Technology AG, a company listed on the Frankfurt
Stock Exchange (Stock Code: ZEF), since September 2016. He previously served as an independent non-executive director of Da Sen Holdings
Group Limited, a company listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (Stock Code: 1580), from November 2016 to November 2021, and
he served with Cayman Golden Century Wheel Group Limited, a company listed on the Korea Exchange (Stock Code: 900280), from October 2016
to October 2018. Mr. Lin holds a Bachelor of Arts from Xiamen University in the PRC and a Bachelor of Commerce, majoring in accounting
and finance, from Macquarie University, Australia. He was conferred the designation of Certified Practicing Accountant by CPA Australia
in January 2000 and was admitted as a Certified Public Accountant by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in February
2025. He was first appointed as a Justice of the Peace (New South Wales) by the Attorney General of New South Wales in December 2000.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Holdco
will be required to file an annual report on Form 20-F within four months of the end of each fiscal year. Press releases relating to
financial results and material events will also be furnished to the SEC on Form 6-K. However, the information Holdco is required to file
with or furnish to the SEC will be less extensive and less timely compared to that required to be filed with the SEC by U.S. domestic
issuers. Accordingly, after the Business Combination, Holdco stockholders will receive less or different information about Holdco than
a stockholder of a U.S. domestic public company would receive. Nonetheless, Holdco intends to align itself with the practices adopted
by Nasdaq-listed U.S. domestic companies to the best of its ability to provide its stockholders with enhanced transparency and protection.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
a foreign private issuer, Holdco may follow qualifying Cayman Islands home-country practices instead of certain Nasdaq corporate governance
requirements, subject to disclosure and the required home-country counsel certification. Holdco currently intends to comply with Nasdaq&rsquo;s
majority-independent board and independent compensation and nominating committee standards and does not intend to rely on the controlled-company
exemptions. It proposes a seven-member board with four independent directors and an audit committee of three independent directors, subject
to the eligibility and appointment requirements described above. Any specific home-country practice Holdco ultimately elects to follow,
and the Nasdaq rule from which it differs, will be identified before listing. The applicable audit committee requirements under Exchange
Act Rule 10A-3 and Nasdaq Rule 5605(c), and the compensation recovery requirements under Nasdaq Rule 5608, must be satisfied notwithstanding
general FPI or controlled-company status.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Holdco
will adopt and administer a compensation recovery policy that complies with Exchange Act Rule 10D-1 and Nasdaq Rule 5608. The policy
will address recovery of erroneously awarded incentive-based compensation from current and former executive officers following a qualifying
accounting restatement and will be filed as an exhibit when required.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
consummation of the Business Combination, Holdco&rsquo;s board of directors will consist of seven directors, including four independent
directors. Additionally, Holdco will establish an audit committee (composed of the three independent directors), a nomination and corporate
governance committee (composed of three independent directors), and a compensation committee (composed of three independent directors).
These arrangements are in compliance with Nasdaq Rules. However, Holdco may follow the home-country practice for certain other corporate
governance practices in the future, which may differ from the requirements applicable to a U.S. company listed on Nasdaq. In addition,
pursuant to the Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association, Holdco may, but shall not (unless required by the law or
the rules and regulations of Nasdaq or the SEC and/or any other competent regulatory authority or otherwise under applicable law) be
obliged to, in each year hold a general meeting as an annual general meeting.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Controlled
Company Status</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> Under the no-redemption, $0.50 underwriting-price
and $10 loan-conversion illustration, Mr. Ng Boon Teik would hold approximately 50.421% of Holdco&rsquo;s voting power
and Holdco would qualify as a &ldquo;controlled company&rdquo; under Nasdaq rules. Actual status will depend on
final issuances, redemptions and cancellations; additional financing could reduce his holding to 50% or less. Under these corporate
governance standards, a company of which more than 50% of the voting power is held by an individual, group or another company is a &ldquo;controlled
company&rdquo; and may elect not to comply with certain corporate governance standards, including the requirements (1) that a majority
of its board of directors consist of independent directors, (2) that its board of directors have a compensation committee that is composed
entirely of independent directors with a written charter addressing the committee&rsquo;s purpose and responsibilities and (3) that its
board of directors have a nominating and corporate governance committee that is composed entirely of independent directors with a written
charter addressing the committee&rsquo;s purpose and responsibilities. Holdco currently does not intend to rely on these controlled-company
exemptions, consistent with its proposed board and committee arrangements described above. Upon completion of the Business Combination,
Holdco anticipates that the size of its board of directors will be seven directors, four of whom will qualify as independent directors
as defined within the meaning of the corporate governance standards of the Nasdaq listing rules and will meet the criteria for independence
set forth in Rule 10A-3 of the Exchange Act. Accordingly, if Holdco subsequently elects not to comply with such corporate governance
standards, you may not have the same protections afforded to stockholders of companies that are subject to all of these corporate governance
requirements.</P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Duties
of Directors</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Under
Cayman Islands law, all of Holdco&rsquo;s directors owe three types of duties to Holdco: (i) statutory duties, (ii) fiduciary duties,
and (iii) common law duties. The Cayman Companies Act imposes a number of statutory duties on a director. A Cayman Islands director&rsquo;s
fiduciary duties are not codified, however, the courts of the Cayman Islands have held that a director owes the following fiduciary duties:
(a) a duty to act in what the director <I>bona fide</I> considers to be in the best interests of the company, (b) a duty to exercise
their powers for the purposes they were conferred, (c) a duty to avoid fettering his or her discretion in the future and (d) a duty to
avoid conflicts of interest and of duty. The common law duties owed by a director are those to act with skill, care and diligence that
may reasonably be expected of a person carrying out the same functions as are carried out by that director in relation to the company
and, also, to act with the skill, care and diligence in keeping with a standard of care commensurate with any particular skill they have
which enables them to meet a higher standard than a director without those skills. In fulfilling their duty of care to Holdco, Holdco&rsquo;s
directors must ensure compliance with Holdco&rsquo;s Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association. Holdco has the right
to seek damages if a duty owed by any of its directors is breached.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
functions and powers of the Holdco Board include, among others:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse">
  <TR STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">appointing
    officers and determining the term of office of the officers;</FONT></TD></TR>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Terms
of Directors and Executive Officers</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The board of directors of Holdco consists
of seven (7) persons. Any Holdco&rsquo;s director whose term of office expires shall be eligible for re-election at a meeting of the
Holdco stockholders or re-appointment by the board of directors of Holdco. A director may be removed by ordinary resolution of stockholders
or by written notice signed by at least two-thirds of the directors then in office. Any vacancy on the board of Holdco
may be filled by directors of Holdco. A remaining director may appoint a director even though there is not a quorum of directors. In
addition, Holdco&rsquo;s officers are elected by and serve at the discretion of the board of directors of the Holdco.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_024"></A>Committees
of the Board of Directors</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
consummation of the Business Combination, Holdco will establish a separately standing audit committee, nominating and corporate governance
committee, and compensation committee. The Holdco Board will adopt a charter for each of these committees. Holdco intends to comply with
future Nasdaq requirements to the extent they will be applicable to Holdco.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Audit
Committee</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
the Closing, Holdco&rsquo;s audit committee will be composed of Triomphe Zheng Lin, Jingfang Chen, and Dato&rsquo; Seri Wong Siew Hai,
with Triomphe Zheng Lin serving as chairperson. The Holdco Board has determined that all such directors meet the independence requirements
under the Nasdaq listing rules and under Rule 10A-3 of the Exchange Act. Each member of the audit committee is financially literate,
in accordance with Nasdaq audit committee requirements, and possesses prior experience sitting in auditing committees of publicly-listed
companies. In arriving at this determination, the Holdco Board examined each audit committee member&rsquo;s scope of experience and the
nature of their prior and/or current employment.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Nomination
and Corporate Governance Committee</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
the Closing, Holdco&rsquo;s nomination and corporate governance committee will be composed of Arne Thompson, Triomphe Zheng Lin, and
Dato&rsquo; Seri Wong Siew Hai, with Arne Thompson serving as chairperson. The nomination and corporate governance committee is responsible
for the assessment of the performance of the board, considering and making recommendations to the Holdco Board with respect to the nominations
or elections of directors and other governance issues.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Compensation
Committee</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
the Closing, Holdco&rsquo;s compensation committee will be composed of Jingfang Chen, Triomphe Zheng Lin, and Dato&rsquo; Seri Wong Siew
Hai, with Jingfang Chen serving as chairperson. The compensation committee is responsible for reviewing and making recommendations to
the Holdco Board regarding its compensation policies for its officers and all forms of compensation. The compensation committee will
also administer Holdco&rsquo;s equity-based and incentive compensation plans and make recommendations to the Holdco Board about amendments
to such plans and the adoption of any new employee incentive compensation plans.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Code
of Ethics</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Holdco
will adopt a code of ethics that applies to all of its employees, officers, and directors. This includes Holdco&rsquo;s principal executive
officer, principal financial officer, and principal accounting officer or controller, or persons performing similar functions. Holdco
intends to disclose on its website any future amendments of the code of ethics or waivers that exempt any principal executive officer,
principal financial officer, principal accounting officer or controller, persons performing similar functions, or Holdco&rsquo;s directors
from provisions in the code of ethics.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Stockholder
Communication with the Board of Directors</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Stockholders
and other interested parties may communicate with the board of directors, including non-management directors, by sending a letter to
us at No. 25 &amp; 27, Lorong Valdor Jaya 3, Golden Gateway Perindustrian Valdor. 14200 Pulau Pinang, Malaysia for submission to the
board of directors or committee or to any specific director to whom the correspondence is directed. Stockholders communicating through
this means should include with the correspondence evidence, such as documentation from a brokerage firm, that the sender is a current
record or beneficial stockholder of Holdco. All communications received as set forth above will be opened by the Corporate Secretary
or his or her designee for the sole purpose of determining whether the contents contain a message to one or more of Holdco&rsquo;s directors.
Any contents that are not advertising materials, promotions of a product or service, patently offensive materials or matters deemed,
using reasonable judgment, inappropriate for the board of directors will be forwarded promptly to the chairman of the board of directors,
the appropriate committee or the specific director, as applicable.</FONT></P>

after the Company successfully consummates a business combination with an unaffiliated entity, that entity may desire to employ or retain

option or insurance programs or other similar programs have been adopted by the Company for the benefit of its employees.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

peer companies, which are designed to align the interest of executive officers with those of its stakeholders, while enabling Holdco
to attract, motivate, and retain individuals who contribute to the long-term success of Holdco. Specific determinations with respect

Directors. The proposed Appointment Agreements would appoint each independent director for an initial term
of two years, which will be automatically extended for successive 1-year terms unless either party gives the other party one-month prior
written notice to terminate.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Subject
to the procedures set forth in the relevant laws, regulations, and the Holdco&rsquo;s Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of
Association, an Independent Director shall be terminated for cause when he or she (i) is convicted of a criminal offense (ii) is sanctioned
by relevant securities regulatory authorities, or (iii) otherwise becomes ineligible to serve as a director or independent director under
applicable laws, regulations, the Nasdaq rules, and the Holdco&rsquo;s Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association. An
Independent Director may also be terminated by the stockholders of Holdco in accordance with the terms of the Holdco&rsquo;s Amended
and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association. If an Independent Director&rsquo;s direct family members (including parents, spouse,
children and their spouses, siblings, etc.) or other related parties become senior managers or related persons of Holdco, the Independent
Director must promptly notify Holdco in writing and resign. If, for any reasons, Holdco cannot elect a new director before the termination
or end of the Independent Director&rsquo;s term, the Independent Directors shall continue to perform their duties until the new Independent
Director(s) of the Holdco Board are elected. To the extent that an Independent Director is terminated or resigns without cause, Holdco
will negotiate the termination terms with the Independent Director in good faith.</FONT></P>

represent 20% of the outstanding shares upon completion of this offering (excluding the placement units and underlying securities). Up
to 375,000 insider shares held by our sponsor were subject to forfeiture by our sponsor depending on the extent to which the underwriters&rsquo;

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_028"></A>Holdco

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Advances
to Directors</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
Malaysia provided advances to certain directors of CCISB for the purpose of securing construction projects on the Company&rsquo;s behalf.
These advances were non-interest-bearing, unsecured, due on demand and were not supported by any written agreement. In February 2026,

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt"> The proposed Holdco board has seven members.
Under the proposed Holdco articles described in the transaction disclosure, director removal is by shareholder ordinary resolution or
written notice signed by at least two-thirds of directors then in office, subject to the operative articles. Investors should also review
the material risks concerning foreign enforcement, forum provisions and minority protections in Item 1A.<FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">(a)
Capital Stock.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company is authorized by its Certificate of Incorporation to issue an aggregate of 101,000,000 shares of capital stock, of which 100,000,000
are shares of Common Stock and 1,000,000 are shares of Preferred Stock. As of the date of filing this Registration Statement,
2,997,866 shares of Common Stock, including 6,969 shares subject to possible redemption, and zero shares of Preferred Stock
were issued and outstanding.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><I>Common
Stock</I></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
holders of Common Stock are entitled to one vote per share on all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders of the Company. All stockholders
are entitled to share equally in dividends, if any, as may be declared from time to time by the Company&rsquo;s board of directors out
of funds legally available. In the event of liquidation, the holders of Common Stock are entitled to share ratably in all assets remaining
after payment of all liabilities. The stockholders do not have cumulative or pre-emptive rights.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><I>Preferred
Stock</I></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our
Certificate of Incorporation authorizes the issuance of up to 1,000,000 shares of Preferred Stock with designations, rights and preferences
determined from time to time by our board of directors. Accordingly, our board of directors is empowered, without stockholder approval,
to issue Preferred Stock with dividend, liquidation, conversion, voting, or other rights which could adversely affect the voting power
or other rights of the holders of the Common Stock. In the event of issuance, the Preferred Stock could be utilized, under certain circumstances,
as a method of discouraging, delaying or preventing a change in control of the Company. Although we have no present intention to issue
any shares of our authorized Preferred Stock, there can be no assurance that the Company will not do so in the future.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
description of certain matters relating to the securities of the Company is a summary and is qualified in its entirety by the provisions
of the Company&rsquo;s Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaws, copies of which are filed herewith as exhibits.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">(c)
Warrants and Rights.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Except
in cases where the Company is not the surviving company in a Business Combination, each holder of a Public Right will automatically receive
one-tenth (1/10) of one share of common stock upon consummation of a Business Combination, even if the holder of a Public Right converted
all shares held by him, her or it in connection with a Business Combination or an amendment to the Company&rsquo;s Amended and Restated
Certificate of Incorporation with respect to its pre-business combination activities. In the event that the Company will not be the surviving
company upon completion of a Business Combination, each holder of a Public Right will be required to affirmatively convert his, her or
its rights in order to receive the one-tenth (1/10) of a share underlying each Public Right upon consummation of the Business Combination.
The Company will not issue fractional shares in connection with an exchange of Public Rights. Fractional shares will either be rounded
down to the nearest whole share or otherwise addressed in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Delaware General Corporation
Law. As a result, the holders of the Public Rights must hold rights in multiples of 10 in order to receive shares for all of the holders&rsquo;
rights upon closing of a Business Combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_034"></A>Item
12. Indemnification of Directors and Officers.</B></FONT></P>




<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">BRAC&rsquo;s
directors&rsquo; and officers&rsquo; insurance has lapsed. In addition to the indemnification arrangements described below, the amended
Business Combination Agreement requires prior-acts and go-forward directors&rsquo; and officers&rsquo; coverage at Closing, subject to
its specified availability standards and waiver procedures. Management intends to secure full protection in connection with the de-SPAC.
See Item 1A for the risks of the lapse and limitations of replacement coverage and Exhibit 2.3, Sections 6.7 and 9.2, for the contractual
requirements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Section
145 of the Delaware General Corporation Law provides that a corporation may indemnify directors and officers as well as other employees
and individuals against expenses including attorneys&rsquo; fees, judgments, fines and amounts paid in settlement in connection with
various actions, suits or proceedings, whether civil, criminal, administrative or investigative other than an action by or in the right
of the corporation, a derivative action, if they acted in good faith and in a manner they reasonably believed to be in or not opposed
to the best interests of the corporation, and, with respect to any criminal action or proceeding, if they had no reasonable cause to
believe their conduct was unlawful. A similar standard is applicable in the case of derivative actions, except that indemnification only
extends to expenses including attorneys&rsquo; fees incurred in connection with the defense or settlement of such actions, and the statute
requires court approval before there can be any indemnification where the person seeking indemnification has been found liable to the
corporation. The statute provides that it is not exclusive of other indemnification that may be granted by a corporation&rsquo;s certificate
of incorporation, bylaws, agreement, a vote of stockholders or disinterested directors or otherwise.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s Certificate of Incorporation provides that it will indemnify and hold harmless, to the fullest extent permitted by Section
145 of the Delaware General Corporation Law, as amended from time to time, each person that such section grants us the power to indemnify.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Delaware General Corporation Law permits a corporation to provide in its certificate of incorporation that a director of the corporation
shall not be personally liable to the corporation or its stockholders for monetary damages for breach of fiduciary duty as a director,
except for liability for:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

converts the reported loans, reduces the underwriting obligation to the model&rsquo;s retained $1,500,000 liability, and includes rights,
illustrative loan shares and 3,000,000 illustrative settlement shares in the SPAC-side share count. It retains the $530,000 administrative-fee
and $291,400 trust over-withdrawal liabilities. It does not import Conwall&rsquo;s book value into the SPAC-only numerator. The $10 IPO
Unit price is shown as a benchmark; each Unit included one common share and one right, and the table does not allocate that price between
those components. The analysis is preliminary because final settlement accounting, creditor terms and additional transaction costs remain
incomplete. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify"> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
the final row only, the assumed equity value of the target immediately after its September distributions is added to the preceding SPAC-only
tangible-book amount and divided by full combined legal shares of 32,293,888, 32,290,404 or 32,286,919. The value that makes that quotient
$10 is $10 multiplied by the applicable full share count less the SPAC-only tangible-book amount. This is a valuation sensitivity, not
a fairness conclusion, share-price forecast or estimate of Conwall&rsquo;s market value. The thresholds are equity values; they are not
directly comparable with the agreement&rsquo;s $250,000,000 enterprise value, which requires the contractual net-indebtedness adjustment.
Costs charged against equity would increase the threshold dollar for dollar; additional issuances would increase the share requirement.
A reclassification of the retained $1,500,000 settlement liability wholly to equity, with no other effect, would increase the SPAC-only
numerator by $1,500,000 and reduce each threshold by that amount. Final classification, measurement, offering-price allocation and share
treatment must be resolved before this preliminary illustration is used as the finalized Item 1604(c) disclosure.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> <B>Audit reports and auditor-related exhibits</B> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> MaloneBailey, LLP, PCAOB ID 206, issued BRAC&rsquo;s
signed report dated August 12, 2026 on its December 31, 2025 and 2024 financial statements. The report includes a going-concern paragraph
and an emphasis paragraph concerning use of trust withdrawals for operating expenses rather than corporate income taxes. KG CPA LLP,
PCAOB ID 6914, issued the signed August 10, 2026 report on Conwall&rsquo;s March 31, 2026 and 2025 statements. Neither report is an audit
opinion on internal control; neither annual report supplies an audit opinion on the subsequent unaudited quarter or the pro forma information. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> &nbsp; </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> A separate Securities Act auditor consent is not
required solely because a signed report is included in this Exchange Act Form 10, subject to any separate Securities Act incorporation
or use that requires consent. The signed reports remain required. Consent and report-use requirements for Holdco&rsquo;s Form F-4 must
be evaluated separately. Auditor clearance of the precise statements and report reproduced, including subsequent events and any reissuance
or dual dating, is distinct from filing a Securities Act consent. No unissued consent, clearance or interim review report is represented
as obtained. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><A NAME="a_019"></A><B>REPORT
OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-indent: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"></P>

<P STYLE="text-indent: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">To
the Shareholders and Board of Directors of</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-indent: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Broad
Capital Acquisition Corp.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-indent: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-indent: 0pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Opinion
on the Financial Statements</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
have audited the accompanying balance sheets of Broad Capital Acquisition Corp. (the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;) as of December 31, 2025 and
2024, and the related statements of operations, changes in stockholders&rsquo; deficit, and cash flows for the years then ended, and
the related notes (collectively referred to as the &ldquo;financial statements&rdquo;). In our opinion, the financial statements present
fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, and the results of its operations
and its cash flows for the years then ended, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Going
Concern Matter</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
accompanying financial statements have been prepared assuming that the Company will continue as a going concern. As discussed in Note
1 to the financial statements, the Company has incurred and expects to continue to incur significant costs in pursuit of its financing
and acquisition plans and the Company&rsquo;s business plan is dependent on the completion of a business combination within a prescribed
period of time and if not completed will cease all operations except for the purpose of liquidating. These factors raise substantial
doubt about the Company&rsquo;s ability to continue as a going concern. Management&rsquo;s plans in regard to these matters are also described
in Note 1. The financial statements do not include any adjustments that might result from the outcome of this uncertainty.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Emphasis
of a Matter - Corporate Income Tax Withdrawals from Trust Account</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
discussed in Note 3 to the financial statements, as of December 31, 2025, the Company withdrew $0.9 million of interest income earned
in the Trust Account for payment of the Company&rsquo;s corporate income tax liabilities as permitted by the terms of the Trust Agreement
governing the Trust Account. Through December 31, 2025, the Company had not used those funds to pay its tax obligations; instead the
funds were used to pay for general operating expenses which was not in accordance with the Trust Agreement.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Basis
for Opinion</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">These

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>BROAD
CAPITAL ACQUISITION CORP</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="a_022"></A>NOTES
TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>NOTE
1. DESCRIPTION OF ORGANIZATION, BUSINESS OPERATIONS</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Broad
Capital Acquisition Corp. (the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;) is a blank check company incorporated in the State of Delaware on April
16, 2021. The Company was formed for the purpose of acquiring, engaging in a share exchange, share reconstruction and amalgamation with,
purchasing all or substantially all of the assets of, entering into contractual arrangements with, or engaging in any other similar business
combination with one or more businesses or entities (a &ldquo;Business Combination&rdquo;). The Company is not limited to a particular
industry or sector for purposes of consummating a Business Combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>The
Financing</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of December 31, 2025, the Company had not commenced any operations. All activity from April 16, 2021 (inception) through December 31,
2025, relates to the Company&rsquo;s formation, the Initial Public Offering (as defined below), and its pursuit of an initial Business
Combination. The Company will not generate any operating revenues until after the completion of its initial Business Combination, at
the earliest. The Company will generate non-operating income in the form of interest income on cash and cash equivalents from the proceeds
derived from the Initial Public Offering. The Company has selected December 31 as its fiscal year end. The Company is an early stage
and emerging growth company and, as such, the Company is subject to all of the risks associated with early stage and emerging growth
companies.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s sponsor is Broad Capital LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the &ldquo;Sponsor&rdquo;). The registration statement
for the Company&rsquo;s Initial Public Offering was declared effective on January 10, 2022. On January 13, 2022, the Company closed its
Initial Public Offering of 10,000,000 units (the &ldquo;Units&rdquo; and, with respect to the shares of common stock included in the
Units being offered, the &ldquo;Public Shares&rdquo;), at $10.00 per Unit, generating gross proceeds of $100,000,000 (the &ldquo;Initial
Public Offering&rdquo;), and incurring transaction costs of $6,917,226, of which $3,500,000 was for deferred underwriting commissions
(see Note 7). The Company granted the underwriter a 45-day option to purchase up to 1,500,000 Units at the Initial Public Offering
price to cover over-allotments, if any. On February 9, 2022, the Underwriters partially exercised the over-allotment option and on February
10, 2022, purchased an additional 159,069 Units from the Company (the &ldquo;Over-Allotment Units&rdquo;), generating gross proceeds
of $1,590,690, and forfeited the remainder of the option.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Simultaneously
with the consummation of the closing of the Initial Public Offering, the Company consummated the private placement of an aggregate of
446,358 units (the &ldquo;Placement Units&rdquo;) to the Sponsor at a price of $10.00 per Placement Unit, generating total gross proceeds
of $4,463,580 (the &ldquo;Private Placement&rdquo;) (see Note 4). With the exercise of the Over-Allotment Units, the Company consummated
the Private Placement of 4,772 Placement Units to the Sponsor generating gross proceeds of $47,720.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
February 9, 2022, the underwriters partially exercised the over-allotment option and purchased an additional 159,069 Units, generating
gross proceeds of $1,590,690 and forfeited the remainder of the option, which is 335,233 shares of common stock. In connection with the
closing and sale of the Over-Allotment Units and the additional Placement Units (together, the &ldquo;Over-Allotment Closing&rdquo;),
a total of $1,606,597 in proceeds from the Over-Allotment Closing (which amount includes $31,814 of the Underwriters&rsquo; deferred
discount) was placed in a U.S.-based trust account established for the benefit of the Company&rsquo;s public stockholders, maintained
by Continental Stock Transfer &amp; Trust Company, acting as trustee.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Following
the closing of the Initial Public Offering on January 13, 2022, an amount of $101,000,000 ($10.10 per Unit) from the net proceeds of
the sale of the Units in the Initial Public Offering and a portion of the proceeds from the sale of the Placement Units was placed in
a trust account (the &ldquo;Trust Account&rdquo;), located in the United States and held as cash items or may be invested in U.S. government
securities, within the meaning set forth in Section 2(a)(16) of the Investment Company Act, with a maturity of 185 days or less, or in
any open-ended investment company that holds itself out as a money market fund meeting the conditions of Rule 2a-7 of the Investment
Company Act, as determined by the Company, until the earlier of: (i) the consummation of a Business Combination or (ii) the distribution
of the funds in the Trust Account to the Company&rsquo;s stockholders, as described below.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Trust
Account</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s management has broad discretion with respect to the specific application of the net proceeds of the Initial Public Offering
and the sale of Placement Units, although substantially all of the net proceeds are intended to be applied generally toward consummating
a Business Combination. There is no assurance that the Company will be able to complete a Business Combination successfully. The Company
must complete one or more initial Business Combinations with one or more operating businesses or assets with a fair market value equal
to at least 80% of the value of the net assets held in the Trust Account (as defined below) (excluding the deferred underwriting commissions
and taxes payable on the interest earned on the Trust Account). The Company will only complete a Business Combination if the post transaction
company owns or acquires 50% or more of the outstanding voting securities of the target or otherwise acquires a controlling interest
in the target business sufficient for it not to be required to register as an investment company under the Investment Company Act of
1940, as amended (the &ldquo;Investment Company Act&rdquo;).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
the closing of the Initial Public Offering, management has agreed that an amount equal to at least $10.10 per Unit sold in the Initial
Public Offering, including proceeds of the Placement Units, will be held in a trust account (&ldquo;Trust Account&rdquo;), located in
the United States and invested only in U.S. government securities, within the meaning set forth in Section 2(a)(16) of the Investment
Company Act, with a maturity of 185 days or less or in any open-ended investment company that holds itself out as a money market fund
selected by the Company meeting certain conditions of Rule 2a-7 of the Investment Company Act, as determined by the Company, until the
earlier of: (i) the completion of a Business Combination and (ii) the distribution of the funds held in the Trust Account, as described
below.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Redemption
Option</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company will provide the holders of the outstanding Public Shares (the &ldquo;Public Stockholders&rdquo;) with the opportunity to redeem
all or a portion of their Public Shares either (i) in connection with a stockholders meeting called to approve the Business Combination
or (ii) by means of a tender offer in connection with the Business Combination. The decision as to whether the Company will seek stockholder
approval of a Business Combination or conduct a tender offer, will be made by the Company. The Public Stockholders will be entitled to
redeem their Public Shares for a pro rata portion of the amount then in the Trust Account (initially anticipated to be $10.10 per Public
Share, plus any pro rata interest then in the Trust Account, net of taxes payable). The Public Shares subject to redemption will be recorded
at a redemption value and classified as temporary equity upon the completion of the Initial Public Offering in accordance with the Accounting
Standards Codification (&ldquo;ASC&rdquo;) Topic 480 &ldquo;<I>Distinguishing Liabilities from Equity</I>&rdquo;.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company will not redeem Public Shares in an amount that would cause its net tangible assets to be less than $5,000,001 (so that it does
not then become subject to the SEC&rsquo;s &ldquo;penny stock&rdquo; rules) or any greater net tangible asset or cash requirement which
may be contained in the agreement relating to the Business Combination. If the Company seeks stockholder approval of the Business Combination,
the Company will proceed with a Business Combination if a majority of the outstanding shares voted are voted in favor of the Business
Combination, or such other vote as required by law or stock exchange rule. If a stockholder vote is not required by applicable law or
stock exchange listing requirements and the Company does not decide to hold a stockholder vote for business or other reasons, the Company
will, pursuant to its second amended and restated certificate of incorporation (the &ldquo;Certificate of Incorporation&rdquo;), conduct
the redemptions pursuant to the tender offer rules of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (&ldquo;SEC&rdquo;) and file tender
offer documents with the SEC prior to completing a Business Combination.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><I>Stockholder
Approval</I></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">If,
however, stockholder approval of the transaction is required by applicable law or stock exchange listing requirements, or the Company
decides to obtain stockholder approval for business or other reasons, the Company will offer to redeem shares in conjunction with a proxy
solicitation pursuant to the proxy rules and not pursuant to the tender offer rules. If the Company seeks stockholder approval in connection
with a Business Combination, the Sponsor has agreed to vote its Insider shares (as defined in Note 6) and any Public Shares purchased
during or after the Public Offering in favor of approving a Business Combination. Additionally, each Public Stockholder may elect to
redeem their Public Shares without voting, and if they do vote, irrespective of whether they vote for or against the proposed transaction.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
