preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect reported
amounts. These estimates are based on information available through the date of the issuance of the financial statements. Therefore,
actual results could differ from those estimates.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84E_eus-gaap--FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy_z5NHbfbL8xm7" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Fair
Value of Financial Instruments</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company adopted ASC 820 &ldquo;Fair Value Measurements,&rdquo; which defines fair value, establishes a three-level valuation hierarchy
for disclosures of fair value measurement and enhances disclosures requirements for fair value measures. Current assets and current liabilities
qualified as financial instruments and management believes their carrying amounts are a reasonable estimate of fair value because of
the short period of time between the origination of such instruments and their expected realization and if applicable, their current
interest rate is equivalent to interest rates currently available. The three levels are defined as follow:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse">
  <TR STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 0.75in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Level
    1:</B></FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Inputs
    to the valuation methodology are quoted prices (unadjusted) for identical assets or liabilities in active markets.</FONT></TD></TR>
  <TR STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD></TR>
  <TR STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Level
    2:</B></FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Inputs
    to the valuation methodology include quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, and inputs that are observable
    for the assets or liability, either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the financial instruments.</FONT></TD></TR>
  <TR STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD></TR>
  <TR STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Level
    3:</B></FONT></TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Inputs
    to the valuation methodology are unobservable and significant to the fair value.</FONT></TD></TR>
  </TABLE>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of the balance sheet date, the estimated fair values of the financial instruments approximated their fair values due to the short-term
nature of these instruments. Determining which category an asset or liability falls within the hierarchy requires significant judgment.
The Company evaluates the hierarchy disclosures each year.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84D_eus-gaap--CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock_zVo2vrnq2pkh" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Cash
and Cash Equivalents</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Cash
and cash equivalents include cash on hand and cash in time deposits, certificates of deposit and all other highly liquid instruments
with original maturities of three months or less.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84B_ecustom--RestrictedFixedDepositsPolicyTextBlock_z8NkTat2eShf" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Restricted
Fixed Deposits</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Certain
customers occasionally require the Company to place fixed deposits with licensed financial institutions as security deposits to guarantee
the completion of construction projects. The Company places such fixed deposits with reputable banks for terms generally ranging from
six to twelve months. These deposits are typically withdrawn upon completion of the related construction projects or upon customer approval.
At that time, the principal and accrued interest are released to the Company and become available for working capital purposes. The Company
recognizes interest income on these fixed deposits over the term of the deposit.</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_85F_zTYm4SIqIte6" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>CONWALL

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>NOTES
TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" BORDER="0" STYLE="width: 100%; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
  <TD STYLE="width: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Note 2-</B></FONT></TD>
  <TD><B>SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued)</B></TD></TR>
</TABLE>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84B_eus-gaap--TradeAndOtherAccountsReceivablePolicy_zqLzqEOxwQAk" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Accounts
Receivable, net</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Accounts
receivable, net represent amounts for which the Company has an unconditional right to consideration and are stated at the invoiced amount,
net of an allowance for expected credit losses.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company evaluates the collectability of its accounts receivable on a recurring basis and maintains adequate allowance for expected credit
losses based on management&rsquo;s estimate of lifetime expected credit losses. In estimating the allowance, the Company considers historical
collection experience, the aging of receivable balances, customers&rsquo; financial condition and creditworthiness, current economic
conditions, reasonable and supportable forecasts, and other relevant factors that may affect customers&rsquo; ability to pay.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Accounts
receivable are written off against the allowance when management determines that collection is not probable. Subsequent recoveries of
amounts previously written off are recorded by reversing the allowance and reducing bad debt expense in the period received.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84F_ecustom--AdvancePaymentsPolicyTextBlock_zjgx4S5n9tO4" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Advance
Payments</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Advance
payments represent amounts paid to material suppliers and subcontractors in accordance with the terms of purchase contracts and subcontract
agreements. These payments are applied against future billings from the respective suppliers and subcontractors as materials are delivered
or services are performed.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Advance
payments are classified as current or non-current assets based on the Company&rsquo;s expectation of when the related goods or services
will be received and the advances will be applied. Amounts expected to be applied within one year after the balance sheet date are classified
as current assets, while amounts expected to be applied after one year are classified as non-current assets.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_842_ecustom--ProjectRetentionPolicyTextBlock_zcXdXCpIi0m" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Project
Retention</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Project
retention represents the portion of the contract price withheld by customers from progress payments on completed construction projects.
These retentions serve as security for the satisfactory performance of the Company&rsquo;s contractual obligations, including any defects
or warranty claims.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Retained
amounts are generally released to the Company in accordance with the terms of the respective contracts, typically within one to two years
after project completion upon the expiry of the warranty or defect liability period. Project retentions are classified as current or
non-current, depending on the expected release date, and are stated at their original amount less any allowance for doubtful accounts,
if required.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company periodically reviews the collectability of project retentions and recognizes an allowance when there is objective evidence that
the amounts may not be fully recoverable. Write-offs and recoveries are accounted for in the same manner as accounts receivable.</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_853_zt23SGCjr9Mk" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84B_ecustom--RefundableInsurancePremiumPolicyTextBlock_zsqOdKkeYdVi" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Refundable

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
August 7, 2025, the Company purchased a five-year key person life insurance policy covering one of its executive officers. The policy
provides a death benefit of $<FONT ID="xdx_90D_ecustom--DeathBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_c20250807_z5MZLH0fRegg" TITLE="Death benefit value of life insurance">370,627</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_908_ecustom--DeathBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_uMYR_c20250807_zZPPiVJx74w5" TITLE="Death benefit value of life insurance">1,500,000</FONT>) and a total and permanent disability benefit of $<FONT ID="xdx_903_ecustom--TotalAndPermanentDisabilityBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_c20250807_zNwPHeygc1fd" TITLE="Total and permanent disability benefit value of life insurance">370,627</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_90E_ecustom--TotalAndPermanentDisabilityBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_uMYR_c20250807_zFaWhVo7EtZ1" TITLE="Total and permanent disability benefit value of life insurance">1,500,000</FONT>) through August
6, 2030.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company paid a single premium of $<FONT ID="xdx_901_eus-gaap--PaymentsToAcquireLifeInsurancePolicies_c20250807__20250807_zomackHkNjVa" TITLE="Life insurance premium paid">247,161</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_906_eus-gaap--PaymentsToAcquireLifeInsurancePolicies_uMYR_c20250807__20250807_zHcps8mepYL3" TITLE="Life insurance single premium paid">1,000,311</FONT>) (exclusive of applicable taxes) upon issuance of the policy. The premium was
financed through a bank loan, with the loan proceeds disbursed directly by the lending institution to the insurer, as more fully disclosed
in Note 11 &ndash; Bank Loan &ndash; Fixed Loan. The policy does not provide any cash surrender value during its five-year coverage term.
Under the terms of the policy, if no death or total and permanent disability claim is made during the coverage period and the policy
remains in force through its maturity date, the insurer is contractually obligated to refund 100% of the single premium paid to the Company
upon maturity.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Because
the policy has no cash surrender value and the premium is contractually refundable only upon maturity, the Company records the refundable
premium as a noncurrent asset in the consolidated balance sheets. The Company evaluates the recoverability of this asset at each reporting
date and records an allowance for credit losses or impairment when collection of the refundable premium is no longer considered probable.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company does not recognize the $<FONT ID="xdx_903_ecustom--TotalAndPermanentDisabilityBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_c20250807_zNm07AOaghFb" TITLE="Total and permanent disability benefit value of life insurance">370,627</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_90E_ecustom--TotalAndPermanentDisabilityBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_uMYR_c20250807_zhijYd0jIpK1" TITLE="Total and permanent disability benefit value of life insurance">1,500,000</FONT>) death benefit or total and permanent disability benefit as an asset because the
receipt of such benefits is contingent upon future insured events. Any proceeds received under the policy in excess of the carrying amount
of the refundable premium will be recognized in earnings when realized.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_849_eus-gaap--ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock_ziyzL6HUN16" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Impairment
of long-lived assets</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company reviews long-lived assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an
asset may not be recoverable. Recoverability of assets to be held and used is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of an asset
to the future undiscounted cash flows expected to be generated by the asset. If such assets are considered to be impaired, the impairment
recognized is measured by the amount by which the carrying amount of the assets exceeds the fair value of the assets. <FONT ID="xdx_905_eus-gaap--ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsToBeDisposedOf_do_c20250401__20260331_zTTluzOdlbS2" TITLE="Impairment of long-lived assets"><FONT ID="xdx_909_eus-gaap--ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsToBeDisposedOf_do_c20240401__20250331_zB2ksgxG8ny3" TITLE="Impairment of long-lived assets">No</FONT></FONT> impairment of
long-lived assets was recognized for the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025.</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_849_eus-gaap--DepositContractsPolicy_zXMXRIclXlX6" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Project
Security Deposits </B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Project
security deposits represent amounts received from subcontractors as security for the satisfactory performance of their contractual obligations.
These deposits are refundable upon the completion of the related projects and the expiration of the applicable warranty period, provided
the subcontractors have fulfilled all contractual requirements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Project
security deposits are classified as current or non-current liabilities based on the Company&rsquo;s expectation of when the related deposits
will become refundable. Deposits expected to be refunded within one year after the balance sheet date are classified as current liabilities,
while those expected to be refunded after one year are classified as non-current liabilities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_841_eus-gaap--LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock_z6jQ3jbrGUja" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Lease</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company leases are classified as operating leases in accordance with Topic 842. Under Topic 842, lessees are required to recognize the
following for all leases (with the exception of short-term leases) on the commencement date: (i) lease liability, which is a lessee&rsquo;s
obligation to make lease payments arising from a lease, measured on a discounted basis; and (ii) right-of-use asset, which is an asset
that represents the lessee&rsquo;s right to use, or control the use of, a specified asset for the lease term.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">At
the commencement date, the Company recognizes the lease liability at the present value of the lease payments not yet paid, discounted
using the interest rate implicit in the lease or, if that rate cannot be readily determined, the Company&rsquo;s incremental borrowing
rate for the same term as the underlying lease. The right-of-use asset is recognized initially at cost, which primarily comprises the
initial amount of the lease liability, plus any initial direct costs incurred, consisting mainly of brokerage commissions, less any lease
incentives received. All right-of-use assets are reviewed for impairment. <FONT ID="xdx_902_eus-gaap--OperatingLeaseImpairmentLoss_do_c20250401__20260331_zVXtFHBzMVo7" TITLE="Impairment for right-of-use lease assets"><FONT ID="xdx_906_eus-gaap--OperatingLeaseImpairmentLoss_do_c20240401__20250331_zyjaKaQDbOh3" TITLE="Impairment for right-of-use lease assets">No</FONT></FONT> impairment for right-of-use lease assets incurred in the
years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_845_eus-gaap--ConcentrationRiskCreditRisk_zRQ1lg3Wdon" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Concentration
of Credit Risk</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Financial
instruments the Company holds that are subject to concentrations of credit risk are cash and accounts receivable arising from its normal
business activities. The Company maintains cash balances with high-credit-quality financial institutions that periodically exceed insured
limits. As of March 31, 2026 and 2025, substantially all of the Company&rsquo;s cash deposits were held with financial institutions in
Malaysia, and certain balances exceeded the applicable deposit insurance limits. Management regularly monitors the creditworthiness of
these institutions. The Company has not experienced any losses on such deposits and believes it is not exposed to any significant credit
risk on its cash balances.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, two customers and four customers, respectively, accounted for more than 10% of
the Company&rsquo;s total sales.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, two vendors and one vendor, respectively, accounted for more than 10% of
the Company&rsquo;s total purchases. </FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_853_zsZ0zDlybEM5" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_847_eus-gaap--RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock_zoRoGUAQhYak" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Revenue
Recognition</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company adopted ASC 606 upon inception. Under ASC 606, revenue is recognized when a customer obtains control of promised goods or services,
in an amount that reflects the consideration which the entity expects to receive in exchange for those goods or services. To determine
revenue recognition for arrangements that an entity determines are within the scope of ASC 606, the Company performs the following five
steps: (i) identify the contract(s) with a customer; (ii) identify the performance obligations in the contract; (iii) determine the transaction
price; (iv) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract; and (v) recognize revenue when (or as) the
entity satisfies a performance obligation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company derives its revenue primarily from construction contracts with customers. Revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606 when
control of the promised goods or services is transferred to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration the Company expects
to receive in exchange for those goods or services.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Construction
contracts generally contain a single performance obligation because the individual services provided under the contract are not separately
identifiable and are integrated into a single combined output, which is the completed construction project.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Revenue
from construction contracts is recognized over time, as the Company&rsquo;s performance creates or enhances an asset that the customer
controls as the asset is constructed. Progress toward completion is measured using the cost-to-cost input method, under which the percentage
of completion is determined by comparing costs incurred to date with total estimated contract costs. Revenue recognized to date is calculated
by applying the percentage of completion to the total transaction price of the contract. Revenue recognized in the current period represents
the cumulative revenue recognized to date less amounts recognized in prior periods.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Costs
incurred include direct materials, direct labor, subcontractor costs, and other costs directly attributable to the contract. Management
periodically reviews and updates estimates of total contract costs. Changes in estimated costs or contract value are recognized as cumulative
catch-up adjustments to revenue in the period the estimates change.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Timing
differences between revenue recognized and amounts billed to customers result in contract assets or contract liabilities. A contract
asset is recorded when revenue recognized exceeds billings to the customer, while a contract liability is recorded when billings exceed
revenue recognized. The Company expects substantially all contract assets outstanding as of March 31, 2026 to be billed and collected
within one year. The Company also expects substantially all contract liabilities outstanding as of March 31, 2026 to be recognized as
revenue within one year.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">If
at any time the estimated total costs of a contract exceed the transaction price, the Company recognizes the entire estimated loss immediately
in the period in which the loss becomes probable.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Revenue
Recognition (continued)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
certain sundry construction projects with a total contract price of less than $<FONT ID="xdx_909_eus-gaap--ConstructionPayableCurrent_iI_c20260331_zLS5nIEZv34e" TITLE="Contract price">24,020</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_903_eus-gaap--ConstructionPayableCurrent_iI_uMYR_c20260331_zwmjPufJEBPc" TITLE="Contract price">100,000</FONT>) or an expected duration of less than
<FONT ID="xdx_908_eus-gaap--ConstructionContractorContractDuration_dc_c20250401__20260331__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MaximumMember_zyydvNAO0uT7" TITLE="Contract duration">three months</FONT>, the Company does not apply the cost-to-cost input method to measure progress toward completion. Due to the short-term nature
and immaterial size of these contracts, revenue is recognized by matching revenue with the related costs incurred within the same reporting
period. Management has concluded that this approach does not result in a material difference from the revenue that would have been recognized
using the cost-to-cost input method.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company generally provides limited warranties for work performed under its contracts. These warranties are assurance-type warranties
that provide customers with assurance that the completed work complies with agreed-upon specifications and do not represent separate
performance obligations. Historically, warranty claims have not resulted in material costs incurred. Any estimated warranty costs are
included in the individual project cost estimates used in accounting for long-term contracts.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_845_ecustom--ProjectEstimatesPolicyTextBlock_zymHtR8T7bT4" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Project
Estimates</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Due
to the nature of our industry, there is significant complexity in our estimation of total expected revenue and cost, for which we must
make significant judgments. Our contracts with our customers may contain several types of variable consideration, including claims, unpriced
change orders, award and incentive fees, liquidated damages and penalties or other provisions that can either increase or decrease the
contract price to arrive at estimated revenue. Certain variable consideration, such as award and incentive fees, generally are earned
upon achievement of certain performance metrics, program milestones or cost targets and can be based upon customer discretion. We estimate
variable consideration at the most likely amount to which we expect to be entitled upon completion of a project. We include estimated
amounts in the transaction price to the extent it is probable we will realize that amount. Our estimates of variable consideration and
our determination of its inclusion in project revenue are based on an assessment of our anticipated performance and other information
that may be available to us.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">At
a project level, we have specific practices and procedures to review our estimate of total revenue and cost. Each project team reviews
the progress and execution of our performance obligations, which impact the project&rsquo;s accounting outcome. As part of this process,
the project team reviews information such as any outstanding key contract matters, progress towards completion and the related program
schedule and identified risks and opportunities. The accuracy of our revenue and profit recognition in a given period depends on the
accuracy of our project estimates, which can change from period to period due to a variety of factors including:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

  <TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">&#9679;</TD>
  <TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Complexity in original design;</FONT></TD></TR>

    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
  <TD>&#9679;</TD>
  <TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Different site conditions than assumed in our bid;</FONT></TD></TR>

    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
recognize changes in contract estimates on a cumulative catch-up basis in the period in which the changes are identified. Such changes
in contract estimates can result in the recognition of revenue in a current period for performance obligations which were satisfied or
partially satisfied in prior periods. Changes in contract estimates may also result in the reversal of previously recognized revenue
if the current estimate adversely differs from the previous estimate.</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_848_eus-gaap--RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationProvisionForLossPolicyTextBlock_zhFwnomZX8Z2" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Remaining
Performance Obligations </B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s remaining performance obligations as of March 31, 2026 represent a measure of the total dollar value of work to be performed
on contracts awarded and in progress. The Company had approximately $<FONT ID="xdx_909_eus-gaap--RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation_iI_c20260331_zJve80BCDDoa" TITLE="Remaining performance obligations">18,062,490</FONT> in remaining performance obligations as of March 31,
2026. <FONT ID="xdx_900_eus-gaap--RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationExpectedTimingOfSatisfactionExplanation_c20250401__20260331_znCuMGSxQjNg" TITLE="Remaining performance obligations description">The Company expects to recognize 100% of our remaining performance obligations within the next twelve months</FONT>.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Although
remaining performance obligations reflect business that is considered to be firm, cancellations, scope adjustments, foreign currency
exchange fluctuations or project deferrals may occur that impact their volume or the expected timing of their recognition. Remaining
performance obligations are adjusted to reflect any known project.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_849_eus-gaap--ComprehensiveIncomePolicyPolicyTextBlock_zxeO7QQ0TjD2" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Comprehensive
Income (Loss)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">ASC
220 &ldquo;Comprehensive Income&rdquo; established standards for reporting and display of comprehensive income/loss, its components and
accumulated balances. Components of comprehensive income/loss include net income/loss and foreign currency translation adjustments. The
component of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) consisted of foreign currency translation adjustments.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84F_eus-gaap--EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock_zDUZWHprSZqk" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Earnings
per share</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Basic
earnings per ordinary share is computed by dividing net earnings attributable to ordinary shareholders by the weighted-average number
of ordinary shares outstanding during the period. Diluted earnings per share is computed by dividing net income attributable to ordinary
shareholders by the sum of the weighted average number of ordinary share outstanding and of potential ordinary share (e.g., convertible
securities, options and warrants) as if they had been converted at the beginning of the periods presented, or issuance date, if later.
Potential ordinary shares that have an anti-dilutive effect (i.e., those that increase income per share or decrease loss per share) are
excluded from the calculation of diluted earnings per share. For the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company had <FONT ID="xdx_906_eus-gaap--WeightedAverageNumberDilutedSharesOutstandingAdjustment_do_c20250401__20260331_zItSYXZXTuKd" TITLE="Dilutive stocks"><FONT ID="xdx_903_eus-gaap--WeightedAverageNumberDilutedSharesOutstandingAdjustment_do_c20240401__20250331_zRhRNCV3hika" TITLE="Dilutive stocks">no</FONT></FONT> dilutive
stocks.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84A_eus-gaap--SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock_zJMSxZgWCALc" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Segment
Reporting</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">ASC
280, &ldquo;Segment Reporting,&rdquo; requires use of the &ldquo;management approach&rdquo; model for segment reporting. The management
approach model is based on the way a company&rsquo;s chief operating decision maker organizes segments within the Company for making
operating decisions assessing performance and allocating resources. Reportable segments are based on products and services, geography,
legal structure, management structure, or any other manner in which management disaggregates a company.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Management
determined the Company&rsquo;s operations constitute <FONT ID="xdx_90B_eus-gaap--NumberOfReportableSegments_pid_dc_uSegment_c20250401__20260331_zZqsDfJb9FFj" TITLE="Number of reportable segment">one</FONT> reportable segment in accordance with ASC 280, construction and maintenance
services.</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_853_zgErNEdg3HAf" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_845_eus-gaap--IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock_z6RugJtwZc5" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Income
Taxes</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company accounts for current income taxes in accordance with the laws of the relevant tax authorities. Deferred income taxes are recognized
when temporary differences exist between the tax bases of assets and liabilities and their reported amounts in the consolidated financial
statements. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years
in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a
change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period including the enactment date. Valuation allowances are established, when necessary,
to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount expected to be realized.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">An
uncertain tax position is recognized only if it is &ldquo;more likely than not&rdquo; that the tax position would be sustained in a tax
examination. The amount recognized is the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than 50% likely of being realized on examination.
For tax positions not meeting the &ldquo;more likely than not&rdquo; test, no tax benefit is recorded. Penalties and interest incurred
related to underpayment of income tax are classified as income tax expense in the period incurred.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

  <TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(1)</B></FONT></TD>
  <TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Income tax of Cayman Islands</B></FONT></TD></TR>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: right"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
was incorporated in the Cayman Islands as an exempted company and is governed by the tax laws of the Cayman Islands. Under the current
laws of the Cayman Islands, Conwall is not subject to income taxes or capital gains taxes. In addition, upon payment of dividends by
Conwall to its shareholders, no Cayman Islands withholding tax will be imposed.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

  <TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(2)</B></FONT></TD>
  <TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Income tax of Malaysia</B></FONT></TD></TR>
</TABLE>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
Malaysia was incorporated in Malaysia, and accordingly are governed by the income tax laws of Malaysia. The income tax provision in respect
of operations in Malaysia is calculated at the applicable tax rates on the taxable income for the periods based on existing legislation,
interpretations, and practices. Under the Income Tax Act of Malaysia, enterprises incorporated in Malaysia are usually subject to a unified
<FONT ID="xdx_90D_ecustom--EnterpriseIncomeTaxRate_pid_dp_c20250401__20260331__srt--StatementGeographicalAxis__country--MY_zXrABcsNMz8j" TITLE="Enterprise income tax rate">24</FONT>% enterprise income tax rate while prefer, tax holidays, and tax exemptions may be granted on a case-by-case basis. <FONT ID="xdx_90D_ecustom--EnterpriseIncomeTaxRateDescription_c20250401__20260331__srt--StatementGeographicalAxis__country--MY_zAJGqgbmu3J4" TITLE="Enterprise income tax rate description">The tax rate for
small and medium sized companies (generally companies incorporated in Malaysia with paid-in capital of $617,711 (RM2,500,000) or less,
and gross income of not more than $12,010,280 (RM50,000,000) is 15% on the first $36,030 (RM150,000) of taxable income and 17% on taxable
income from $36,031 (RM150,001) to $144,123 (RM600,000), with any remaining taxable income taxed at the standard rate of 24%</FONT>.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
local tax authority conducts periodic and ad hoc tax filing reviews on business enterprises after those enterprises complete their relevant
tax filings. Therefore, the Company&rsquo;s tax filings are subject to examination. It is therefore uncertain as to whether the local
tax authority may take different views about the Company&rsquo;s tax filings, which may lead to additional tax liabilities. As of March
31, 2026 and 2025, all of the Company&rsquo;s tax returns remain open for statutory examination by relevant tax authorities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
Malaysia evaluates its uncertain tax positions in accordance with applicable accounting guidance. The Company recognizes interest and
penalties related to uncertain tax positions, if any, as a component of income tax expense. As of March 31, 2026, the Company did not
have any significant uncertain tax positions requiring recognition or disclosure in the accompanying consolidated financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_852_ztyj0dEGs2r1" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84D_ecustom--ServiceTaxesPolicyTextBlock_zwxCLWwLFtY7" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Service
taxes</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Service
tax is a consumption tax levied by Malaysian tax authorities and is charged on any taxable service income provided in Malaysia by a registered
company in carrying on their business. Conwall Malaysia is engaged in the business of construction services, which became subject to
certain construction-related service tax on July 1, 2025. Conwall registered with the local tax authorities in August 2025 and commenced
filing service tax returns and remitting service tax beginning in September 2025.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
construction-related services, the applicable service tax rates are <FONT ID="xdx_903_ecustom--ServiceTaxRatesForConstructionWork_iI_pid_dp_c20260331_zOOEzV0wtAbk" TITLE="Service tax rates for construction work">6</FONT>% ad valorem for construction work and <FONT ID="xdx_904_ecustom--ServiceTaxRatesForMaintenanceOrRepairWork_iI_pid_dp_c20260331_zUWxmpwbyfhi" TITLE="Service tax rates for maintenance or repair work">8</FONT>% ad valorem for maintenance
or repair work. A company is required to register for service tax purposes if the total value of its taxable services over a rolling
12-month period exceeds, or is expected to exceed, the prescribed registration threshold of $<FONT ID="xdx_90A_ecustom--TaxableServicesRegistrationThresholdValue_iI_c20260331_zORGO0d34oQ7" TITLE="Taxable services registration threshold value">370,627</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_906_ecustom--TaxableServicesRegistrationThresholdValue_iI_uMYR_c20260331_zWkJvbYZ6mHb" TITLE="Taxable services registration threshold value">1,500,000</FONT>) for construction service
providers.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Service
tax collected is not an expense of the Company and is recorded as a liability until remitted to the Malaysian tax authorities. The Company
presents revenue net of service tax collected.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_842_ecustom--PayrollTaxesAndStatutoryContributionsPolicyTextBlock_zZ7kuhLZ2jz3" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Payroll
Taxes and Statutory Contributions</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Under
Malaysian income tax regulations, employers are required to withhold employee income taxes under the Monthly Tax Deduction (&ldquo;MTD&rdquo;),
also known as Potongan Cukai Bulanan (&ldquo;PCB&rdquo;), system administered by the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia. The Company withholds
the required amounts from employees&rsquo; salaries and remits them to the Malaysian tax authorities on a monthly basis. As the Company
acts solely as a withholding agent, amounts withheld from employees&rsquo; compensation are not recognized as an expense of the Company
and are recorded as payroll tax payable until remitted.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
addition to employee income tax withholdings, the Company is required to make statutory employer contributions to employee benefit programs,
including the Employees Provident Fund (&ldquo;EPF&rdquo;), the Social Security Organization (&ldquo;SOCSO&rdquo;), the Employment Insurance
System (&ldquo;EIS&rdquo;), and, where applicable, the Human Resource Development Corporation (&ldquo;HRD Corp&rdquo;). Employer contributions
are recognized as employee benefit expense in the period in which the related services are rendered. Amounts due but not yet remitted
are included in accrued payroll-related liabilities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">HRD
Corp administers Malaysia&rsquo;s Human Resources Development Fund, which is financed through a statutory levy paid by eligible employers.
Employers subject to the levy may apply for grants or reimbursements for qualifying employee training and workforce development programs.
Levies paid to HRD Corp are recognized as employee benefit expense, while reimbursements received for approved training programs are
recognized as a reduction of the related training expense or as other operating income, as appropriate, when realization is probable.</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_851_zFdeaIBoFsVc" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_847_ecustom--RelatedPartiesTransactionsPolicyTextBlock_zvsxI47o2RNc" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Related
Parties Transactions</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company identifies related parties, and accounts for, discloses related party transactions in accordance with ASC 850, &ldquo;Related
Party Disclosures&rdquo; and other relevant ASC standards.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">A
related party is generally defined as (i) any person that holds 10% or more of the Company&rsquo;s securities and their immediate families,
(ii) the Company&rsquo;s management, (iii) someone that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by or is under common control
with the Company, or (iv) anyone who can significantly influence the financial and operating decisions of the Company. A transaction
is considered as a related party transaction when there is a transfer of resources or obligations between related parties. Related parties
may be individuals or corporate entities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Transactions
involving related parties cannot be presumed to be carried out on an arm&rsquo;s-length basis, as the requisite conditions of competitive,
free market dealings may not exist. Representations about transactions with related parties, if made, shall not imply that the related
party transactions were consummated on terms equivalent to those that prevail in arm&rsquo;s-length transactions unless such representations
can be substantiated. It is not, however, practical to determine the fair value of amounts of related party transactions due to their
related party nature.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84B_eus-gaap--NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock_zr82MxLremnb" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Recently
Issued Accounting Pronouncements</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
November 2024, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (&ldquo;ASU&rdquo;) No. 2024-03, Income Statement &ndash; Reporting Comprehensive
Income &ndash; Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses, requiring public companies
to disclose additional information about specific expense categories in the notes to the consolidated financial statements on an annual
and interim basis. ASU No. 2024-03 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2026, and for interim periods beginning
after December 15, 2027. Early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of this ASU on its unaudited consolidated
financial statements and related disclosures.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
December 2025, the FASB issued ASU No. 2025-11, Interim Reporting (Topic 270): Narrow-Scope Improvements, which clarifies the guidance
in Topic 270 to improve the consistency of interim financial reporting. The ASU provides a comprehensive list of required interim disclosures
and introduces a disclosure principle requiring entities to disclose events since the end of the last annual reporting period that have
a material impact on the entity. ASU No. 2025-11 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2027, including interim periods
within those fiscal years, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of this ASU on its unaudited
interim consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.</FONT></P>

These leases have lease terms ranging from <FONT ID="xdx_908_eus-gaap--LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract_iI_dtY_c20260331__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MinimumMember_zntHSaxPh1S4" TITLE="Lease term" STYLE="display: none">2
</FONT>two to <FONT ID="xdx_909_eus-gaap--LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract_iI_dc_c20260331__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MaximumMember_zrOrTUH2jlKa" TITLE="Lease term">four years</FONT>. The Company has elected to not recognize lease assets and liabilities for leases with a term less than twelve
months.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Operating lease right-of-use assets and corresponding liabilities are recognized at commencement date based on the present value of lease
payments over the lease term. The discount rate used to calculate present value is incremental borrowing rate or, if available, the rate
implicit in the lease. The Company determines the incremental borrowing rates for these leases based primarily on lease terms were <FONT ID="xdx_906_eus-gaap--OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageDiscountRatePercent_iI_pid_dp_c20260331_z2UpMnRjvRbj" TITLE="Lease incremental borrowing rates">6</FONT>%.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
loan is scheduled to mature during the year ending March 31, 2027. The remaining contractual payments total $<FONT ID="xdx_907_eus-gaap--ContractualObligation_iI_c20260331__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--VehicleFinancingAgreementMember_ziXNJF7FAy9a" TITLE="Remaining contractual payments">3,099</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_906_eus-gaap--ContractualObligation_iI_uMYR_c20260331__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--VehicleFinancingAgreementMember_z6spAryfnrW" TITLE="Remaining contractual payments">12,545</FONT>), consisting
of $<FONT ID="xdx_90A_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentFaceAmount_iI_c20260331__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--VehicleFinancingAgreementMember_zhSv6YY0H4ah" TITLE="Principal amount payable">3,076</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_901_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentFaceAmount_iI_uMYR_c20260331__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--VehicleFinancingAgreementMember_zZTOKbRqnii7" TITLE="Principal amount payable">12,450</FONT>) of principal and $<FONT ID="xdx_909_eus-gaap--InterestPayableCurrent_iI_c20260331__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--VehicleFinancingAgreementMember_z8kghPR5C1n3" TITLE="Interest payable">23</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_908_eus-gaap--InterestPayableCurrent_iI_uMYR_c20260331__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--VehicleFinancingAgreementMember_zxPsrXSR6hp" TITLE="Interest payable">95</FONT>) of interest.</FONT></P>
