<P ID="xdx_80D_ecustom--InvoiceFinancingLiabilitiesTextBlock_zd8J8wus2L78" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" BORDER="0" STYLE="width: 100%; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
  <TD STYLE="width: 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Note 9-</B></FONT></TD>
  <TD><B><FONT ID="xdx_82F_za4g7WXCLyf2">INVOICE FINANCING LIABILITIES</FONT></B></TD></TR>
</TABLE>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company participates in accounts receivable (&ldquo;AR&rdquo;) and accounts payable (&ldquo;AP&rdquo;) invoice financing arrangements
with financial institutions to manage working capital and enhance liquidity.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: right"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" BORDER="0" STYLE="width: 100%; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">&nbsp;</TD>
  <TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(1)</B></FONT></TD>
  <TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Accounts Receivable Invoice Financing</B></FONT></TD></TR>
</TABLE>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Accounts
receivable invoice financing is an arrangement under which the Company pledges eligible trade receivables as collateral to obtain short-term
financing from financial institutions prior to customer collection. The Company retains ownership of the underlying receivables and continues
to recognize such receivables in its consolidated balance sheets. Accordingly, the arrangement is accounted for as a secured borrowing.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
November 2025, the Company pledged accounts receivable with a carrying amount of $<FONT ID="xdx_905_ecustom--AccountsReceivableCarryingAmount_iI_c20251130_zpAnaQr9oM32" TITLE="Accounts receivable carrying amount">11,118,798</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_903_ecustom--AccountsReceivableCarryingAmount_iI_uMYR_c20251130_zeJGvsdanCX3" TITLE="Accounts receivable carrying amount">45,000,000</FONT>) as collateral to obtain a
27-day loan of $<FONT ID="xdx_90E_eus-gaap--AccountsNotesAndLoansReceivableNetCurrent_iI_c20251130_zS7LJUFhcm93" TITLE="Accounts receivable loan amount">4,941,688</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_900_eus-gaap--AccountsNotesAndLoansReceivableNetCurrent_iI_uMYR_c20251130_zAza82Hy2b33" TITLE="Accounts receivable loan amount">20,000,000</FONT>). The financing bore interest at an annual rate of <FONT ID="xdx_902_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage_iI_pid_dp_c20251130_z3FWCnFJJDd" TITLE="Percentage of annual interest rate">4.6</FONT>%, and the Company incurred interest expense
of $<FONT ID="xdx_906_eus-gaap--InterestExpense_c20251130__20251130_zdib2Q7ke9ol" TITLE="Interest expense">16,347</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_903_eus-gaap--InterestExpense_uMYR_c20251130__20251130_z6GoOlDO1c91" TITLE="Interest expense">68,055</FONT>).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
loan was repaid in full upon its maturity in December 2025, and the related customer collections were received during the same period.
Accordingly, as of March 31, 2026, the Company had no outstanding accounts receivable invoice financing arrangements. For the year ended
March 31, 2026, the Company recognized $<FONT ID="xdx_908_ecustom--InterestExpenseRelatedToAccountsReceivable_c20250401__20260331_zDvwgKZE0IJb" TITLE="Interest expense related to accounts receivable">16,347</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_904_ecustom--InterestExpenseRelatedToAccountsReceivable_uMYR_c20250401__20260331_zafntKgORh7e" TITLE="Interest expense related to accounts receivable">68,055</FONT>) of interest expense related to accounts receivable invoice financing.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s accounts receivable invoice financing arrangement is accounted for as a secured borrowing. Accordingly, cash proceeds
received from the financing arrangement and repayments of principal are presented as cash flows from financing activities in the consolidated
statements of cash flows. Cash collections of the underlying trade accounts receivable are presented as operating activities, consistent
with the Company&rsquo;s normal cash receipts for accounts receivable from customers. Interest paid is included in cash flows from operating
activities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: right"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" BORDER="0" STYLE="width: 100%; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">&nbsp;</TD>
  <TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(2)</B></FONT></TD>
  <TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Accounts Payable invoice financing</B></FONT></TD></TR>
</TABLE>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Accounts
payable invoice financing is a supplier finance arrangement under which a financial institution settles eligible supplier invoices on
behalf of the Company, and the Company repays the financial institution at a later date in accordance with the agreed terms.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Beginning
in August 2025, the Company entered into an Account Payable invoice financing arrangement with a financial institution to facilitate settlement of
eligible supplier invoices. Under the arrangement, the Company may obtain financing of up to $<FONT ID="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--AccountsPayableOtherCurrentAndNoncurrent_iI_c20250831__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MaximumMember_zaE5J66IK0w2" TITLE="Accounts payable outstanding principal amount">9,883,376</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_908_eus-gaap--AccountsPayableOtherCurrentAndNoncurrent_iI_uMYR_c20250831__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MaximumMember_zeNNLvwKQQRk" TITLE="Accounts payable outstanding principal amount">40,000,000</FONT>) in outstanding
principal at any time, with individual financing terms of up to 90 days. Amounts financed bear interest at a rate of <FONT ID="xdx_902_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage_iI_pid_dp_c20250831_zVf6jzlOmki8" TITLE="Percentage of annual interest rate">1.5</FONT>% per annum above
the financial institution&rsquo;s prevailing Effective Cost of Funds. Accordingly, the effective interest rate fluctuates based on changes
in the underlying benchmark rate.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
repayment obligations under the Account Payable invoice financing facility are guaranteed by the directors of Conwall Construction Industries Sdn.
Bhd., Mr. Hu Jingji and Mr. Ng Boon Teik, up to the maximum facility amount of $<FONT ID="xdx_904_eus-gaap--LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity_iI_c20260331_zkDz3IdQBbNc" TITLE="maximum facility amount">9,883,376</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_906_eus-gaap--LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity_iI_uMYR_c20260331_zql82CE2TfH2" TITLE="maximum facility amount">40,000,000</FONT>).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: right"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" BORDER="0" STYLE="width: 100%; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">&nbsp;</TD>
  <TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(2)</B></FONT></TD>
  <TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Accounts Payable invoice financing (continued)</B></FONT></TD></TR>
</TABLE>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">From
time to time, the Company submits eligible supplier invoices to the financial institution, which pays the suppliers directly on the Company&rsquo;s
behalf. Upon payment by the financial institution, the Company&rsquo;s obligation to the supplier is satisfied and a corresponding obligation
to the financial institution is recognized. The Company subsequently repays the financial institution at maturity or earlier, together
with accrued interest and bank charges.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
repayment of the outstanding financing, the Company may submit additional eligible supplier invoices to the financial institution for
financing, provided that the aggregate outstanding financing balance does not exceed the maximum financing facility of $<FONT ID="xdx_902_eus-gaap--LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity_iI_c20260630_zDonfxXMP5T" TITLE="maximum facility amount">9,883,376</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_901_eus-gaap--LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity_iI_uMYR_c20260630_z6bv2TUwIJFl" TITLE="maximum facility amount">40,000,000</FONT>).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company accounts for the arrangement as a financing obligation. Accordingly, amounts outstanding under the arrangement are presented
separately from trade accounts payable in the consolidated balance sheets as Invoice Financing Liabilities. At the time the financial
institution settles eligible supplier invoices on the Company&rsquo;s behalf, the payments made directly to the suppliers are considered
non-cash financing activities and, accordingly, are excluded from changes in accounts payable in the consolidated statements of cash
flows. Subsequent repayments of principal to the financial institution are presented as cash flows from financing activities, while interest
paid is presented as cash flows from operating activities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
the year ended March 31, 2026, the Company recognized $<FONT ID="xdx_906_ecustom--InterestExpenseRelatedToAccountsPayable_c20250401__20260331_zVSzaZCmjn3b" TITLE="Interest expense related to accounts payable">73,967</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_907_ecustom--InterestExpenseRelatedToAccountsPayable_uMYR_c20250401__20260331_zbJublwtYjEk" TITLE="Interest expense related to accounts payable">307,932</FONT>) of interest expense related to the accounts payable invoice
financing arrangement. The effective interest rate applicable to amounts financed under the arrangements ranged from <FONT ID="xdx_905_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage_iI_pid_dp_c20260331__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MinimumMember_z7u0I2cSKzZ2" TITLE="Percentage of annual interest rate">4.60</FONT>% to <FONT ID="xdx_902_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage_iI_pid_dp_c20260331__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MaximumMember_zCQ0F0klQFy8" TITLE="Percentage of annual interest rate">4.88</FONT>% per
annum. As of March 31, 2026, the outstanding balance under the arrangement was $<FONT ID="xdx_90F_ecustom--InvoiceFinancingLiabilitiesCurrent_iI_c20260331_zPqcNPIFsC1h" TITLE="Accounts payable invoice financing outstanding balance">1,711,459</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_900_ecustom--InvoiceFinancingLiabilitiesCurrent_iI_uMYR_c20260331_zLUoAdj4CJWk" TITLE="Accounts payable invoice financing outstanding balance">6,926,617</FONT>).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_89D_ecustom--ScheduleOfChangesInAccountsPayableInvoiceFinancingTableTextBlock_zxcelEM8sK7h" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s operations are substantially carried out in Malaysia. Accordingly, the Company&rsquo;s business, financial condition

business may be influenced by changes in governmental policies with respect to laws and regulations, anti-inflationary measures, currency
conversion and remittance abroad, rates and methods of taxation among other factors.</FONT></P>

risk</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company is exposed to liquidity risk which is risk that it is unable to provide sufficient capital resources and liquidity to meet its
commitments and business needs. Liquidity risk is controlled by the application of financial position analysis and monitoring procedures.
When necessary, the Company will turn to other financial institutions and the shareholders to obtain short-term funding to meet the liquidity
shortage.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s business, financial condition and results of operations may also be negatively impacted by risks related to natural disasters,
extreme weather conditions, health epidemics and other catastrophic incidents, such as the COVID-19 outbreak and spread, which could
significantly disrupt the Company&rsquo;s operations.</FONT></P>

1- <FONT ID="xdx_82C_zh6rjVdyP5af">ORGANIZATION</FONT></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
Construction Industries Limited (the &ldquo;Company&rdquo; or &ldquo;Conwall&rdquo;) was incorporated on February 12, 2026, under the
laws of the Cayman Islands as an exempted company. Conwall was incorporated as a holding company for the purpose of acquiring operating
companies. On July 16, 2026, the Company completed the share exchange described below and became the holding company of Conwall Construction
Industries Sdn. Bhd.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
July 16, 2026, the Company entered into a Share Swap Agreement (the &ldquo;Share Swap Agreement&rdquo;) with the shareholders holding
all <FONT ID="xdx_904_eus-gaap--CommonStockSharesIssued_iI_pid_c20260716__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--ShareSwapAgreementMember__srt--StatementScenarioAxis__srt--ScenarioForecastMember_z9uH5nMiseSl" TITLE="Common stock, shares issued"><FONT ID="xdx_90D_eus-gaap--CommonStockSharesOutstanding_iI_pid_c20260716__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--ShareSwapAgreementMember__srt--StatementScenarioAxis__srt--ScenarioForecastMember_zkkHDN7CxKv2" TITLE="Common stock, shares outstanding">750,000</FONT></FONT> issued and outstanding ordinary shares of Conwall Construction Industries Sdn. Bhd. (&ldquo;Conwall Malaysia&rdquo;). Conwall
Malaysia was incorporated in Malaysia on October 8, 2019, as a private company limited by shares under the Companies Act 2016 and is
engaged in the business of providing construction and maintenance services.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Pursuant
to the Share Swap Agreement, the Company issued an aggregate of <FONT ID="xdx_90D_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues_pid_c20260716__20260716__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--ShareSwapAgreementMember__srt--StatementScenarioAxis__srt--ScenarioForecastMember_zY7PWmnjLSM4" TITLE="Number of shares issued">30,000,000</FONT> shares of its common stock to the shareholders of Conwall
Malaysia in exchange for all of the issued and outstanding ordinary shares of Conwall Malaysia. shares of its common stock to Mr. Ng Boon Teik in exchange for his <FONT ID="xdx_90D_eus-gaap--ConversionOfStockSharesIssued1_pid_c20260716__20260716__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--ShareSwapAgreementMember__srt--TitleOfIndividualAxis__custom--MrNgBoonTeikMember__srt--StatementScenarioAxis__srt--ScenarioForecastMember_zBLqIu9g7iq2" TITLE="Common stock, shares exchange">525,000</FONT> ordinary shares of Conwall Malaysia, and <FONT ID="xdx_90E_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues_pid_c20260716__20260716__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--ShareSwapAgreementMember__srt--TitleOfIndividualAxis__custom--MrHuJingjiMember__srt--StatementScenarioAxis__srt--ScenarioForecastMember_zCnhz8gTAK3d" TITLE="Nummber of shares issued">9,000,000</FONT> shares

Upon completion of the share exchange,
the Company became the sole shareholder of Conwall Malaysia.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

share exchanges have been accounted for as a recapitalization of entities under common control because the same controlling shareholders
controlled both entities before and after the transaction. Accordingly, the consolidation of the Company and its subsidiary has been
accounted for at historical cost, and the accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared as if the transaction had
occurred at the beginning of the earliest period presented.</FONT></P>

appropriate, the terms &ldquo;we,&rdquo; &ldquo;our,&rdquo; and &ldquo;us&rdquo; refer collectively to Conwall and its subsidiary.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
accompanying consolidated financial statements are presented in United States dollar (&ldquo;USD&rdquo;), which is the reporting currency
of the Company. The functional currency of Conwall is USD. The functional currency of Conwall Malaysia is Malaysian Ringgit (&ldquo;MYR&rdquo;).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company maintains the books and record in the functional currency. Transactions denominated in currencies other than the functional currency
are translated into the functional currency at the exchange rates prevailing at the dates of the transaction. The resulting exchange
differences are recorded in the statements of operations.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
reporting currency of the Company is the United States Dollars (&ldquo;USD&rdquo;), and the accompanying consolidated financial statements
have been expressed in USD. In accordance with ASC Topic 830- 30, &ldquo;Translation of Financial Statements&rdquo;, assets and liabilities
of the Company whose functional currency is not US$ are translated into USD, using the exchange rate on the balance sheet date. Revenues
and expenses are translated at average rates prevailing during the period. The gains and losses resulting from the translation of financial
statements are recorded as a separate component of accumulated other comprehensive gain (loss) within the statements of changes in shareholders&rsquo;
equity (deficit).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Note
2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_848_eus-gaap--UseOfEstimates_zogdOCyir3c2" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Use
of Estimates</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect reported
amounts. These estimates are based on information available through the date of the issuance of the financial statements. Therefore,
actual results could differ from those estimates.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84E_eus-gaap--FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy_zhWo2OTNZcU9" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Fair
Value of Financial Instruments</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company adopted ASC 820 &ldquo;Fair Value Measurements,&rdquo; which defines fair value, establishes a three-level valuation hierarchy
for disclosures of fair value measurement and enhances disclosures requirements for fair value measures. Current assets and current liabilities
qualified as financial instruments and management believes their carrying amounts are a reasonable estimate of fair value because of
the short period of time between the origination of such instruments and their expected realization and if applicable, their current
interest rate is equivalent to interest rates currently available. The three levels are defined as follow:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Level
1:</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Inputs
to the valuation methodology are quoted prices (unadjusted) for identical assets or liabilities in active markets.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Level
2:</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Inputs
to the valuation methodology include quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, and inputs that are observable
for the assets or liability, either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the financial instruments.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Level
3:</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Inputs
to the valuation methodology are unobservable and significant to the fair value.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of the balance sheet date, the estimated fair values of the financial instruments approximated their fair values due to the short-term
nature of these instruments. Determining which category an asset or liability falls within the hierarchy requires significant judgment.
The Company evaluates the hierarchy disclosures each year.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84D_eus-gaap--CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock_z6DJ57muhCV8" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Cash
and Cash Equivalents</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Cash
and cash equivalents include cash on hand and cash in time deposits, certificates of deposit and all other highly liquid instruments
with original maturities of three months or less.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_848_ecustom--RestrictedFixedDepositsPolicyTextBlock_zqlT5ZcpgHrc" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Restricted
Fixed Deposits</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Certain
customers occasionally require the Company to place fixed deposits with licensed financial institutions as security deposits to guarantee
the completion of construction projects. The Company places such fixed deposits with reputable banks for terms generally ranging from
six to twelve months. These deposits are typically withdrawn upon completion of the related construction projects or upon customer approval.
At that time, the principal and accrued interest are released to the Company and become available for working capital purposes. The Company
recognizes interest income on these fixed deposits over the term of the deposit.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>CONWALL

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>NOTES
TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">(Unaudited)</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Note
2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84B_eus-gaap--TradeAndOtherAccountsReceivablePolicy_zehJb41tbzsc" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Accounts
Receivable, net</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Accounts
receivable, net represent amounts for which the Company has an unconditional right to consideration and are stated at the invoiced amount,
net of an allowance for expected credit losses.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company evaluates the collectability of its accounts receivable on a recurring basis and maintains adequate allowance for expected credit
losses based on management&rsquo;s estimate of lifetime expected credit losses. In estimating the allowance, the Company considers historical
collection experience, the aging of receivable balances, customers&rsquo; financial condition and creditworthiness, current economic
conditions, reasonable and supportable forecasts, and other relevant factors that may affect customers&rsquo; ability to pay.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Accounts
receivable are written off against the allowance when management determines that collection is not probable. Subsequent recoveries of
amounts previously written off are recorded by reversing the allowance and reducing bad debt expense in the period received.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84B_ecustom--AdvancePaymentsPolicyTextBlock_zOKVXt0jdwDf" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Advance
Payments</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Advance
payments represent amounts paid to material suppliers and subcontractors in accordance with the terms of purchase contracts and subcontract
agreements. These payments are applied against future billings from the respective suppliers and subcontractors as materials are delivered
or services are performed.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Advance
payments are classified as current or non-current assets based on the Company&rsquo;s expectation of when the related goods or services
will be received and the advances will be applied. Amounts expected to be applied within one year after the balance sheet date are classified
as current assets, while amounts expected to be applied after one year are classified as non-current assets.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_849_ecustom--ProjectRetentionPolicyTextBlock_zVW4SE7fcNcc" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Project
Retention</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Project
retention represents the portion of the contract price withheld by customers from progress payments on completed construction projects.
These retentions serve as security for the satisfactory performance of the Company&rsquo;s contractual obligations, including any defects
or warranty claims.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Retained
amounts are generally released to the Company in accordance with the terms of the respective contracts, typically within one to two years
after project completion upon the expiry of the warranty or defect liability period. Project retentions are classified as current or
non-current, depending on the expected release date, and are stated at their original amount less any allowance for doubtful accounts,
if required.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company periodically reviews the collectability of project retentions and recognizes an allowance when there is objective evidence that
the amounts may not be fully recoverable. Write- offs and recoveries are accounted for in the same manner as accounts receivable.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_845_ecustom--RefundableInsurancePremiumPolicyTextBlock_zA9tgfRsiEt7" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Refundable
Insurance Premium</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
August 7, 2025, the Company purchased a five-year key person life insurance policy covering one of its executive officers. The policy
provides a death benefit of $<FONT ID="xdx_90D_ecustom--DeathBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_c20250807_zBVGdQOwhsG4" TITLE="Death benefit value of life insurance">370,627</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_908_ecustom--DeathBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_uMYR_c20250807_z0RrHypHnL4j" TITLE="Death benefit value of life insurance">1,500,000</FONT>) and a total and permanent disability benefit of $<FONT ID="xdx_903_ecustom--TotalAndPermanentDisabilityBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_c20250807_zbVa5kXasya8" TITLE="Total and permanent disability benefit value of life insurance">370,627</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_90E_ecustom--TotalAndPermanentDisabilityBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_uMYR_c20250807_zTvFWhgVbvG9" TITLE="Total and permanent disability benefit value of life insurance">1,500,000</FONT>) through August
6, 2030.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company paid a single premium of $<FONT ID="xdx_901_eus-gaap--PaymentsToAcquireLifeInsurancePolicies_c20250807__20250807_zFpOh1uIF4n1" TITLE="Life insurance premium paid">247,161</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_906_eus-gaap--PaymentsToAcquireLifeInsurancePolicies_uMYR_c20250807__20250807_zxbF1hTtDBWl" TITLE="Life insurance single premium paid">1,000,311</FONT>) (exclusive of applicable taxes) upon issuance of the policy. The premium was
financed through a bank loan, with the loan proceeds disbursed directly by the lending institution to the insurer, as more fully disclosed
in Note 11 &ndash; Bank Loan &ndash; Fixed Loan. <FONT ID="xdx_904_eus-gaap--LifeInsuranceCorporateOrBankOwnedAdditionalInformation_c20250807__20250807_zzAXjSmMkz8e" TITLE="Life insurance description">The policy does not provide any cash surrender value during its five-year coverage term.
Under the terms of the policy, if no death or total and permanent disability claim is made during the coverage period and the policy
remains in force through its maturity date, the insurer is contractually obligated to refund 100% of the single premium paid to the Company
upon maturity.</FONT></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Because
the policy has no cash surrender value and the premium is contractually refundable only upon maturity, the Company records the refundable
premium as a noncurrent asset in the consolidated balance sheets. The Company evaluates the recoverability of this asset at each reporting
date and records an allowance for credit losses or impairment when collection of the refundable premium is no longer considered probable.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company does not recognize the $<FONT ID="xdx_903_ecustom--TotalAndPermanentDisabilityBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_c20250807_zCz1Hj2w8WDl" TITLE="Total and permanent disability benefit value of life insurance">370,627</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_90E_ecustom--TotalAndPermanentDisabilityBenefitValueOfLifeInsurance_iI_uMYR_c20250807_ztVa6R7gRyM1" TITLE="Total and permanent disability benefit value of life insurance">1,500,000</FONT>) death benefit or total and permanent disability benefit as an asset because the
receipt of such benefits is contingent upon future insured events. Any proceeds received under the policy in excess of the carrying amount
of the refundable premium will be recognized in earnings when realized.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_849_eus-gaap--ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock_zvzPFdO4kpl4" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Impairment
of long-lived assets</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company reviews long-lived assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an
asset may not be recoverable. Recoverability of assets to be held and used is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of an asset
to the future undiscounted cash flows expected to be generated by the asset. If such assets are considered to be impaired, the impairment
recognized is measured by the amount by which the carrying amount of the assets exceeds the fair value of the assets. <FONT ID="xdx_90B_eus-gaap--ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsToBeDisposedOf_do_c20260401__20260630_zSFS4UmigwYh" TITLE="Impairment of long-lived assets"><FONT ID="xdx_908_eus-gaap--ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsToBeDisposedOf_do_c20250401__20250630_zwCNjMVelVS9" TITLE="Impairment of long-lived assets">No</FONT></FONT> impairment of
long-lived assets was recognized for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_849_eus-gaap--DepositContractsPolicy_zt5n0llRLT8a" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Project
Security Deposits</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Project
security deposits represent amounts received from subcontractors as security for the satisfactory performance of their contractual obligations.
These deposits are refundable upon the completion of the related projects and the expiration of the applicable warranty period, provided
the subcontractors have fulfilled all contractual requirements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Project
security deposits are classified as current or non-current liabilities based on the Company&rsquo;s expectation of when the related deposits
will become refundable. Deposits expected to be refunded within one year after the balance sheet date are classified as current liabilities,
while those expected to be refunded after one year are classified as non-current liabilities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_841_eus-gaap--LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock_zuS3FjO6xiW2" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Lease</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company leases are classified as operating leases in accordance with Topic 842. Under Topic 842, lessees are required to recognize the
following for all leases (with the exception of short-term leases) on the commencement date: (i) lease liability, which is a lessee&rsquo;s
obligation to make lease payments arising from a lease, measured on a discounted basis; and (ii) right-of-use asset, which is an asset
that represents the lessee&rsquo;s right to use, or control the use of, a specified asset for the lease term.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">At
the commencement date, the Company recognizes the lease liability at the present value of the lease payments not yet paid, discounted
using the interest rate implicit in the lease or, if that rate cannot be readily determined, the Company&rsquo;s incremental borrowing
rate for the same term as the underlying lease. The right-of-use asset is recognized initially at cost, which primarily comprises the
initial amount of the lease liability, plus any initial direct costs incurred, consisting mainly of brokerage commissions, less any lease
incentives received. All right-of-use assets are reviewed for impairment. <FONT ID="xdx_903_eus-gaap--OperatingLeaseImpairmentLoss_do_c20260401__20260630_z13Kpilzreea" TITLE="Impairment for right-of-use lease assets"><FONT ID="xdx_904_eus-gaap--OperatingLeaseImpairmentLoss_do_c20250401__20250630_z1XYva8keKKf" TITLE="Impairment for right-of-use lease assets">No</FONT></FONT> impairment for right-of-use lease assets incurred in the
three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_845_eus-gaap--ConcentrationRiskCreditRisk_zWCkVsnBVlw8" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Concentration
of Credit Risk</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Financial
instruments the Company holds that are subject to concentrations of credit risk are cash and accounts receivable arising from its normal
business activities. The Company maintains cash balances with high-credit-quality financial institutions that periodically exceed insured
limits. As of June 30, 2026 and 2025, substantially all of the Company&rsquo;s cash deposits were held with financial institutions in
Malaysia, and certain balances exceeded the applicable deposit insurance limits. Management regularly monitors the creditworthiness of
these institutions. The Company has not experienced any losses on such deposits and believes it is not exposed to any significant credit
risk on its cash balances.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, two customers and one customer, respectively, accounted for more than 10% of the
Company&rsquo;s total sales.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, two vendors and three vendors, respectively, accounted for more than 10% of the
Company&rsquo;s total purchases. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Note

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_847_eus-gaap--RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock_zZ5T1nkE9s1g" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Revenue
Recognition</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company adopted ASC 606 upon inception. Under ASC 606, revenue is recognized when a customer obtains control of promised goods or services,
in an amount that reflects the consideration which the entity expects to receive in exchange for those goods or services. To determine
revenue recognition for arrangements that an entity determines are within the scope of ASC 606, the Company performs the following five
steps: (i) identify the contract(s) with a customer; (ii) identify the performance obligations in the contract; (iii) determine the transaction
price; (iv) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract; and (v) recognize revenue when (or as) the
entity satisfies a performance obligation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company derives its revenue primarily from construction contracts with customers. Revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606 when
control of the promised goods or services is transferred to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration the Company expects
to receive in exchange for those goods or services.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Construction
contracts generally contain a single performance obligation because the individual services provided under the contract are not separately
identifiable and are integrated into a single combined output, which is the completed construction project.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Revenue
from construction contracts is recognized over time, as the Company&rsquo;s performance creates or enhances an asset that the customer
controls as the asset is constructed. Progress toward completion is measured using the cost-to-cost input method, under which the percentage
of completion is determined by comparing costs incurred to date with total estimated contract costs. Revenue recognized to date is calculated
by applying the percentage of completion to the total transaction price of the contract. Revenue recognized in the current period represents
the cumulative revenue recognized to date less amounts recognized in prior periods.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Costs
incurred include direct materials, direct labor, subcontractor costs, and other costs directly attributable to the contract. Management
periodically reviews and updates estimates of total contract costs. Changes in estimated costs or contract value are recognized as cumulative
catch-up adjustments to revenue in the period the estimates change.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Timing
differences between revenue recognized and amounts billed to customers result in contract assets or contract liabilities. A contract
asset is recorded when revenue recognized exceeds billings to the customer, while a contract liability is recorded when billings exceed
revenue recognized. The Company expects substantially all contract assets outstanding as of June 30, 2026 to be billed and collected
within one year. The Company also expects substantially all contract liabilities outstanding as of June 30, 2026 to be recognized as
revenue within one year.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">If
at any time the estimated total costs of a contract exceed the transaction price, the Company recognizes the entire estimated loss immediately
in the period in which the loss becomes probable.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Note

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Revenue
Recognition (continued)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
certain sundry construction projects with a total contract price of less than $<FONT ID="xdx_905_eus-gaap--ConstructionPayableCurrent_iI_c20260630_zu4VglCbLc38" TITLE="Contract price">24,020</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_903_eus-gaap--ConstructionPayableCurrent_iI_uMYR_c20260630_zsgjUyV8jzie" TITLE="Contract price">100,000</FONT>) or an expected duration of less than
<FONT ID="xdx_903_eus-gaap--ConstructionContractorContractDuration_dc_c20260401__20260630__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MaximumMember_za0iDJYOb2Wg" TITLE="Contract duration">three months</FONT>, the Company does not apply the cost-to-cost input method to measure progress toward completion. Due to the short-term nature
and immaterial size of these contracts, revenue is recognized by matching revenue with the related costs incurred within the same reporting
period. Management has concluded that this approach does not result in a material difference from the revenue that would have been recognized
using the cost-to-cost input method.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company generally provides limited warranties for work performed under its contracts. These warranties are assurance-type warranties
that provide customers with assurance that the completed work complies with agreed-upon specifications and do not represent separate
performance obligations. Historically, warranty claims have not resulted in material costs incurred. Any estimated warranty costs are
included in the individual project cost estimates used in accounting for long-term contracts.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_845_ecustom--ProjectEstimatesPolicyTextBlock_zjLdkBUNjvI" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Project
Estimates</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Due
to the nature of our industry, there is significant complexity in our estimation of total expected revenue and cost, for which we must
make significant judgments. Our contracts with our customers may contain several types of variable consideration, including claims, unpriced
change orders, award and incentive fees, liquidated damages and penalties or other provisions that can either increase or decrease the
contract price to arrive at estimated revenue. Certain variable consideration, such as award and incentive fees, generally are earned
upon achievement of certain performance metrics, program milestones or cost targets and can be based upon customer discretion. We estimate
variable consideration at the most likely amount to which we expect to be entitled upon completion of a project. We include estimated
amounts in the transaction price to the extent it is probable we will realize that amount. Our estimates of variable consideration and
our determination of its inclusion in project revenue are based on an assessment of our anticipated performance and other information
that may be available to us.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">At
a project level, we have specific practices and procedures to review our estimate of total revenue and cost. Each project team reviews
the progress and execution of our performance obligations, which impact the project&rsquo;s accounting outcome. As part of this process,
the project team reviews information such as any outstanding key contract matters, progress towards completion and the related program
schedule and identified risks and opportunities. The accuracy of our revenue and profit recognition in a given period depends on the
accuracy of our project estimates, which can change from period to period due to a variety of factors including:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

  <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">&#9679;</TD>
  <TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our ability to recover for additional contract costs.</FONT></TD></TR>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
recognize changes in contract estimates on a cumulative catch-up basis in the period in which the changes are identified. Such changes
in contract estimates can result in the recognition of revenue in a current period for performance obligations which were satisfied or
partially satisfied in prior periods. Changes in contract estimates may also result in the reversal of previously recognized revenue
if the current estimate adversely differs from the previous estimate.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_848_eus-gaap--RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationProvisionForLossPolicyTextBlock_zSu2CRslhl5g" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Remaining
Performance Obligations</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s remaining performance obligations as of June 30, 2026 represent a measure of the total dollar value of work to be performed
on contracts awarded and in progress. The Company had approximately $<FONT ID="xdx_902_eus-gaap--RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation_iI_c20260630_z67DRdVIq083" TITLE="Remaining performance obligations">7,605,215</FONT> in remaining performance obligations as of June 30, 2026.
<FONT ID="xdx_907_eus-gaap--RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationExpectedTimingOfSatisfactionExplanation_c20260401__20260630_zC6rwv5t1CZ3" TITLE="Remaining performance obligations description">The Company expects to recognize 100% of our remaining performance obligations within the next twelve months.</FONT></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Although
remaining performance obligations reflect business that is considered to be firm, cancellations, scope adjustments, foreign currency
exchange fluctuations or project deferrals may occur that impact their volume or the expected timing of their recognition. Remaining
performance obligations are adjusted to reflect any known project.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_849_eus-gaap--ComprehensiveIncomePolicyPolicyTextBlock_zl5xAtbHjtF3" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Comprehensive
Income (Loss)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">ASC
220 &ldquo;Comprehensive Income&rdquo; established standards for reporting and display of comprehensive income/loss, its components and
accumulated balances. Components of comprehensive income/loss include net income/loss and foreign currency translation adjustments. The
component of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) consisted of foreign currency translation adjustments.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84F_eus-gaap--EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock_z3HdnUxpilr7" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Earnings
per share</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Basic
earnings per ordinary share is computed by dividing net earnings attributable to ordinary shareholders by the weighted-average number
of ordinary shares outstanding during the period. Diluted earnings per ordinary share is computed by dividing net income attributable
to ordinary shareholders by the sum of the weighted-average number of ordinary shares outstanding and potential ordinary
shares, such as convertible securities, options and warrants, as if they had been converted at the beginning of the periods
presented or on the issuance date, if later. Potential ordinary shares that have an anti-dilutive effect, meaning those
that increase income per share or decrease loss per share, are excluded from the calculation of diluted earnings per share. For
the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company had no dilutive securities. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84A_eus-gaap--SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock_zknCNtne3zk8" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Segment
Reporting</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">ASC
280, &ldquo;Segment Reporting,&rdquo; requires use of the &ldquo;management approach&rdquo; model for segment reporting. The management
approach model is based on the way a company&rsquo;s chief operating decision maker organizes segments within the Company for making
operating decisions assessing performance and allocating resources. Reportable segments are based on products and services, geography,
legal structure, management structure, or any other manner in which management disaggregates a company.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Management
determined the Company&rsquo;s operations constitute <FONT ID="xdx_909_eus-gaap--NumberOfReportableSegments_pid_dc_uSegment_c20260401__20260630_zwE9VyBKkNoj" TITLE="Number of reportable segment">one</FONT> reportable segment in accordance with ASC 280, construction and maintenance
services.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
