<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_845_eus-gaap--IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock_zksRfBbuVaYe" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Income
Taxes</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company accounts for current income taxes in accordance with the laws of the relevant tax authorities. Deferred income taxes are recognized
when temporary differences exist between the tax bases of assets and liabilities and their reported amounts in the consolidated financial
statements. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years
in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a
change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period including the enactment date. Valuation allowances are established, when necessary,
to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount expected to be realized.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">An
uncertain tax position is recognized only if it is &ldquo;more likely than not&rdquo; that the tax position would be sustained in a tax
examination. The amount recognized is the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than 50% likely of being realized on examination.
For tax positions not meeting the &ldquo;more likely than not&rdquo; test, no tax benefit is recorded. Penalties and interest incurred
related to underpayment of income tax are classified as income tax expense in the period incurred.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company accounts for income taxes in interim periods in accordance with FASB ASC 740-270, &ldquo;Interim Reporting.&rdquo; The Company
has determined an estimated annual effective tax rate. The rate will be revised, if necessary, as of the end of each successive interim
period during the Company&rsquo;s fiscal year to its best current estimate. The estimated annual effective tax rate is applied to the
year- to-date ordinary income (or loss) at the end of the interim period.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(1)
Income tax of Cayman Islands</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
was incorporated in the Cayman Islands as an exempted company and is governed by the tax laws of the Cayman Islands. Under the current
laws of the Cayman Islands, Conwall is not subject to income taxes or capital gains taxes. In addition, upon payment of dividends by
Conwall to its shareholders, no Cayman Islands withholding tax will be imposed.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(2)
Income tax of Malaysia</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
Malaysia was incorporated in Malaysia, and accordingly are governed by the income tax laws of Malaysia. The income tax provision in respect
of operations in Malaysia is calculated at the applicable tax rates on the taxable income for the periods based on existing legislation,
interpretations, and practices. Under the Income Tax Act of Malaysia, enterprises incorporated in Malaysia are usually subject to a unified
<FONT ID="xdx_908_ecustom--EnterpriseIncomeTaxRate_pid_dp_c20260401__20260630__srt--StatementGeographicalAxis__country--MY_zu5vQAl6VDS9" TITLE="Enterprise income tax rate">24</FONT>% enterprise income tax rate while prefer, tax holidays, and tax exemptions may be granted on a case-by-case basis. <FONT ID="xdx_901_ecustom--EnterpriseIncomeTaxRateDescription_c20260401__20260630__srt--StatementGeographicalAxis__country--MY_zITo1Ujd86Hh" TITLE="Enterprise income tax rate description">The tax rate for
small and medium sized companies (generally companies incorporated in Malaysia with paid-in capital of $617,711 (RM2,500,000) or less,
and gross income of not more than $12,010,280 (RM50,000,000) is 15% on the first $36,030 (RM150,000) of taxable income and 17% on taxable
income from $36,031 (RM150,001) to $144,123 (RM600,000), with any remaining taxable income taxed at the standard rate of 24%.</FONT></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
local tax authority conducts periodic and ad hoc tax filing reviews on business enterprises after those enterprises complete their relevant
tax filings. Therefore, the Company&rsquo;s tax filings are subject to examination. It is therefore uncertain as to whether the local
tax authority may take different views about the Company&rsquo;s tax filings, which may lead to additional tax liabilities. As of June
30, 2026 and 2025, all of the Company&rsquo;s tax returns remain open for statutory examination by relevant tax authorities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(2)
Income tax of Malaysia (continued)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conwall
Malaysia evaluates its uncertain tax positions in accordance with applicable accounting guidance. The Company recognizes interest and
penalties related to uncertain tax positions, if any, as a component of income tax expense. As of June 30, 2026, the Company did not
have any significant uncertain tax positions requiring recognition or disclosure in the accompanying consolidated financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84D_ecustom--ServiceTaxesPolicyTextBlock_zc91tx7Eer7h" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Service
taxes</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Service
tax is a consumption tax levied by Malaysian tax authorities and is charged on any taxable service income provided in Malaysia by a registered
company in carrying on their business. Conwall Malaysia is engaged in the business of construction services, which became subject to
certain construction-related service tax on July 1, 2025. Conwall registered with the local tax authorities in August 2025 and commenced
filing service tax returns and remitting service tax beginning in September 2025.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
construction-related services, the applicable service tax rates are <FONT ID="xdx_903_ecustom--ServiceTaxRatesForConstructionWork_iI_pid_dp_c20260630_zpFs4l1zF9Fe" TITLE="Service tax rates for construction work">6</FONT>% ad valorem for construction work and <FONT ID="xdx_904_ecustom--ServiceTaxRatesForMaintenanceOrRepairWork_iI_pid_dp_c20260630_zKHw1ve7Agbj" TITLE="Service tax rates for maintenance or repair work">8</FONT>% ad valorem for maintenance
or repair work. A company is required to register for service tax purposes if the total value of its taxable services over a rolling
12-month period exceeds, or is expected to exceed, the prescribed registration threshold of $<FONT ID="xdx_90D_ecustom--TaxableServicesRegistrationThresholdValue_iI_c20260630_zhZS6HX5oxS8" TITLE="Taxable services registration threshold value">370,627</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_90F_ecustom--TaxableServicesRegistrationThresholdValue_iI_uMYR_c20260630_z1JoE7JFbFxg" TITLE="Taxable services registration threshold value">1,500,000</FONT>) for construction service
providers.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Service
tax collected is not an expense of the Company and is recorded as a liability until remitted to the Malaysian tax authorities. The Company
presents revenue net of service tax collected.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_842_ecustom--PayrollTaxesAndStatutoryContributionsPolicyTextBlock_zDQUFlrpVgN" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Payroll
Taxes and Statutory Contributions</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Under
Malaysian income tax regulations, employers are required to withhold employee income taxes under the Monthly Tax Deduction (&ldquo;MTD&rdquo;),
also known as Potongan Cukai Bulanan (&ldquo;PCB&rdquo;), system administered by the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia. The Company withholds
the required amounts from employees&rsquo; salaries and remits them to the Malaysian tax authorities on a monthly basis. As the Company
acts solely as a withholding agent, amounts withheld from employees&rsquo; compensation are not recognized as an expense of the Company
and are recorded as payroll tax payable until remitted.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
addition to employee income tax withholdings, the Company is required to make statutory employer contributions to employee benefit programs,
including the Employees Provident Fund (&ldquo;EPF&rdquo;), the Social Security Organization (&ldquo;SOCSO&rdquo;), the Employment Insurance
System (&ldquo;EIS&rdquo;), and, where applicable, the Human Resource Development Corporation (&ldquo;HRD Corp&rdquo;). Employer contributions
are recognized as employee benefit expense in the period in which the related services are rendered. Amounts due but not yet remitted
are included in accrued payroll-related liabilities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Note
2- SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Payroll
Taxes and Statutory Contributions (continued)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">HRD
Corp administers Malaysia&rsquo;s Human Resources Development Fund, which is financed through a statutory levy paid by eligible employers.
Employers subject to the levy may apply for grants or reimbursements for qualifying employee training and workforce development programs.
Levies paid to HRD Corp are recognized as employee benefit expense, while reimbursements received for approved training programs are
recognized as a reduction of the related training expense or as other operating income, as appropriate, when realization is probable.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_847_ecustom--RelatedPartiesTransactionsPolicyTextBlock_zs0QsRNKwZt2" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Related
Parties Transactions</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company identifies related parties, and accounts for, discloses related party transactions in accordance with ASC 850, &ldquo;Related
Party Disclosures&rdquo; and other relevant ASC standards.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">A
related party is generally defined as (i) any person that holds 10% or more of the Company&rsquo;s securities and their immediate families,
(ii) the Company&rsquo;s management, (iii) someone that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by or is under common control
with the Company, or (iv) anyone who can significantly influence the financial and operating decisions of the Company. A transaction
is considered as a related party transaction when there is a transfer of resources or obligations between related parties. Related parties
may be individuals or corporate entities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Transactions
involving related parties cannot be presumed to be carried out on an arm&rsquo;s-length basis, as the requisite conditions of competitive,
free market dealings may not exist. Representations about transactions with related parties, if made, shall not imply that the related
party transactions were consummated on terms equivalent to those that prevail in arm&rsquo;s-length transactions unless such representations
can be substantiated. It is not, however, practical to determine the fair value of amounts of related party transactions due to their
related party nature.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_84B_eus-gaap--NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock_zjYfbrIPBaOk" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Recently
Issued Accounting Pronouncements</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
November 2024, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (&ldquo;ASU&rdquo;) No. 2024-03, Income Statement &ndash; Reporting Comprehensive
Income &ndash; Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220- 40): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses, requiring public companies
to disclose additional information about specific expense categories in the notes to the consolidated financial statements on an annual
and interim basis. ASU No. 2024-03 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2026, and for interim periods beginning
after December 15, 2027. Early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of this ASU on its unaudited consolidated
financial statements and related disclosures.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
December 2025, the FASB issued ASU No. 2025-11, Interim Reporting (Topic 270): Narrow- Scope Improvements, which clarifies the guidance
in Topic 270 to improve the consistency of interim financial reporting. The ASU provides a comprehensive list of required interim disclosures
and introduces a disclosure principle requiring entities to disclose events since the end of the last annual reporting period that have
a material impact on the entity. ASU No. 2025-11 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2027, including interim periods
within those fiscal years, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of this ASU on its unaudited
interim consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.</FONT></P>

<P ID="xdx_859_zpeOb7OxGjw8" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

These leases have lease terms ranging from <FONT ID="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract_iI_dtY_c20260630__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MinimumMember_zfFC8eBIhHRc" TITLE="Lease term" STYLE="display: none">2</FONT> two
to <FONT ID="xdx_90A_eus-gaap--LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract_iI_dc_c20260630__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MaximumMember_z50XlRpnLIOi" TITLE="Lease term">four years</FONT>. The Company has elected to not recognize lease assets and liabilities for leases with a term less than twelve months.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Operating lease right-of-use assets and corresponding liabilities are recognized at commencement date based on the present value of lease
payments over the lease term. The discount rate used to calculate present value is incremental borrowing rate or, if available, the rate
implicit in the lease. The Company determines the incremental borrowing rates for these leases based primarily on lease terms were <FONT ID="xdx_90B_eus-gaap--OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageDiscountRatePercent_iI_pid_dp_c20260630_zia1MwseiNvd" TITLE="Lease incremental borrowing rates">6</FONT>%.</FONT></P>

Accounts Receivable Invoice Financing</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Accounts
receivable invoice financing is an arrangement under which the Company pledges eligible trade receivables as collateral to obtain short-term
financing from financial institutions prior to the collection of the underlying receivables. The financial institutions generally deduct
the applicable interest and bank fees from the financing proceeds and deposit the net proceeds into the Company&rsquo;s bank account.
On the maturity date, the Company is required to repay the full amount of the financing to the financial institutions. If the Company
repays the financing before the maturity date, the financial institution generally does not refund any interest deducted from the financing
proceeds at inception.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company retains ownership of the underlying receivables and continues to recognize such receivables in its consolidated balance sheets.
Accordingly, the arrangement is accounted for as a secured borrowing. Cash proceeds received from the financing arrangement and repayments
of principal are presented as cash flows from financing activities in the consolidated statements of cash flows. Cash collections of
the underlying trade accounts receivable are presented as operating activities, consistent with the Company&rsquo;s normal cash receipts
for accounts receivable from customers. Interest paid is included in cash flows from operating activities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
May 2026, the Company pledged accounts receivable with a carrying amount of $<FONT ID="xdx_900_ecustom--AccountsReceivableCarryingAmount_iI_c20260531_zzzNd9rr2VGc" TITLE="Accounts receivable carrying amount">5,433,214</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_90E_ecustom--AccountsReceivableCarryingAmount_iI_uMYR_c20260531_zhWiSd2orNH1" TITLE="Accounts receivable carrying amount">22,178,380</FONT>) as collateral for a short-term
financing of $<FONT ID="xdx_90F_eus-gaap--AccountsNotesAndLoansReceivableNetCurrent_iI_c20260531_zvbhnowI2BKi" TITLE="Accounts receivable loan amount">3,753,566</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_904_eus-gaap--AccountsNotesAndLoansReceivableNetCurrent_iI_uMYR_c20260531_zv9NBBJuENL2" TITLE="Accounts receivable loan amount">15,000,000</FONT>), which had an original maturity of 78 days and bore interest at an annual rate of <FONT ID="xdx_904_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage_iI_pid_dp_c20260531_zjNPi1OVY7u4" TITLE="Percentage of annual interest rate">4.95</FONT>%. The lender
deducted interest of $<FONT ID="xdx_90A_ecustom--DeductedInterest_iI_c20260531_zd4zjbZ6jpO9" TITLE="Deducted interest">39,705</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_903_ecustom--DeductedInterest_iI_uMYR_c20260531_zrdicgDYnng3" TITLE="Deducted interest">158,671</FONT>) from the financing proceeds at inception. The Company fully repaid the financing on July 2,
2026, as more fully disclosed in Note 15 Subsequent Events. The lender did not refund any portion of the interest deducted from the financing
proceeds upon early repayment.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
related customer collections were received in June 2026. As of June 30, 2026, the outstanding accounts receivable invoice financing arrangements
were $<FONT ID="xdx_90F_eus-gaap--IncreaseDecreaseInAccountsReceivableAndOtherOperatingAssets_c20260401__20260630_zse6pajXyBzk">3,674,669</FONT></FONT>
<FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">(RM<FONT ID="xdx_90E_eus-gaap--IncreaseDecreaseInAccountsReceivableAndOtherOperatingAssets_uMYR_c20260401__20260630_z0naR7Tjyfu2">15,000,000</FONT></FONT> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">),</FONT> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">
which was included in Invoice Financing Liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets and subsequently paid off on July 2, 2026,
as more fully disclosed in Note 15, Subsequent Events. For the three months ended June 30, 2026, the Company recognized interest
expense of $<FONT ID="xdx_90B_ecustom--InterestExpenseRelatedToAccountsReceivable_c20260401__20260630_zRxom2aqK7r9">19,344</FONT></FONT>
<FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">(RM<FONT ID="xdx_90E_ecustom--InterestExpenseRelatedToAccountsReceivable_uMYR_c20260401__20260630_zhdhXpcnDip7">77,301</FONT></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">)
related to accounts receivable invoice financing.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(2)
Accounts Payable invoice financing</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Accounts
payable invoice financing is a supplier finance arrangement under which a financial institution settles eligible supplier invoices on
behalf of the Company, and the Company repays the financial institution at a later date in accordance with the agreed terms.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Beginning
in August 2025, the Company entered into an AP invoice financing arrangement with a financial institution to facilitate settlement of
eligible supplier invoices. Under the arrangement, the Company may obtain financing of up to $<FONT ID="xdx_90F_eus-gaap--AccountsPayableOtherCurrentAndNoncurrent_iI_c20250831_zUePkqPpIcwk" TITLE="Accounts payable outstanding principal amount">9,883,376</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_90F_eus-gaap--AccountsPayableOtherCurrentAndNoncurrent_iI_uMYR_c20250831_zqU8gAZAdhtb" TITLE="Accounts payable outstanding principal amount">40,000,000</FONT>) in outstanding
principal at any time, with individual financing terms of up to 90 days. Amounts financed bear interest at a rate of <FONT ID="xdx_900_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage_iI_pid_dp_c20250831_zr7kcsYdql06" TITLE="Percentage of annual interest rate">1.5</FONT>% per annum above
the financial institution&rsquo;s prevailing Effective Cost of Funds. Accordingly, the effective interest rate fluctuates based on changes
in the underlying benchmark rate.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Note
9- INVOICE FINANCING LIABILITIES (continued)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(2)
Accounts Payable invoice financing (continued)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
repayment obligations under the AP invoice financing facility are guaranteed by the directors of Conwall Construction Industries Sdn.
Bhd., Mr. Hu Jingji and Mr. Ng Boon Teik, up to the maximum facility amount of $<FONT ID="xdx_904_eus-gaap--LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity_iI_c20260630_z0BbEAIQ1gu4" TITLE="maximum facility amount">9,883,376</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_900_eus-gaap--LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity_iI_uMYR_c20260630_zwVZX4UhaCTd" TITLE="maximum facility amount">40,000,000</FONT>).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">From
time to time, the Company submits eligible supplier invoices to the financial institution, which pays the suppliers directly on the Company&rsquo;s
behalf. Upon payment by the financial institution, the Company&rsquo;s obligation to the supplier is satisfied and a corresponding obligation
to the financial institution is recognized. The Company subsequently repays the financial institution at maturity or earlier, together
with accrued interest and bank charges.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Upon
repayment of the outstanding financing, the Company may submit additional eligible supplier invoices to the financial institution for
financing, provided that the aggregate outstanding financing balance does not exceed the maximum financing facility of $<FONT ID="xdx_90A_eus-gaap--LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity_iI_c20260630_znzLchvPP4ak" TITLE="maximum facility amount">9,883,376</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_901_eus-gaap--LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity_iI_uMYR_c20260630_zKq0lg66JIae" TITLE="maximum facility amount">40,000,000</FONT>).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company accounts for the arrangement as a financing obligation. Accordingly, amounts outstanding under the arrangement are presented
separately from trade accounts payable in the consolidated balance sheets as Invoice Financing Liabilities. At the time the financial
institution settles eligible supplier invoices on the Company&rsquo;s behalf, the payments made directly to the suppliers are considered
non-cash financing activities and, accordingly, are excluded from changes in accounts payable in the consolidated statements of cash
flows. Subsequent repayments of principal to the financial institution are presented as cash flows from financing activities, while interest
paid is presented as cash flows from operating activities.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
the three months ended June 30, 2026, the Company recognized interest expenses of $<FONT ID="xdx_90B_ecustom--InterestExpenseRelatedToAccountsPayable_c20260401__20260630_zeFORVTwPS5l" TITLE="Interest expense related to accounts payable">19,302</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_907_ecustom--InterestExpenseRelatedToAccountsPayable_uMYR_c20260401__20260630_zTgEyWMg0zxi" TITLE="Interest expense related to accounts payable">77,137</FONT>) related to the accounts payable
invoice financing arrangement. <FONT ID="xdx_907_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage_iI_pid_dp_c20260630__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MaximumMember_zy5pEzqkVgKb" TITLE="Percentage of annual interest rate">5.05</FONT>% per annum. <P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
August 2025, the Company had a Multi-Option Loan (&ldquo;MOL&rdquo;) facility with a financial institution providing a maximum principal
amount of $<FONT ID="xdx_904_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentFaceAmount_iI_c20250831__us-gaap--DebtInstrumentAxis__custom--MultiOptionLoanMember__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MaximumMember_zVORbQkYbe2g">6,385,069</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_908_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentFaceAmount_iI_uMYR_c20250831__us-gaap--DebtInstrumentAxis__custom--MultiOptionLoanMember__srt--RangeAxis__srt--MaximumMember_z5JPuqYFmjOa" TITLE="Principal amount">26,600,000</FONT>) to finance the acquisition of the manufacturing facility, as more fully described in Note 4 &ndash;
Property, Plant and Equipment. The loan proceeds would be disbursed directly by the lending institution to the seller. In October 2025,
the Company drew $<FONT ID="xdx_904_eus-gaap--ProceedsFromLoanOriginations1_c20251001__20251031__us-gaap--DebtInstrumentAxis__custom--MultiOptionLoanMember__us-gaap--PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis__us-gaap--ManufacturingFacilityMember_zttajZRJ18Wl">5,164,064</FONT> (RM<FONT ID="xdx_903_eus-gaap--ProceedsFromLoanOriginations1_uMYR_c20251001__20251031__us-gaap--DebtInstrumentAxis__custom--MultiOptionLoanMember__us-gaap--PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis__us-gaap--ManufacturingFacilityMember_zu5VWdTRRM3l">20,900,000</FONT>) under the facility to fund a portion of the purchase price of the manufacturing facility.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

Cost of Funds, with interest calculated on monthly rests. Accordingly, the interest rate fluctuates with changes in the underlying benchmark
rate.</FONT></P>

of principal and accrued interest, followed by payment of the remaining outstanding principal together with any accrued interest in the

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

14- <FONT ID="xdx_82B_ziKEmsZ1H8jl">CONTINGENCIES, RISKS AND UNCERTAINTIES</FONT></B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Foreign
operation</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s operations are substantially carried out in Malaysia. Accordingly, the Company&rsquo;s business, financial condition
and results of operations may be influenced by the political, economic and legal environments therein. In addition, the Company&rsquo;s
business may be influenced by changes in governmental policies with respect to laws and regulations, anti-inflationary measures, currency
conversion and remittance abroad, rates and methods of taxation among other factors.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Liquidity
risk</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company is exposed to liquidity risk which is risk that it is unable to provide sufficient capital resources and liquidity to meet its
commitments and business needs. Liquidity risk is controlled by the application of financial position analysis and monitoring procedures.
When necessary, the Company will turn to other financial institutions and the shareholders to obtain short-term funding to meet the liquidity
shortage.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Other
risk</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company&rsquo;s business, financial condition and results of operations may also be negatively impacted by risks related to natural disasters,
extreme weather conditions, health epidemics and other catastrophic incidents, such as the COVID-19 outbreak and spread, which could
significantly disrupt the Company&rsquo;s operations.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_038"></A>Unaudited

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><I>&nbsp;</I></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><I>Defined
terms included below have the same meanings as terms defined and included elsewhere in this registration statement.</I></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_039"></A>Introduction,
Transaction Description and Basis of Presentation</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
following unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial information presents the combination of the historical financial information
of Conwall Construction Industries Limited and its consolidated subsidiaries (collectively, &ldquo;Conwall&rdquo; or the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;)
and Broad Capital Acquisition Corp. (&ldquo;BRAC&rdquo;), after giving effect to the Reorganization, the BRAC Merger and the related
transactions contemplated by the Business Combination Agreement (collectively, the &ldquo;Business Combination&rdquo;). Following Closing,
Holdco will be the parent of CCISB and BRAC and is referred to in this section as the &ldquo;Combined Company,&rdquo; subject
to the listing conditions and other qualifications described herein. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial information has been prepared in accordance with Article 11 of Regulation S-X, as amended.
It reflects the application of transaction accounting adjustments that are necessary to depict the accounting for the Business Combination.
The Combined Company has elected not to present Management&rsquo;s Adjustments, including projected synergies, cost savings, integration
effects or other forward-looking operating adjustments.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Description
of the Business Combination</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Pursuant
to the Business Combination Agreement, the Business Combination is being effected through a two-step process. First, on July 16, 2026,
the share-swap Reorganization made CCISB a wholly owned subsidiary of Holdco. At the Closing, following the completed
Reorganization, Conwall DE Sub Inc., a Delaware corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of Holdco (&ldquo;Merger Sub&rdquo;),
will merge with and into BRAC, with BRAC surviving the merger as a wholly owned subsidiary of Holdco.</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">At
the BRAC Merger Effective Time, each issued and outstanding share of BRAC Common Stock that is not redeemed or otherwise cancelled will
be converted into the right to receive one newly issued Holdco Ordinary Share. In addition, every ten BRAC Rights issued and outstanding
immediately prior to the BRAC Merger Effective Time will be cancelled and converted into one newly issued Holdco Ordinary Share. The
fixed existing Conwall equity-holder block is 24,670,924 shares. For the other Closing issuances, 2,910,897 Holdco Ordinary Shares are
expected to be received by the BRAC Sponsor and 80,000 by BRAC&rsquo;s four independent directors, up to 6,969 Holdco Ordinary Shares
are expected to be received by BRAC public shareholders that do not redeem, and 1,061,020 Holdco Ordinary Shares are expected to be issued
upon conversion of the BRAC Rights. In addition, the actual Loan Conversion Shares and all underwriting settlement and other shares then
outstanding are included in Closing capitalization. Completed Company-share issuances are credited without duplication.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Under
the Business Combination Agreement, as amended, the Company Reorganization Consideration is the fixed net block of 24,670,924 Holdco
Ordinary Shares allocated among Ng Boon Teik, Jingji Hu, ENSP Limited, HK Xingfu Capital Holding Limited and Haibiao Deng in Schedule
A to the Business Combination Agreement, after giving effect once to the cancellation of 5,329,076 of the original 30,000,000 shares
and the identified transfers. Completed issuances, transfers and cancellations are credited in full and will not be repeated. The retained
Company Equity Value definition does not recalculate this fixed block. The Payment Spreadsheet reflects its allocation, and the
final closing capitalization schedule separately reflects the other Closing issuances. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Accounting
Treatment of the Business Combination</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Business Combination is expected to be accounted for as a capital reorganization, with Conwall treated as the accounting acquirer and
BRAC treated as the accounting acquiree. BRAC is a special purpose acquisition company and does not meet the definition of a business
for purposes of the expected accounting treatment. Accordingly, the Business Combination is expected to be treated as a reverse recapitalization
rather than as a business combination accounted for under the acquisition method. No goodwill or other intangible assets are expected
to be recognized as a result of the BRAC Merger.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Under
this accounting treatment, the historical financial statements of Conwall are treated as the historical financial statements of the Combined
Company. The net assets and liabilities of BRAC are combined with those of Conwall at historical carrying amounts, subject to the transaction
accounting adjustments described below, and the equity structure is recast to reflect the legal capital structure of Holdco following
the Closing.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Basis
of Pro Forma Presentation</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
unaudited pro forma condensed combined balance sheet combines the historical balance sheets of Conwall and BRAC as of June 30, 2026 and
gives effect to the Business Combination and the other transactions described in the accompanying notes as if they had occurred on June
30, 2026. The unaudited pro forma condensed combined statements of operations and comprehensive income for the year ended March 31, 2026
and the three months ended June 30, 2026 give effect to those transactions as if they had occurred on April 1, 2025. BRAC&rsquo;s historical
results for the year ended March 31, 2026 are derived from its year ended December 31, 2025, plus the three months ended March 31, 2026,
less the three months ended March 31, 2025. The June quarterly pro forma statement uses BRAC&rsquo;s results for the three months ended
June 30, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
historical financial statements of both Conwall and BRAC are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in
the United States of America (&ldquo;U.S. GAAP&rdquo;). Accordingly, no accounting-framework conversion adjustment is reflected. Certain
historical captions have been reclassified solely to conform presentation; such reclassifications do not affect historical total assets,
total liabilities, shareholders&rsquo; equity or net income.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial information is presented for illustrative purposes only and is not necessarily indicative
of the financial position or results of operations that would have been achieved had the Business Combination occurred on the dates indicated,
nor is it indicative of the future financial position or results of operations of the Combined Company. The pro forma adjustments are
based on information currently available and on assumptions that management believes are reasonable and factually supportable. The pro
forma financial information will require updating if the final financing, loan settlement, transaction expense or other Closing arrangements
differ materially from the assumptions described herein.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

of the date of this registration statement, the parties have not entered into any definitive PIPE investment or other third-party financing
agreement. Accordingly, the unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial information does not give effect to any uncommitted PIPE
or other financing. Although Section 6.11 of the Business Combination Agreement contemplates that the Company will use commercially reasonable
efforts to arrange financing of approximately $3.0 million to $5.0 million, the parties have acknowledged that such financing is a non-binding
target and that neither the consummation of such financing nor the receipt of any minimum amount of financing proceeds is a condition
to the Closing unless added pursuant to a written amendment to the Business Combination Agreement executed by BRAC, the Company
and Holdco. The Business Combination Agreement also permits the Conwall Companies to receive up to $10.0 million in aggregate
proceeds from the sale of Conwall Company Interests during the Interim Period as the Post-Signing Investment Amount, subject to the terms
of the Business Combination Agreement. No such financing proceeds are reflected in the unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial
information unless and until the applicable financing becomes factually supportable.</FONT></P>

of affiliated and unaffiliated lenders. The amended Business Combination Agreement requires conversion at Closing of the entire actual
Covered Loan Amount, including contractually convertible interest and subsequent permitted advances, net of repayments,
credits and effective waivers. No Loan Conversion Agreements have been executed; creditor-specific prices and fractional-share terms
will be set before Closing. The assumed $10 price and 564,078 shares are illustrative. The amended agreement provides
no $1.5 million conversion cap or election to receive cash, BRAC Units or BRAC Rights; existing rights convert separately.
See note (j) for the accounting, reported interest elimination and unfinalized Closing schedule. </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"> BRAC&rsquo;s historical $3,555,674 deferred
underwriting obligation is reduced in the preliminary model to the $1,500,000 contractual settlement, with a $2,055,674 credit
to additional paid-in capital. Settlement is in Holdco shares at the higher of $0.50 and ten times the contractual
recent average BRAC Rights price, subject to the 9.9% cap and return of unsold excess shares after the
$1,500,000 net-proceeds limit is reached. The 3,000,000-share illustration uses the floor price before application
of the cap; it is not a fixed award or part of Covered Loan conversion. The model retains a $1,500,000 liability and excludes
those shares from preliminary EPS pending classification and returnability analysis. All legally outstanding settlement shares
are included in the legal capitalization illustration. See note (c) for the full settlement terms and the incomplete
accounting, and &ldquo;Incomplete transaction accounting and sensitivities&rdquo; below for its potential magnitude. </P>

for the $60,000 of BRAC costs paid by Conwall. Classification and measurement may affect settlement liabilities, additional paid-in capital
or earnings. Cost allocation may affect expenses, equity issuance costs or liability instruments, and intercompany reconciliation may
affect receivables, payables and equity. The affected face statements, adjustment notes, capitalization and per-share data must be updated
together. No final Closing date or more specific accounting-completion date is provided. Finalization depends on obtaining and reviewing

fall by the stated amount, and a cash-paid cost would also reduce cash by $1,000,000. No reasonable range of additional transaction costs
is supplied because invoices, estimates and allocation information are incomplete. The existing $60,000 is separately subject to intercompany
reconciliation and is not added again as a new expense.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>No
Minimum Cash or Net Tangible Assets Closing Condition</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Business Combination Agreement does not require Holdco, the Company or BRAC to satisfy any minimum cash or minimum net tangible assets
threshold as a condition to Closing. Any independently applicable charter limitation, including the Section 9.2(a) net-tangible-asset
restriction unless validly removed, must separately be satisfied or amended. Accordingly, the Minimum Redemption Scenario and Maximum
Redemption Scenario presented in this unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial information are illustrative Article 11 presentation
scenarios only; they do not represent contractual minimum cash, net tangible assets or maximum redemption conditions to Closing. Redemptions
by BRAC public shareholders will reduce the cash available from the Trust Account and will change the relative ownership percentages
of the post-Closing shareholders, but redemptions, standing alone, will not prevent consummation of the Business Combination solely because
the Trust Account balance or pro forma net tangible assets fall below a specified threshold under the Business Combination Agreement.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B><A NAME="ns_043"></A>NOTES
TO UNAUDITED PRO FORMA CONDENSED COMBINED FINANCIAL INFORMATION</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: center; background-color: white"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>1.
Transaction and purpose</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial information gives effect to the proposed business combination in which Conwall DE Sub
Inc. merges with and into Broad Capital Acquisition Corp. (BRAC), with BRAC surviving as a subsidiary of Conwall Construction
Industries Limited (Holdco). It also reflects the September share cancellation and dividend described in note (g). The information is
for illustrative purposes and does not represent the results that would necessarily have occurred had the transactions taken place on
the assumed dates or predict future financial position or results.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>2.
Basis and periods</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
historical financial information of Conwall and BRAC is prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The unaudited pro forma condensed combined
balance sheet assumes the transactions occurred on June 30, 2026. The annual and interim statements of operations assume the transactions
occurred on April 1, 2025. The presentation assumes a March 31 fiscal year. BRAC annual results comprise the year ended December 31,
2025 plus the quarter ended March 31, 2026 less the quarter ended March 31, 2025. Both interim historical columns cover April through
June 2026. Face statements are in U.S. dollars, except share and per-share amounts. Amounts in these notes and supplemental schedules
are in U.S. dollars unless otherwise indicated. Minimum redemption assumes no additional redemptions; maximum redemption assumes redemption
of all 6,969 remaining public shares.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>3.
Accounting treatment and estimates</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
pro forma information assumes that Conwall is the accounting acquirer and that the business combination is a reverse recapitalization
of a nonoperating shell. BRAC net assets and liabilities are included at historical carrying amounts, with no goodwill or acquisition-related
fair-value step-up. This assumption reflects Conwall&rsquo;s operating business and approximately 84% of the illustrative share subtotal
before underwriting and other additional issuances. The accounting for settlement instruments, transaction costs, intercompany balances,
dilution and tax effects is preliminary. Final accounting and closing amounts may differ materially from this presentation. The accounting
for underwriting share settlement and the related EPS effects is incomplete, as described in notes (c) and (f); the illustrated capitalization
subtotal excludes those shares.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(a)
Trust liquidation</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
adjustments eliminate BRAC&rsquo;s $87,208 trust asset. Under minimum redemption, the balance is transferred to unrestricted cash. Under
maximum redemption, it is distributed to holders of all 6,969 remaining public shares. No additional trust earnings are assumed. The
separate $291,400 trust over-withdrawal liability is retained and is neither netted against the trust balance nor assumed to be forgiven.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(b)
Redemption and temporary equity</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
adjustments eliminate $87,208 of common stock subject to possible redemption. Under minimum redemption, the amount is reclassified to
permanent equity. Under maximum redemption, it is eliminated against the trust cash distributed. The illustrative redemption price equals
$87,208 divided by 6,969 shares, or approximately $12.51 per share. The scenarios do not establish that all closing or listing conditions
will be satisfied. No incremental redemption excise-tax adjustment is included.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(c)
Underwriter settlement</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Deferred Underwriting Fees are $1,500,000 and will be settled at Closing through the issuance of Holdco Ordinary Shares at a price per
share equal to the higher of $0.50 and ten times the recent average trading price of BRAC Rights, subject to a 9.9% ownership cap. The
underwriter&rsquo;s net proceeds from sales of those shares may not exceed $1,500,000, and any remaining shares must be returned to Holdco
for no consideration. The 3,000,000-share figure is an illustration at the $0.50 floor before application of the variable price and ownership
cap, not a fixed issuance. All settlement shares legally outstanding at Closing are included in Closing capitalization even if they may
later be returned. The underwriting obligation is separate from the Covered Loan Amount and does not cap loan conversion. The pro forma
accounting for the share settlement is incomplete. The preliminary presentation retains a $1,500,000 settlement liability and a $2,055,674
credit to additional paid-in capital from reducing the historical $3,555,674 obligation. Those preliminary entries do not establish that
cash settlement is permitted or that the settlement obligation remains payable after the contractual Closing share issuance. Classification,
measurement, the related equity or earnings effects and basic and diluted EPS depend on the issued instrument&rsquo;s terms and the applicable
accounting for the proceeds cap and return provisions. The complete Closing capitalization includes all settlement shares legally outstanding,
while their EPS treatment is assessed separately. These accounting determinations and the share-price inputs may materially change the
preliminary figures presented. &nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(d)
Reverse recapitalization and legal capital</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Pro
forma basic shares comprise 24,670,924 Conwall shares, 2,990,897 nonredeemable BRAC shares, 1,061,020 shares issued upon conversion of
BRAC rights, 564,078 loan-conversion shares, and either 6,969 or zero remaining public shares. The totals are 29,293,888 shares under
minimum redemption and 29,286,919 shares under maximum redemption. Holdco ordinary shares have a par value of $0.0001. BRAC historical
common stock and accumulated deficit are eliminated through recapitalization. Conwall retained earnings and accumulated other comprehensive
income are preserved, apart from the dividend in note (g). The loan-conversion adjustment reclassifies the carrying amount of the loans
to share capital and additional paid-in capital as described in note (j).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(h)

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

period. The historical accrued unpaid balance of $530,000 remains a liability. No replacement administrative agreement is assumed.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
U.S. federal tax effect of the trust-interest, administrative-fee and converted-loan-interest adjustments is calculated at 21%. An equal
valuation-allowance offset is assumed, based on BRAC&rsquo;s reported net losses and full valuation allowance, resulting in no net tax
adjustment. Conwall&rsquo;s Malaysian tax expense is unchanged. No additional settlement, state, cross-border or redemption excise-tax
effect is included. Final transaction tax consequences may differ from these assumptions.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>(j)
Full loan-and-interest conversion into ordinary shares</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Both
scenarios assume conversion of BRAC&rsquo;s June 30 working-capital loans of $2,134,116 and extension loans of $3,506,664, totaling $5,640,780,
without cash repayment. At an illustrative conversion price of $10 per ordinary share, the conversion results in 564,078 shares. The
$10 direct-share conversion price is an illustrative assumption. No Loan Conversion Agreements have been executed
as of the date of this registration statement. The agreements will be entered into in due course and amended as necessary before Closing
to set out each creditor&rsquo;s conversion price and fractional-share treatment. No incremental rights are assumed. The adjustment
eliminates the reported loan liabilities and credits share capital at $0.0001 per share and additional paid-in capital for the remainder.
It also eliminates reported BRAC loan interest expense of $351,635 for the annual period and $90,585 for the June quarter. No additional
estimated interest, debt remeasurement or post-June interest is included. Conversion does not, by itself, establish that the shares are
freely tradable. The entire actual Covered Loan Amount at Closing, including contractually convertible accrued interest and subsequent
permitted advances net of repayments, credits and effective waivers, converts under the amended Business Combination Agreement. The June
30 illustration is not a cap and does not exclude such amounts from the contractual conversion.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
