<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>4.
Transaction costs and intercompany balances</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Historical
expenses include $60,000 of BRAC transaction costs paid by Conwall and credited to BRAC additional paid-in capital. A corresponding
intercompany elimination is not reflected. Matching payment and ledger records are needed to determine whether any receivable,
payable, expense or capital contribution must be eliminated or reclassified; the $60,000 is not assumed to be a second incremental Closing
expense. Additional legal, audit, advisory, underwriting, listing and other Closing costs have not been quantified. Final
invoices and estimates and the applicable accounting classification are needed to allocate them among expenses, equity issuance
costs and liability instruments. Cash payment would reduce liquidity; expensed or equity-charged amounts would reduce earnings or
equity as applicable. The preliminary figures do not establish a zero balance for these costs. See &ldquo;Incomplete transaction accounting
and sensitivities&rdquo; for the available magnitude illustration and completion dependencies. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>5.
Nonrecurring items</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Historical
transaction expenses are retained, including the $60,000 in note 4. No additional nonrecurring Closing expense, settlement gain or
related tax effect has been quantified; their exclusion reflects incomplete inputs rather than a conclusion that such items are absent.
Transaction Accounting Adjustments are required to depict the applicable accounting effects even when an expense or gain is nonrecurring;
material items that will not recur beyond twelve months must be identified separately in the final notes. No optional Management&rsquo;s
Adjustments for anticipated synergies or dis-synergies, and no Autonomous Entity Adjustments, are included.</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>6.
Financing, consideration and liquidity</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
presentation assumes conversion of $5,640,780 of reported loans into equity without a cash outflow. No uncommitted financing proceeds
are included. Pro forma cash reflects the assumed June 30 transactions and is not a projection of cash available at closing. Actual liquidity
will depend on redemptions, operating cash flows, transaction costs and final financing and settlement terms.</FONT></P>
